Take the bark of a young oak from the half facing the sun, strip it from the base toward the top, and discard the uppermost part, bruise it very finely in the milk of a single-coloured cow, and take a pennyworth of saffron in fine powder, and boil the whole well over a slow fire, then strain it and drink morning and night in three draughts or more, and you will truly be healed through God. Amen.

A PLASTER TO DRAW AN ABSCESS.

§ 141. Take great blessed thistle, and cinquefoil, and brewer's herb, and roses, and lard, and butter, and boil the herbs well in water, then take it off the fire and pound the herbs well, then put them back in the same water a second time on the fire, with the butter and the lard, mix them, and boil until they become a paste, and apply to the abscess, and it will truly reduce it, and healing will follow.

118 THE PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST LABOUR PAINS AND FAINTING.

§ 142. Take wheat bran and cold water, and drink it in three draughts, and truly you will be well, with God's help.

FOR A WOMAN WHOSE FRUIT IS MOVING TOO MUCH.

§ 143. Take wheat flour and cold milk, and drink it thus, and truly you will be well.

AGAINST THE WOMB RISING IN A WOMAN.

§ 144. Get as much as a bean of frankincense, place it on three live coals, and inhale the steam through your nostrils and mouth, and it will reduce the swelling; also take hart's horn and use it in the same manner, and you will be healed.

AGAINST JAUNDICE.

§ 145. Take the herbs that grow on the tops of hawthorn and mistletoe, called holly, and boil them in wine or good old ale, until reduced by half, then take it off, strain it, and drink it for nine mornings, three times a day, that is morning, noon, and night, and you will be healed.

AGAINST THE WOMB RISING IN A WOMAN WHO IS SWOLLEN IN THE STOMACH.

§ 146. Take hyssop and the grey herbs, and make a drink of them with good old ale, and strain it clean through a cloth after boiling, and give the woman three draughts at three meals, and it will truly reduce the ailment, and this drink is good against soreness and stomach pain, because the grey herbs are truly good for those conditions, and likewise against all tumours in the body of a person, whether in the stomach, in the blood, or in the kidneys.

A DRINK AGAINST STOMACH CRAMP AND CRAMP OF THE FLESH.

§ 147. Get a handful of rosemary, a handful of hyssop, a handful of clary, a handful of white wormwood, and a handful of

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 119

red fennel, pound them well, boil them in a gallon of strong dark ale made from barley malt, put it in an earthen vessel to keep, seal it well, leave it there for three days, and then take three doses every morning on an empty stomach, and at the end of the night, warm it to blood heat, and then take a pennyworth of the grain called grains of paradise, a pennyworth of cloves, a pennyworth of saffron, and a pennyworth of cinnamon, pound them all together in a mortar into a fine powder, and cast some of that powder on the surface of the drink, and do so for as long as the drink lasts in the drinking of it, and it is truly good, and it has been proven, and good also against all tumors in the body of a man; it is proven.

FOR PAIN OF THE LUNGS.

§ 148. Take the root of the beet (called in Latin Beta,) and cut off the stalks and heads, and take three gallons of clean water and boil them, and draw out the beet, and leave the liquor to boil, then draw it off the heat and leave it to stand at the warmth of embers in moderate heat, and set it upon fresh dregs, and leave it to work until it has settled, and then give it to the patient to drink until nine meals have passed as his only drink, then take the beet and draw it through butter and powder of mallows, and give it to the patient to take until nine meals have passed, and he will be healed, through God, Amen. And very good is this remedy against the three-day fever.

FOR THE FEVER AND THE SWEATING SICKNESS.

§ 149. Take a handful of iris root, and three quarts of good strong ale, and pound the iris well, and boil it in the ale until the three become one, and then strain it, and take a pennyworth of powdered grains of paradise and boil it a second time gently, and divide it over four days before the fever, and you will be healed.

120 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

AGAINST INTERNAL PAIN CALLED THE SPLEEN.

§ 150. Take the herb called yellow dock, which grows in meadows and on mountains, creeping along the ground, bearing a plain blue flower; gather of those herbs a bagful, and pound them fine in a large wooden mortar, and take an equal measure of the water of springs, and pound those firmly together, and take a red cockerel, and kill it, and pluck it, and draw out its entrails, and make it thoroughly clean, and place it in a brass pot to boil with clean water therein, at least two gallons, and boil the cockerel in the water and the herbs, until the bones come away from it, and then remove from the fire, and pull the bones out completely, and put the meat back into the pot on top of the herbs, and boil a second time thoroughly, until you see it becoming thick, and nearly losing its boil on account of its thickness, and then remove from the fire, and take a strong linen cloth and strain all of it together with the meat, and the liquid that comes through the cloth put on the fire, then take a halfpenny-worth of powdered pepper and throw it into that liquid while warm, then take it off to cool, and mix it well while it cools, and give to the patient on his food and on his drink at every meal until the disease is seen to dissolve and run through him: and truly I have proved this on small and great alike, and this is called the blue composition for the spleen.

IF A PERSON HAS BEEN POISONED BY A HORNET.

§ 151. Take nine cloves of garlic, and peel them clean, and take a spoonful of treacle, and half a quart of strong new ale, and mix these together and give to the patient to drink a full draught of it, and put enough clothing on him until he sweats; if the drink stays one hour in his body, though there be black spots on him they will come out, and he will escape, and this remedy is also good for a person bitten by a snake.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 121

FOR SWELLING AND PAIN OF A MAN'S THROAT, OR LUMPS AT THE BASE OF THE EARS.

§ 152. Take the celandine and the roots of red fennel, and the tops of leeks, and red wine, and butter, pound them together, apply it to the affected area as a cold poultice, and you will truly be healed through the help of God.

FOR SCABS AND SCURF ON A MAN'S FLESH.

§ 153. Take the celandine, and the roots of alexanders, and wood sorrel, and boil them in as much water as will cover them until it is reduced by half, and with that liquid wash the wound, and it will heal; this is proven.

FOR PAIN IN THE BACK.

§ 154. Let blood from the back of the foot near the thumb, and bind the leg after it has been fomented with warm water, and it will truly heal.

FOR RHEUMATIC PAIN IN THE LEGS AND IN THE LIMBS.

§ 155. Take the herb called hart's horn, and boil it in three gallons of water until it is reduced to a bottle, and then add a gallon of ale to it, and boil it again until it is reduced to a bottle, and strain it, and keep it in a clean place, and anoint the pain very frequently, and it will heal.

FOR COSTIVENESS AND ITS PAIN.

§ 156. Take the red crowfoot, which some call tormentil, and parsley, pound them together, and boil them through honey and old ale, strain it clean, and drink it night and morning, and you will be healed in the name of God.

122 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR EARACHE.

§ 157. Take ash keys — others call them ash locks — and boil them firmly in the patient's water, and anoint the pain with it, and place black wool in the ears, and the patient will be healed, by God.

FOR THE YELLOW SICKNESS (JAUNDICE).

§ 158. Take an apple, the largest that can be found, and cut its eye out round, and draw out the core of the apple with a bone or wooden spoon, and fill it with the juice of celandine — which others call eye-of-the-day — and saffron, then replace the eye back in its place, then set the apple to bake under the embers, and when it is done take it out of the embers, and pound it finely, and give it to the patient to eat, and he will truly be healed.

FOR HEART DISEASE.

§ 159. Take the bark of the blackthorn, and scrape away the outermost part, and boil the white bark in water in which beef has been boiled, and after this boil an egg hard, and take the yolk and wheat flour, and mix that yolk well with the flour, and take a portion of the liquid in which the bark was boiled, and of the yield of the flour and egg yolk, and make bread of them, and bake on a hearthstone, and eat it night and morning, and take care that the patient drinks no other drink except the liquid in which the bark was boiling, or red wine, and he will be healed. — Philip the Physician.

FOR FAINTING ABOUT THE HEART.

§ 160. Take the juice of fennel and honey, measure for measure, and boil until it sets hard, and eat the size of an egg of it night and morning, and you will be healed. — P. the Physician.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 123

FOR A HARD BELLY.

§ 161. Take two spoonfuls of the juice of holly leaves, and drink it three times a day, until nine days are past, and you will be well, through God.

FOR A WET STOMACH.

§ 162. Take the root of leeks, and make them into a powder by roasting at a distance before the fire and pounding them, then take a spoonful of that powder in a good draught of red wine, and drink it last thing at night, two hours after food and drink, for three days, and you will be well through God and Amen.

FOR THE LUNGS.

§ 163. Take the three herbs named here, namely the grey herbs, that is to say tansy, and red fennel — and a good handful of each of the three herbs is sufficient — pound them well, and make them into a drink with good, wholesome old ale, then boil on a slow fire, strain it clean, and drink it cold three times, and it will break the pain that lies under the shoulder blade, through God, and the person will be well.
Another way to make it: pound the herbs fine, and add three parts of ale, or good old mead, to the bruised herbs, and after it has stood thus for half an hour in the cold, strain it firmly through a clean linen cloth, and give the patient three doses every three hours, and through God it will heal him.

AN OINTMENT AGAINST ALL MANNER OF PAIN.

§ 164. Take the flowers of broom, and when there are no flowers, the leaves and the husks, and the peelings, and the root of the great hemlock, and the leaves of alexanders, and the grey herbs, and the root of red dock, and pound them well, and make an ointment of them with butter, and anoint the pain frequently, and it will heal.

124 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

AGAINST DISSOLVING OF THE LIVER.

§ 165. Take a little of the tansy, that is the wild tansy, and pound them well with wine, and strain hard, and drink three times a day for three days, and you will be healed, through God.

Where there is no wine, take strong wholesome ale, or wholesome and strong mead in its place.

Ox tongue draws away the red colour, but pounding it well with wine and drinking it causes a man to have good memory and senses, warm and dry, in truth.

AGAINST THIRST IN A SICK OR HEALTHY PERSON.

§ 166. Take the herb known as Lady's School by some, and pound it with warm water and strain it, and when it is cold drink it; this will benefit the lungs and the stomach where there is great heartburn, and will heal the patient.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE FEET, AND SWELLING IN THE ANKLE.

§ 167. Take the root of the great cleavers, and pull away the bark, and then boil well, and afterwards pound well with old lard, and apply it as a plaster upon the pain.

AGAINST THE DRY FILM ON A PERSON'S EYE.

§ 168. Take the leaves of the strawberry (others call them strawberry leaves,) red ones, and pound them together with leg lard and virgin butter, and anoint your eyes when you go to sleep, and the butter will enter your eyes, and they will be healed through God.

ANOTHER.

§ 169. Take leg lard, and virgin butter, and a little purified aloe, and boil them a little, and let them cool, then anoint your eyes when you go to sleep.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 125

AGAINST BRUISES ON A PERSON.

§ 170. Take the juice of leeks, and honey, and ground pepper, and vinegar, and mix well until it is of moderate consistency, and give it to the patient as three drinks, and he will be healed.

AGAINST THE FLUX AND SORENESS, AND ALSO PAIN IN THE GROIN.

§ 171. Take two handfuls of the herbs of the pond, and pound them in a mortar until fine, then boil them in spring water in which beef has been boiled, and then they will become thick; after that boil barley flour on the surface of the broth, and mix it well, then draw it off and place it on a cloth or flannel against the wound front and back, and apply this plaster frequently until the end of nine days. Then take two quarts of clear wine, and a quarter of the blessed distillate (that is to say, aqua vitae,) and put into the wine as much as the patient is able to drink, and let no drink be taken as warm as possible, with the distillate cold first, every evening and morning, and continue thus as long as the condition lasts. Also along with these things take mutton, and boil it in a large spring water, and then draw off the meat, and let the water cool, and take the surface off the water and make it into a ball, and melt that tallow, and boil it for a while with some of the distillate until it becomes an ointment over a slow fire, with a close-fitting lid on the vessel in which it is boiled, and anoint the pain with that ointment front and back. And take kiln-dried wheaten bread, or instead of that a slice of crisp wheaten bread, and mutton as food, and take no other kind of food for a long time, and practice this and you will be healed; for indeed it has been proven true.

AGAINST BURNING EVEN WHERE IT AFFECTS THE JOINTS AND VEINS.

§ 172. Take the polypody fern, others call it the great fern, and take the juice of the root after scraping the upper

126 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

away, and egg white, and mix the juice with the egg white, and
apply it with a feather to the pain morning and night, and it will heal.

TO DRAW OUT A BONE OF A MAN OR A NAIL.

§ 173. Take the plant called in Latin cucumbri,
and Lady's herbs, and pepper in wine, and drink this nine times
on an empty stomach and you will truly be healed.

FOR PAIN OF THE BREASTS.

§ 174. Take the herb greflys, the large griswil and old fat, and
pound them well, and apply to the pain, and that will first reduce it, and
the next day take the henlydan, and
a glove-full of Mair's comb, and boil them down to
half and apply on cloth or flannel, and put it on her when she goes to
sleep, and give her a cup of wine, and she will obtain her natural
rest that night. i. h. u. y.

AGAINST PARASITES ON A PERSON'S FLESH.

§ 175. Take the rue, and pound it fine, and take
the herbs in fine linen and rub the flesh, and they will
die, and this is good against the sweating sickness on a person
which greatly weakens him.

AN OINTMENT AGAINST ALL THICK SKIN.

§ 176. Take the small physician herb, and the green of the wood, and
the long bush, and the broad of the road, and the tame guardian, equal amounts of
each, and pound them firmly, and take unsalted butter
and boil it through until the butter is gone, and boil the herbs, and strain
them clean, and place in a box, and with this anoint every thick
skin.

HERE IS AN OINTMENT TO DRAW OUT INFECTION FROM THE BOTTOM BY THE STRENGTH OF THE OINTMENT.

§ 177. Take the small physician herb, and grey herbs,
and the gaswenwyn, which is called leaves of the berglasar, on erllyriad,

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 127

that which is called broadleaf plantain, and the leaves of the cleavers, and pound them well, then take unsalted butter, and a little new yellow wax and rosin, and grey tallow fat, and boil them well together, and the virtues of the herbs will pass into the butter, tallow, wax, and rosin, and strain it cleanly through linen, and place in a box, and this will draw a plug from the bottom of every tun, and it will heal.

There are three breaks of skin on a man that a physician ought not to interfere with: namely, the membranes of the brain, the second, a rupture of a man's gut, and the third, a water blister; for there is nothing to do but leave them to God, and they do heal fairly often, as is seen in men wounded in war, and neither food nor drink should be given save milk and breast-milk to any who receive a wound in one of those three skins.

AGAINST WORMS IN THE STOMACH.

§ 178. Make slices of turnip by cutting and toasting them before the fire, then grind them, and give to the patient to eat cold on an empty stomach nine mornings, or until the ninth meal of that name, and he will be well.

AGAINST THE BITE OF A SNAKE.

§ 179. Take broadleaf plantain, and the juice of green comfrey, and olive oil, equal parts of each, and give the patient a dry swallow of it, and anoint the wound with it, and this will destroy the poison, and he will be well.

ANOTHER REMEDY AGAINST THE BITE OF A SNAKE.

§ 180. Take the brain of a red cockerel, and the plant called hart's tongue, and pound them firmly, and mix them well with white wine or milk, and let the patient drink a full dry swallow of it, and wash the wound with it, and he will be healed through God.

128 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR A SPOTTY FACE.

§ 181. Anoint it with bull's blood, or with hare's blood.

FOR SWELLING IN A MAN'S KNEES OR JOINTS.

§ 182. Take lady's mantle, called the red ganri, and pound it well, then press it well through water in a clean linen cloth, and give it to the patient to drink.

FOR EXCESSIVE THIRST.

§ 183. Take lady's mantle, and a little mountain ray-grass, and pound them well, then squeeze them over dark wort made from barley malt, or place them in an earthen vessel to stand overnight in the wort, and then give it to the patient to drink in the morning, and that will truly break the thirst.

FOR INTERNAL SWELLING IN THE BODY.

§ 184. Take plums and boil them in goat's milk, and when it is cool, give it to the patient to drink in the morning, and at night as late as you can.

FOR OBSTRUCTION OF URINATION AND BURNING IN THE PRIVATE PARTS OF A MAN OR WOMAN.

§ 185. Take the brain of a hare, and put it in sour white wine, and give it to the patient to drink.

FOR RINGWORM.

§ 186. Take lodestone, and grind it fine, and take beef tallow, and the root of dock, and boil the tallow and the root, and when it begins to cool take the powdered lodestone, and mix into that tallow as much of it as will make the ointment firm enough, and that will truly kill the ringworm.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 129

AGAINST PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 187. Whoever frequently has pain in his head, let him make a lye-wash with the blessed oak, and the combs of St. Ffraid, and the chamomile, and a little of the red funnel, and let him wash his head three times in the week with this, and he will be well.

AGAINST DEAFNESS OF THE EARS.

§ 188. Take eel-fat and water of a snail, and the bark of the elder tree, which grows hidden in the woods, and an egg, warming it, and mix them together and cast it into the ear upon the pain a little at a time, and it will be healed.

AN OINTMENT FOR AN OLD ULCER.

§ 189. Take a good handful of ivy leaves, pound them well together with goat's dung and fresh butter, beating them well together, and apply as a plaster to the ulcer, and it will be healed.

AGAINST HEADACHE IN A PERSON.

§ 190. Take the herbs of the trough, and pound them well with vinegar and red wine, and apply as a plaster to the forehead of the patient.
He who does not eat food when he has appetite for it, his stomach will fill with wind and unhealthiness, and this will cause pain in the head; and taking dry food of bread with salted mutton will make him well.

AGAINST ALL MANNER OF PAIN.

§ 191. Take a measure of the flowers of broom, and iris, and primroses, and a handful of the roots of the red nettles, and the root of that which is called the great hemlock, and the leaves of the marsh mallow, and the broad leaves of the wayside plantain that has seeds upon them, and a quart of seeds, and mix them, and pound them fine and well through pure butter,

130 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

and boil them briskly through the butter, strain through a clean linen cloth, and store in a closed box, and it is a valuable ointment against every kind of pain.

TO KILL WORMS IN A MAN'S STOMACH, WHICH WILL NEITHER ALLOW FOOD NOR DRINK WITHOUT OPPOSING THEM.

§ 192. Take the herbs called honey-herbs, and pound them well with white wine, warming it a little, and give to the patient to drink on an empty stomach in the morning for three mornings, and he will be well.

FOR PAIN IN THE BACK, OR HIP PAIN.

§ 193. Take the herb called mouse-ear, and pound it well, and boil it with butter, and strain it clean, and anoint the back in the warmth of the fire with it, and he will be well.

FOR DISEASE OF THE LIVER.

§ 194. Take the root of felonwort, and anise seed, and heads of saffron, and alexanders, and pound them well with dark ale or white wine, and strain clean and drink morning and evening, until the pain ceases, and through God you will find healing.

TO RESTORE SIGHT THAT HAS BECOME DIMMED.

§ 195. Take the juice of hemlock, and the juice of yellow-wort, and the juice of swallowwort herbs, and a little vinegar or verjuice, and the blood of an eel, and the gall of a cockerel, mix them together, and place in a clean vessel until it matures, and take the clear liquid and apply it to the eyes of a person who has lost their sight, and, says the art, truly if he has lost it he shall find it again.

FOR PAIN OF THE SPLEEN AND THE LIVER.

§ 196. Take the root of the fern, and pound it well, and mix it with a little warm water, and rub it with your hand in

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 131

mixed, and then strain it under pressure through a linen cloth, and make it into a plaster with barley flour and egg white, and spread it with a spatula on a woollen cloth, and apply it to the sore.

FOR ALL AILMENTS OF THE EYE, AND ESPECIALLY FILMS OR SPECKS.

§ 197. Take the wild or tame danewort, and boil it well in white wine until the virtue of the herbs has passed into the wine, and then take it off the fire, and strain it clean, and let it cool and clear, and then take the clearest of the water, and put camphor into it, and let it dissolve in the liquid, and take a little of the liquid and put it on your eye, and whatever ailment is on the eyes, it will drive them away to health; it is proven, says Aristobolis.

FOR PAIN IN THE STOMACH.

§ 198. Take a little of the danewort, and grind it fine, and add white wine as a drink, and drink it, and you shall be well.

ANOTHER.

§ 199. Take a little of the danewort, and of the herbs of the body, and boil them well with salt, and eat them often while fasting, and you shall be well.

FOR SWELLING ON A PERSON'S HEAD AFTER SUSTAINING A FALL.

§ 200. Take one ounce of bay salt, and three ounces of raw honey, and one ounce of cumin, and two ounces of turpentine, and mix these well on the fire, and afterwards spread them on a linen cloth and make a plaster, and apply it warm to the head, and this will draw out the swelling and bruising, and you shall be well; let neither glue, nor tallow, nor grease of any kind whatsoever be put in a plaster that is to be applied to the head.

132 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST PAIN IN A WOMAN'S BREAST.

§ 201. Take the leaves of hemlock, bruise them fine and boil them with fresh butter over a slow fire in a pan, and apply as hot as she can bear it to her breast on white cloth, and she will be healed; or the leaves may be pounded together with fresh butter, or the juice of the elder, and made into a plaster on white cloth, warmed as hot as can be borne, and applied to the breast.

AGAINST CANCER IN THE MOUTH.

§ 202. Take a cup of wine or claret, and a sprig of rosemary, and boil them together, and add a piece of aloes the size of a hazelnut, and a spoonful of honey, and two spoonfuls of water, mix them well, and wash the mouth frequently, and it will be healed.

TO MAKE THE HAIR GOLDEN YELLOW.

§ 203. Take the rind of rhubarb, and put it in white wine, and wash your head with it, and dry it with a fine clean linen cloth, then dry your head by the fire or in the sun if it be warm; wet your head again, and dry it in the same manner as before, and the more frequently you do this, the finer the hair will be, without causing any harm to the head at any time.

TO REMOVE SPOTS AND FRECKLES FROM THE HANDS.

§ 204. Take the juice of the climbing plant together with a little wine-salt, wash your hands, and let them dry of their own nature, and wash again with it, and you will see all the freckles and spots disappear, and this remedy is truly good against rash and eruption as well.

TO KNOW WHETHER A SICK PERSON WILL LIVE OR DIE.

§ 205. Take the breast milk of a woman who is nursing a boy, and take the patient's urine, and drop the milk on the tip of your finger

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 133

on top of the water, if the milk floats on the surface, the patient will live; if it sinks to the bottom, he will truly die.

ANOTHER.

§ 206. Take daisy flowers, and pound them well with wine, and give to the patient to drink; if he vomits it up, he will die of that illness; if he does not vomit, he will live, and this has been proved true.

FOR A BURN FROM FIRE.

§ 207. Take the roots of fern, and pound them well with butter, and apply them as a plaster to the sore, and it will break the blister.

FOR WILD PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 208. Take leaves of foxglove, and pound them with milk and sheep's tallow until they form a plaster, and apply as hot as can be tolerated to the head.

ANOTHER METHOD OF MAKING IT.

§ 209. Take fine oatmeal, and foxglove leaves and sheep's tallow, and milk, and pound them together well until they form a plaster, and place on the fire until heated, and apply to the head as a plaster as hot as can be tolerated; it is truly good.

FOR THE KNOT-POX (SMALLPOX).

§ 210. Take quicksilver, and turpentine ointment, and white lead, and blue vitriol, and lard, and melt them together into an ointment, and mix well to kill the quicksilver, removing the old and applying the new; and take as a drink to cause it to break outward, long pepper and treacle in stale wine.

134 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST THE GREAT POX.

§ 211. Take the value of two pennies of oil of turpentine, and the value of two pennies of oil of bay, the value of six pennies of quicksilver, the value of two pennies of the gum called mastic, the value of two pennies of green rust called verdigris, the value of two pennies of blue vitriol, the value of a penny of camphor, the value of a penny of aloe, the value of a penny of burned calcined stone, and an obol* of rosin, a pound of pig's lard, a pound of white lead if the patient is moist; mix them all together and anoint the patient; it is a proven remedy.

ANOTHER OINTMENT AGAINST THE GREAT POX.

§ 212. Take a pound of boar's lard, or badger's lard for a man, or if for a woman, sow's lard, and half a pound of the resin called frankincense well pounded, and an ounce of quicksilver, half an ounce of white vitriol, an ounce of green rust, and a little aloe unburned, and an obol of calcined stone; pound them all together well so that one cannot be distinguished from the other, and anoint the patient; it is a proven remedy.

A GROWING OINTMENT AGAINST ALL THIN SKIN.

§ 213. Take female speedwell, and elder bush, and the tame houseleek, and wood sorrel, equal amounts of each, pound them well, and boil them in May butter without salt, then strain through fine linen, and keep in a box, and anoint the sore with it and it will heal; if there is dead flesh in the sore, take a little aloe, or blue vitriol, or red calcined mercury, and mix it with some of the ointment, and that will eat away the dead flesh, and will bring about healing.

AGAINST WARTS ON A MAN'S HANDS OR FEET.

§ 214. Get earthworm, and pound it with salt or fresh butter, and make a plaster of them, and apply it to the place where the warts are, and that will uproot them.

* Obolus, perhaps; worth a halfpenny.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 135

AGAINST WARTS.

215. Take a slow-worm, and cut off its head, and rub the hands, or wherever the warts are, with the blood that comes from it, and then bury the head deep in the earth, and as the head rots, so will the warts disappear.

AGAINST A THORN OR ARROW THAT HAS ENTERED A PERSON AND CANNOT BE DRAWN OUT.

§ 216. Get the root of the rough thistle or its leaves, and egg white, and mix them together, and apply it to the wound, and it will draw it out.

AGAINST BLEEDING OR A BITE.

§ 217. Bind the person's little finger and it will stop the bleeding.

AGAINST THE BITE OF A MAD DOG.

§ 218. Get lentils, and pound them, and mix with milk, and give to the patient as his only drink for nine days, strained through fine linen; others boil the lentils in buttermilk, and strain it under pressure, and give it as a drink until the end of the ninth day to the patient, and let him drink as much as he can, with no other food or drink.

TO CAUSE A WOMAN TO CONCEIVE.

§ 219. Get the liver of a hare, and its kidneys, and some of its blood, and through the sides of the vessel in which the meat is boiled, mash them, and add thereto half an ounce of paris grains in powdered form, and a little fine white wine, and let this be given to her when she goes to bed, and she will be fulfilled with natural disposition.

AGAINST DREAMING IN SLEEP.

§ 220. Take the blessed oak, and hang it around the person's neck, or give them its juice to drink when going to sleep, and he will cease to dream.

136 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

TO KILL A WORM IN A TOOTH.

221. Take the root of the yellow-weed and break it into pieces, and place it under the tooth of the patient for three nights, and it will kill the worm.

AGAINST ALL MANNER OF SCABS AND ERUPTIONS ON A PERSON'S SKIN.

§ 222. Take onions and bruise them in water or vinegar, and with this wash the affected area; this will cure scabs of the head, and every other eruption that may be on the body.

AGAINST NOISE IN THE HEAD, THAT WHICH PREVENTS HEARING.

§ 223. Take a head of garlic that has been peeled, and pierce three or four holes in its middle, and dip it in honey, and place it in the ear, and put black wool in the ear behind it, and let the patient sleep on the other side every night, and leave it for a week or eight days without moving it, and it will break up the mucus from the nose, and the patient will be able to hear.

AN EXCELLENT PLASTER FOR ANY SWELLING.

§ 224. Get cream of milk, or in the absence of cream, fresh milk, and place in a vessel on the fire, with the crumb of white bread and wax, and a little honey; and when it has boiled sufficiently, add about as much elder-tree fat to melt in it, and about as much ivy ointment. If there is great heat in the swelling, add egg white to it, mix well, and apply to the swelling.

A PLASTER TO BREAK PAIN, TUMOURS, AND INFLAMMATION.

§ 225. Get the milk of a single-coloured cow if you can, and oat flour, and a little fat of a young sheep, and a handful of brooklime; pound them well, and boil them together well, and apply lukewarm to the afflicted area, and it will bring relief quickly.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 137

TO DRAW A SWELLING WHEREVER IT MAY BE.

§ 226. Take the juice of broadleaf plantain, and egg whites, and refined honey, and barley flour, mix them together, and apply as a plaster to the swelling; it is proven.

ANOTHER TO DRAW A SWELLING.

§ 227. Get the juice of the cleaver plant, and egg whites, and honey, and wheat or barley flour, and apply as a plaster to the pain, and it will heal.

TO DRAW A SWELLING AND PUS.

§ 228. Take rye flour, and egg whites, and the juice of broadleaf plantain, and apply as a plaster to the pain, and anoint it with honey, and it will heal by God's grace, and where necessary, do so a second and third time.

TO DRAW A SWELLING.

§ 229. Take the leaves of the spotted foxglove, and tallow of the dwarf elder, and oatmeal and milk, and apply as a warm plaster to it, and it will heal.

TO BRING A WOUND TO A HEAD, AND TO DRAW THE MATTER TO THE SURFACE OF THE SKIN.

§ 230. Take the leaves of the spotted foxglove, and pound them mixed with dwarf elder wine and barley flour, and apply to it as a warm plaster.

ANOTHER.

§ 231. Take pressed cheese made with beer, and sheep's milk, and plaster them together.

AGAINST FLEAS.

§ 232. Take a hedgehog and roast it, and place a vessel to receive the drippings, and put those drippings on a rush, and place the rush where the fleas are, and as many as are in that room, they will come to it.

T

138 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

AGAINST ALL MANNER OF PAIN IN THE KNEES, FEET,
ARMS, AND ALL JOINTS.

§ 233. Take a quantity of broom flowers, and flowers of the iris, and leaves of pellitory, and the root of red dock, pound them well together, and make an ointment of them with butter, and anoint the pain with it, and it will heal.

AGAINST THE AILMENT CALLED THE MIGRAINE, BEING
A PAIN ON ONE SIDE OF THE HEAD.

§ 234. Take a live hare, cut off its head and skin it, then boil or roast it, then open the skull, and take flowers of rosemary and powder of the same, place them in the skull, and stitch it up, and bake or roast it, and eat the brains, and sleep therewith; and truly it is good.

AGAINST THE FALLING SICKNESS, CALLED IN LATIN EPILEPSIA.

§ 235. Take the blood of a newly born lamb that has never suckled, and mix it with two spoonfuls of good ale, and drink this fasting three mornings, and this is proven and wonderful.

TO REDUCE VAPOURS THAT RISE TO THE HEAD.

§ 236. Get cumin seed worth a penny, seed of Lady's lace which is called glingal, worth two pence, cinnamon worth two pence, and powder them all well together, and stir into warm liquid to drink, and it is good.

AGAINST THE WEN AND THE SWELLING.

§ 237. Get a good handful of red liverwort, and a handful of rue, and a handful of garlic, and pound them well in strong ale or wine or good mead, then strain it through fine linen, and warm it and drink it warm, and you will be healed through God.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 139

AGAINST THE SITTING-PLACE OF A PERSON BREAKING OUT.

§ 238. Take the herb called cleavers of the hedges, that is, those whose seeds cling to the stockings of those who go among them, in knobs as large as pepper, along the tops of the plants, and pound them well, and then boil them in butter until they become an ointment, strain them under pressure, and with that ointment anoint the affected area.

AGAINST MIGRAINE OR THE DULL HEADACHE.

§ 239. Get frankincense, yellow wax, and honey, and spread them together well, and apply them as a plaster to the forehead, and it is truly good.

FOR A SHORT MAN WHO HAS LOST THE STRENGTH OF HIS LIMBS.

§ 240. It may be that he lost the strength of his limbs through weakness of the back, and to remedy this take turpentine ointment and mistletoe ointment, mix them together and anoint the back of the short man morning and night, and this will strengthen him.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE KNEES, AND FEET, AND ARMS, AND EVERY JOINT.

§ 241. Get turpentine ointment, and butter, and sheep tallow, and goat tallow, and deer tallow, boil them well together in a pan and strain through a cloth, and with that anoint the pain thoroughly.

AGAINST THE STABBING PAIN THAT BEGINS UNDER THE ARM, AND BENEATH THE BREAST, AND SHOOTS THROUGH THE SHOULDER.

§ 242. Make an ointment from good thick cream, and dock root, a handful, and apply it as a plaster to draw it to the skin, and it is truly good.

140 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST THE BITE OF A MAD DOG.

§ 243. Take brooklime, pound it, and strain the juice through a hard press, mix it with milk, and give it to the patient as a drink, for up to nine meals.

AGAINST THE YRWEST, THAT IS HEAVINESS IN THE LUNGS AND LIMBS, AND STIFFNESS IN THEM.

§ 244. Make an ointment with butter, rue, and frankincense, worth three pennies of the blessed distillation, and anoint three times a week for a month in summer; and if in winter, stay in a warm room, and avoid getting cold from work.

FOR A MAN WHO HAS BECOME DELIRIOUS.

§ 245. Take fleabane, and boil it in a quart of good ale, and use that as a drink; and you will indeed be well.

FOR A MAN WHO HAS WEAKNESS OF THE HEAD, THAT IS, GOING OUT OF HIS MIND.

§ 246. Get a quart of red wine vinegar, and half as much juice of the yellow plant, and mix them together, and first get a poultice, and take a drink through spring water and fleabane, boiled and strained, first thing in the morning and last thing at night, and boil the herbs warm to strengthen the head, and make a compress of hemp seed, and boil the herbs upon it, and put the patient in a dark place to sleep, and it is indeed good.

AGAINST WEAKNESS OF THE HEAD CALLED SOFTENING OF THE BRAIN AND WILD FRENZY, CAUSING MADNESS, AND CALLED IN LATIN PHRENESIS, IN WHICH THE PATIENT DOES NOT KNOW WHAT HE SAYS, THAT IS THE ACTION OF THE WATER THAT IS IN THE CAVITY OF THE BRAIN COOLING THE PLACE AND THE MEMBRANE HAVING SUNK, WITHOUT BEING ABLE TO SLEEP AT NIGHT.

§ 247. Get hemp seed, and pound it in a brass mortar, and make a compress of it with clean water, and boil it

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 141

to boil another preparation, and a round pellet of anise seed and ginger ground together, and cast it upon the preparation and give it to the patient to drink four times a day for nine days, and use warm food, and thin wholesome drink, and go to sleep in a dark place.

AGAINST BURNING, SWELLING, AND PAIN IN THE LIMBS, THE HANDS, AND THE FEET.

§ 248. Get spearwort, and pound it fine, and make it into an ointment with butter, and anoint the pain with it, and it is truly good.

AGAINST HAIR FALLING OUT.

§ 249. Take watercress, and pound it well, and press out its juice, and wash your head with it and rinse it well, or take that juice, and you will be healed.

AGAINST FLATULENCE.

§ 250. Get galbanum first, then get these dry herbs, namely cloves, and mastic, and grains of paris, and aloes wood, and pound them well together, a pennyworth of each, and eat them dry every morning, and drink through a straw at other times.

TO DRAW OUT BONES THAT HAVE BEEN BROKEN IN A WOUND ON A MAN'S HEAD.

§ 251. Take St. John's wort, and the blessed oak, and rue, and pound them well together with honey and wheat flour, and the white of an egg, and make it into a plaster, and apply it to the wound.

A PLASTER TO DRAW OUT SWELLING.

§ 252. Get barley flour, and the white of an egg, and mix them and apply them to the pain as a plaster.

FOR A MAN WHO PASSES WATER THAT IS BLOOD.

§ 253. Get a handful of each of these herbs, namely parsley, plantain, and shepherd's purse, and pound them fine,

142 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

and strain it through goat's milk whey, and drink a cupful of it fasting every morning, and continue this practice, and you will be well.

AGAINST THE WILD RINGWORM.

§ 254. Get leaves of ground ivy and leaves of spotted foxglove, pound them well together, and boil them in sour whey, and render it good with ox gall or dwarf elder, then strain it, and anoint the pain with it until it is healed.

TO CAUSE SLEEP.

§ 255. Get the seed of the purslane, and the herb of John which is called orpine, and mix with milk, and make into pills, and give him one at a time, and he will sleep presently.

AGAINST A WOMAN BURNED BY A MAN.

§ 256. Take quicksilver worth two pence, ointment of privet worth two pence, camphor worth a penny, colman worth a penny, white lead worth a penny, blue vitriol one halfpenny, and lard, and mix them together and apply to the pain.

AGAINST ERYSIPELAS, WHICH FIRST BEGINS WITH ITCHING BEFORE IT COMES, AND TO HEAL AND STOP THE ITCHING.

§ 257. Get the herb feverfew, pound it fine, and boil it well in butter, and cast in worth a penny of black soap near the end of the boiling, mix it well, strain it, and anoint the sore morning and night — this is proven. And to cause the skin to whiten or become as fair as other skin, take an oatmeal poultice made with water and oatmeal upon it, as a broad cake, and this will make it grow quickly, after washing it with the poultice first.

AGAINST MANWYNON, WHICH OTHERS CALL THE POX IN THE BLOOD.

§ 258. Get ointment of privet worth a groat, white lead worth two pence, frankincense worth a penny, blue vitriol one halfpenny, wax

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 143

worth a penny, oil of turpentine worth a penny, quicksilver worth
three pence, colman worth a penny, and rendered lard of pig,
mix them all together, and apply a little at a time to the
sore, removing the old and applying the new.

FOR A SWELLING IN THE THROAT OF A MAN THAT
PREVENTS HIM FROM SPEAKING.

§ 259. Take lard of pig, and verjuice, and boil together, and
soak a piece of flannel in it, and wrap it around your throat, and
do this for three days; but if it be a hard lump, put clarified
butter on the flannel, and it will soften it well, and prevent it
from festering.

A PLASTER TO REDUCE A SWELLING FROM AN INJURY.

§ 260. Take of the mallow, and the yarrow, and maiden's hair, and
brooklime, and the herbs of the cask, and boil them well in the
strongest verjuice that can be obtained, and apply it as a plaster
to the sore, and this will reduce every swelling.

TO STRENGTHEN THE TEETH AND MAKE THEM WHITE.

261. Take horse-radish and scrub your teeth well with it,
this will make them firm, and white, and healthy for you.

FOR ERYSIPELAS AFTER IT HAS BROKEN OUT DARK RED.

§ 262. Take the leaves of the stonecrop, and the leaves of the
red alder, and the ferllysg, and the green flowers of the broom,
and the iris, and pound them well, and make them into an ointment
with butter and black soap, and anoint the sore with it, and it
will heal.

FOR A VEIN THAT IS BROKEN IN TWO.

§ 263. Take beans or bean flour, and mutton tallow, and boil
together, and apply as a plaster to the sore, and it is truly good.

144 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

AGAINST SWELLING AND *PAINFUL DISCHARGE IN A MAN'S PURSE OR KIDNEYS.

§ 264. Get great plantain, that is the broad-leaved wayside plant, and the shrub of the lesser plantain called pellitory, and dandelion, and a good handful of earthworms, the largest you can find, and thick fat, and pound them together in a mortar until one cannot be distinguished from the other, and apply as a cold plaster to the pain, and it will heal; it is proven.

TO BREAK UP GRAVEL.

§ 265. Get a pint of fennel juice, boil it with a pint of purified honey, and take a spoonful every morning on an empty stomach, and on the last night at the end of nine days.

FOR A MAN WHO TALKS IN HIS SLEEP.

§ 266. Take a pint of juice of wood sage, and a pint of mercury herb, mix them together and drink it, and this will do good, through grace (i.e. through God.)

AGAINST FLESH FALLING AWAY FROM AROUND THE TEETH.

§ 267. Get two pennies' worth of blessed distillate, or else distilled white wine, and two pennies' worth of white wine vinegar, mix them together, and wash your mouth with it for as long as it lasts.

AGAINST WHITLOWS IF THERE BE WORMS IN IT.

§ 268. Get the flesh of a dog that has been skinned, and cut it into small slices like little chops, and apply it to the sore from time to time, and it will draw out and dry the wound cleanly, and if there be worms like pinworms it will draw them out, and apply fresh flesh of the same kind to it from time to time until the end of four nights, and at each time dry it cleanly. And

* Gwyn — slight/slender, most likely.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 145

To heal and dry the pain, seek ointment of the elm tree worth eight pence, and white lead worth a groat, and boil them well together, and apply it to the bare wound a little in the morning and at night, scraping off the old and applying the new; and if it is unbroken, apply to it a plaster of plaintain and butter.

AN OINTMENT AGAINST WARTS, SMALLPOX AND CANKER.

§ 269. Seek a groat's worth of camphor, a penny's worth of storax, and virgin's wax likewise, treacle likewise, elder ointment worth a penny, and an equal amount of boar's grease, and ointment of the elder tree equal to all the other ointments, rose ointment equal to the other ointments, and three spoonfuls of honey, and pound and mix them all together well, then boil them in goat's milk, and draw from the fire, and boil a second time up to nine times, and strain through raw linen, and store in a horn, and with that anoint the wound, and it will draw the worm's work out of flesh and bones.

AGAINST FLESH THAT IS FESTERING AND BREEDING WORMS.

§ 270. Seek two pennyweights of spermaceti, called in Latin spermaceti, and four pennyweights of verdigris, and pound well and fine and add to a pint of goat's milk, and strain cleanly through raw linen, and give to the patient to drink in good old ale, and it is very good.

AGAINST BLOOD GOING THE WRONG WAY IN A PERSON.

§ 271. Seek speedwell, and a third part of the juice of red fennel, and temper with red wine, and let the patient drink it warm and he will be well.

AGAINST DISEASE OF THE BLOOD, AND AGAINST THE PAINS THAT FOLLOW IT.

§ 272. Take the small plums of wild bushes while they are ripe, and dry them either in strong heat or before the

U

146 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

fire from a distance until they become as dry as they can be powdered, and keep them in a sealed glass bottle, and where a person suffers from this complaint, give a spoonful of this powder into about a pint of good wholesome ale, or strong old cider, or good old mead, and warm it well, and give it to the patient to drink on an empty stomach three mornings, and it will break the pain and the aching, and cure the disease.

Also for this pain, take a cloth of rough new linen, and put therein as much as a goose-egg of the finest good wheat bran that can be had of its kind, and bind it in this raw cloth, and boil in a gallon of spring water until it is reduced to a quart, and let it cool, and boil a little in milk and boil it like gruel, and give it as food at every meal to the person; it is proven.

TO BREAK THE PAIN THAT COMES WITH DISEASE OF THE BLOOD.

§ 273. Take wheaten bread and old cheese, and crumble them fine, and boil them through milk, and add enough pepper thereto and eat it, and continue doing so, and it is good.

AGAINST THE DUMB PALSY, THAT IS, THE LOSS OF STRENGTH ON ONE SIDE, AND BLOOD THAT HAS BEEN STOPPED AND FROZEN IN THE VEINS.

§ 274. Take a handful of fresh foxglove leaves and two handfuls of red nettles, and pound them well together, then boil them well in a quart of honey, and strain it clean and put it in a vessel for keeping, and add thereto the value of three pennies of the blessed distillation, or of distilled wine or cider, and take two cups of sorrel-drink and boil it well, skimming it clean as it boils, and take a bowlful of this each morning and evening while warm, and rub your joints well with it in the warmth of the fire, and then with the preserved ointment, and seek a high place to lean the weight of the side upon, and accustom yourself to walking, and continue doing so, and it is good.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 147

FOR THE THING THAT SWELLS UNDER THE NAVEL,
SOMETIMES LONG, SOMETIMES ROUND, LIKE A BALL
THAT IS BETWEEN FLESH AND SKIN.

§ 275. Get a quart of red vinegar, and pound a handful of leeks through their beards and leaves, and boil a pennyworth of sour rye bread in it, and let it boil well in the sour wine, and apply it as a plaster to the pain every night, and renew it every night, and this will disperse it.

FOR THE WEARING AWAY OF THE NATURAL PASSAGE OF THE ROD.

§ 276. Get fennel seed, and anise seed, and mace, and mix them together and put in warm broth or liquor, and take it until the end of nine days, and it is truly good.

FOR A THORN.

§ 277. Get leaves of scabious, called the bitton by some, and old boar's lard, and agrimony, and pound them together, and apply it to the wound, and this will draw it out.

FOR A POISONOUS THORN.

§ 278. Take boar's lard, and black soap, and egg yolk, and mix together, and apply as a plaster to it, and this will draw it out.

FOR PAIN FROM A THORN'S WORK.

§ 279. Take broom tips and boy's urine, and boil it well and apply as an ointment to the pain, and this will ease it. And wildcat's fat is also good: take also ivy juice, and a pennyworth of camphor, and grind them well together, and apply as a salve to the pain.

FOR THE WHITLOW, THAT IS THE PUSTULE ON THE FINGER.

§ 280. Get rue, and cumin, and pig fat, and wheat flour, and boil in white wine, and turpentine oil, and

148 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

mix well together, and apply to the sore, and when it is ripe open it, and put a salve therein, and it will heal like any other bite or bruise.

ANOTHER FOR THE WHITLOW.

§ 281. Seek the herb of St. John and pound it firmly, mix with egg yolk, and apply to the sore, and it will heal.

The skin will be scaly with a dark red color upon it, and burning at the bone, and the rotting of the sinews is what the whitlow does — thus is this wound to be recognized.

ANOTHER FOR THE WHITLOW.

§ 282. Take a snail out of its shell and cut it very fine, and pound into a plaster, and bind it around the finger; this will ripen and burst it, and thereafter the wound will be cleansed and healed just as any other wound is healed.

ANOTHER FOR THE WHITLOW.

§ 283. Take the clay-wort and pound it fine, and mix it well with rose oil, and apply as a plaster to the sore.

ANOTHER FOR THE WHITLOW.

§ 284. Take rue and the herb cadwgan, and pound them fine, and boil them with storax or rosin and yellow wax, and apply as a plaster to the sore; it is good against swelling of every kind in a finger or in any other joint.

ANOTHER FOR THE WHITLOW.

§ 285. Take rue, and ground-ivy, and body-herbs, and the herb cadwgan, and a snail, and a little boar's lard, and pound together into a plaster, and apply to the sore, changing it every night. Others boil the herbs cooked in lard, and add the snail to them after boiling, having cut it very fine, and beat the whole together into a plaster, and use it accordingly.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 149

ANOTHER REMEDY FOR THE ABSCESS.

§ 286. Take a little blue salt, dried and ground fine, and mix it well with egg yolk, applying it thoroughly, and place it on the sore, and it will heal it quickly, and will break the pain and reduce the swelling.

TO IMPROVE THE SIGHT.

§ 287. Boil fennel in water, and with that water wash your eyes and face every morning and afternoon, and you will be better.

AGAINST A FILM ON THE EYE.

§ 288. Take the bile of a cow, the bile of a hare, and the bile of an old cockerel, and a little blue dye made from the rhuw, and a little juice of celandine, equal amounts of each except that there should be more of the cow's bile, and temper them together with wine that has gone sour, and apply to your eye, and it will destroy the film.

AGAINST DRUNKENNESS.

§ 289. Take a handful of the combs of betony, that is the bitton, and pound them fine, and press in water and strain it clean and drink it before eating any food and before drinking any other liquid, and you will not get drunk that day.

A GOOD REMEDY FOR THE HEAD AND STOMACH.

§ 290. Take three spoonfuls of the juice of betony three mornings in a row, and insert the base of a feather into your nostrils, and that will be a good remedy for the head and for the stomach.

AGAINST AGUE AND SPLEEN.

§ 291. Seek the wing of a lion and fumitory, and put them in drink and drink it heartily in the morning and at midday, and you will truly be well.

150 THE PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

TO KILL THE CANCER.

§ 292. Take quicklime in its natural state before it is burned, and black pepper, and orpiment, as it is called in Latin auripigment, and strong vinegar, rue, honey, and barley flour, equal amounts of each, and boil them together in a new pan or pot until one can make a powder of them, then powder them and boil a second time, and this powder is good for destroying the cancer and warts.

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME AILMENTS.

§ 293. Take the roots of dragonwort, and cut them into small pieces, and dry them and make them into a powder, and take ninepenny weight of this powder and put it in wine, and boil it well, and then let the patient drink it lukewarm on an empty stomach for three days and he will be well, and he shall never suffer from it again, on good authority.

FOR DEAFNESS OF THE EARS.

§ 294. Take a branch of ash wood a foot in length, and place its middle in the fire, and collect the water that comes from its two ends, and take the juice of rhubarb, as it is called in Latin rhubarb, and wine, and the fat of a fresh eel, and of these take equal amounts of each, and mix them all together, and put them in the ears when going to sleep. It is also good for this affliction of the ears to put soured whey in them, with black wool upon it.

THIS IS HOW A STABBED MAN IS TO BE KEPT.

§ 295. Let him not eat cheese, nor butter, nor eggs, nor sea fish, nor beef, nor rye bread, nor newly toasted bread, and let him drink nothing but milk, and water, and milk mixed with a draught of wine or mead once in the twenty-four hours, and let him not practise fornication with women, and he will be saved through God.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 151

AGAINST A WOUND FROM A WEAPON, OR PAIN IN THE SINEWS OR VEINS, OR SWELLING, OR BONE, WHEN IT SWELLS AND BURNS AND FESTERS.

§ 296. Take goat's milk and linseed, and boil them together, and take the milk of a cow of one colour and bean flour, and mix and apply over the other, and let it boil for a long time and strain it and apply it as a plaster to the pain, and leave it until the next day or longer; it will reduce the swelling and the pain, and will purify the flesh, and will cause the sinews to grow, and will cleanse away the dead flesh, and will drive away the scab, and will cause the person to sleep; if necessary, seek a growing ointment.

AN OINTMENT TO BREAK OPEN A BITE OR WOUND, AFTER IT HAS CLOSED BADLY, AND TO HEAL IT.

§ 297. Again, with the same ointment, seek an equal measure of wax, and rosin, and black soap, a few leaves of the broad-leaved vine, and pound them together and boil them on the fire, and strain through a cloth, and put in a vessel to keep, and apply this to it in the manner of a plaster, and it will be healed.

TO MAKE A WATER TO GROW FLESH, AND SKIN, AND BONES.

§ 298. Take a handful of red roses, and spring water, and the juice of yellow weed, and honey, and the juice of water hemlock, and the juice of fennel, and the juice of sowbread leaves, and the juice of elder, and a spoonful of a young person's urine on the breast, and red wine, and mix together, and warm them a little, and strain and put to keep; and with this anoint the wound where flesh is growing dead, and it will consume it, and will grow cleanly with use of it.

AGAINST CANCER AND BAD FLESH.

§ 299. Take good cheese, and pound it firmly, and mix with clear honey, and anoint with it frequently, and apply cabbage leaves upon it, and this will kill it within three days, and it is good.

152 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST A BLISTER.

§ 300. Take honey, and egg yolk, and wheat flour, and mix them together, and apply it as a plaster to the sore, as the case may require, and it is truly good.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE LEG, WHICH RISES IN LUMPS, AND BREAKS IN A SUPPURATING MANNER, AND IN RED PUSTULES, AND SPREADS DOWNWARD TOWARD THE ANKLE, AND AROUND THE LEG, ITS COLOR BEING VERY DARK.

§ 301. Seek rose ointment worth three pence, ivy ointment worth two pence, turpentine ointment worth a penny, a spoonful of honey, and a little wax, and red lead worth three pence, and a little lard of elder or deer, and a little brass stone finely ground, and about a spoonful or two of the blessed distillation, or distilled red wine; mix them together and warm them in a vessel over the fire until the chill has gone through it, and anoint the wound, and it is good.

AGAINST A FOUL WOUND.

§ 302. Take the juice of the elder, called in Latin bocstcs, having been boiled in beer or wine, and wash the wound, and it is good; or take the leaves and pound them well with wine or beer or good mead, and strain through a press, and place in an earthen vessel on the fire until the chill has gone through it, and wash the wound.

TO MAKE AN OINTMENT AGAINST WARTS.

§ 303. Take yellow wax, and rosin, and elder lard, and mercury herb, and the yellow plant, pound them well together, and boil them all together, and strain through a clean cloth, and anoint the wound, and it will heal.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 153

AGAINST WARTS.

§ 304. Take the blessed oak, and pound it fine, and put it in a vessel filling it to the brim, and pour spring water over it into the vessel, and let it stand overnight, and strain it, and take this as your only drink, and you may use wine instead of water on the powdered herbs, and drink a full draught of it once in every twenty-four hours, and take the herb and pound it fine together with an ointment of mistletoe, and boil them together and strain through a press, then add to it a little yellow wax, and a little honey, and a little hart's tallow, and boil together until it becomes an ointment, and put it in a vessel to keep, and anoint the affliction with it. And if you take the root of the herb and wash it clean, and dry it thoroughly, and grind it into flour, and add it with one third wheat flour into bread, and live on that bread and goat's milk as your only food, you will heal more quickly; and this is proven true.

A PLASTER TO DRAW OUT SWELLING AND WORMS FROM WARTS.

§ 305. Take milk from a single-colored cow, and oatmeal, and boil them well, and make it like a small person's porridge, and put thick portions on a cloth, then put honey on its surface, and it will draw out the worms, and reduce the swelling, and will cleanse the flesh of poison, and will soften the hardness within it, and will heal the wound; this is proven.

AGAINST HEAT AND INFLAMMATION OF THE LIVER, AND WIND OF THE WOMB, AND PAIN OF THE TONSILS, AND PAIN IN A PERSON'S LUNGS.

§ 306. Take Our Lady's herb, and liver herbs, and pound them fine and smooth, and put them in a vessel full, and take wine and water half and half, and pour over the herbs so that it passes between them, and let it stand for six hours closed, then strain through a press, and drink a full draught of it morning and evening on an empty stomach, and take

154 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

a broth food made with game meat and these herbs, namely ox tongue, milk-wort, fennel, parsley, and a little honey, and let that be your only food; also make a lye from wood ash or fern, or nettles, and boil in it the worth of two pennies or three of lard, and set it to cool and to stand until the next day, then skim its surface and put it in a vessel to keep, and with that anoint your sides and the places where the pain is, and you will be healed, through God.

AGAINST A BURN FROM FIRE.

§ 307. Put your own urine over a cow-pat, and let it clarify, then strain the clear liquid into a vessel, and wash the sore.

AGAINST SWINE-POX, THAT IS SHINGLES.

§ 308. It breaks out along the skin, raising white blisters, and clear water runs from them. Take the flowers of the broom, and lard, and boil and strain them, and add the worth of two pennies of black soap, and mix it all well, and with that anoint your whole body, and it is good indeed.

FOR A WOMAN WHO HAS LOST HER NATURAL FUNCTION.

§ 309. Make a gruel of fine oatmeal and clean water, and add a pinch of cumin, and a pinch of the stone called cryth, and in Latin creta, and where that is not available take limestone, and grind it as fine as it can be sifted through fine linen or silk, and cast it into the gruel, and mix the whole together, and take a cupful of this warm twice a day for a full week, and it is good.

TO DRAW A TOOTH WITHOUT ANY PAIN.

§ 310. Seek out ants and their eggs, and powder them, and of that powder apply with a feather-quill to the tooth, and let it not touch any other tooth.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 155

FOR TREMBLING HANDS.

§ 311. Take the grey herbs, also called the grey feverfew, and place them in warm water to steep overnight, and wash your hands in this, and you will benefit from it; and if you wash your back from the nape downward with this water, it will strengthen you wonderfully.

TO RELIEVE THE PANGS OF THE WOMB.

§ 312. Seek the white wormwood and the grey wormwood, and the inner bark of the ash tree, and boil them in spring water that never runs dry, boil them well, and strain them, and drink three large spoonfuls on an empty stomach three mornings, and you will be healed, and it will never trouble you again.

FOR BLEEDING OF THE NOSTRILS.

§ 313. Bruise a handful of nettles, and place them in a cloth against your nostrils, and put some of it into your nostrils, and it is good.

ANOTHER.

§ 314. Take a piece of iron, and place it in the fire until it is warm but not red with heat, and let the blood drip onto it, and when enough has dripped, scrape it off the iron and put it as a powder into your nostrils and blow it in with a feather quill. And this will stop bleeding from the nose, and from a wound, and from a bite, wherever it may be on a person's body.

FOR A PERSON WHO HAS BEEN BURNED.

§ 315. Take a handful of mallow leaves, and shelled snails, and the round leaves called pennywort, and linseed, having been ground in a brass mortar, and mixed and pounded together until one cannot be distinguished from the other, and apply this where the swelling or the sore has broken, and keep it

156 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

without dissolving at any time, and if desired, to inject it with elecampane water to wash it, and the work of the plaster will cause the grey fluid to come out of her nostril, and that is good.

TO KNOW WHETHER A SICK MAN SHALL LIVE OR DIE.

§ 316. Anoint the heel of the patient with boar's lard, then give it to a dog to eat, and if the dog eats it, the man shall live, and if not he shall die.

TO KNOW WHETHER A WOMAN IS PREGNANT OR NOT.

§ 317. Let her make water in a brass or copper vessel, and place a henbane in the water, and if she is pregnant it will be full of bloody spots.

TO MAKE THE HAIR GROW.

§ 318. Take the leaves of the elder and fill an iron pot with them, add water to them in proportion, and boil over a gentle fire until half the water is gone, and with this water wash your head twice a day, taking care that the wash does not go on any part of the skin where hair ought not to be.

ANOTHER.

§ 319. Take two spoonfuls of ivy oil, and two spoonfuls of new honey, and an onion the size of a pigeon's egg, and pound them together in a stone mortar until it becomes an ointment, and with this anoint your head morning and night, and wear a leather cap until the hair grows; it is best to pound the onion fine before adding it to the honey and the oil.

TO REMOVE HAIR AND PREVENT IT EVER GROWING AGAIN.

§ 320. Take ants and their eggs, and make them into a powder, and with these mixed with the droppings of a hen in powder form, apply to the place required, and rub hard until the place becomes warm

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 157

twice a day, and this will kill the hair from its root, and it will grow no more in that place; also you may mix it with water to the consistency of woad, and anoint the place with it twice a day.

TO KILL LICE.

§ 321. Take the resin called olibanum, and lard, and boil them well together, and anoint the head or any other place where there is occasion with this ointment, and it will kill them.

FOR A BLOTCHY FACE.

§ 322. Anoint it with the blood of a hare or a bull at night when going to sleep, and in the morning wash the face with sour buttermilk.

TO DRAW A TOOTH.

§ 323. Take gum of ivy, and ivy leaves, and burn them to powder in a new earthen pot, and put this powder upon the juice of the plant called devil's milk, and apply this to the tooth if it be hollow, and it will fall from your head, but take care that you touch no other tooth.

FOR DIFFICULTY IN URINATING.

§ 324. Pound the leaves of mallow and garlic together with white wine, and drink it, and you will be able to make water whatever the cause may be.

HERE IS THE METHOD OF MAKING THE STOMACH CORDIAL WHICH IS GOOD AGAINST DUMB PALSY, TREMBLING PALSY, DUMB AGUE, TREMBLING AGUE, COLDNESS OF THE HEART, DISEASE OF THE JOINTS AND THE LIVER, HEAVINESS IN THE STOMACH, WIND IN THE BELLY, PAIN IN THE KIDNEYS, AND COLDNESS OF THE SINEWS AND VEINS.

§ 325. Seek a handful of rosemary, and a handful of the keeper, and a handful of thyme, and a handful of southernwood, and a handful of hyssop, leaves and tops of each of these, and the root of gladdon, and the root of

158 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

marchalan, and the root of the hiddigl, and the root of tormaen, a handful of each of them, put them in a mortar, and pound them well, and strain them, and put all to boil in three gallons of strong dark bragget until the three gallons become one, then draw it off and cool it, and strain through a clean linen cloth, and take a quart of pure honey and add it to that bragget, and boil until it is reduced to a quart under the boil, and skim it clean, and draw it off to cool, and then take six gallons of fresh strong ale, between its yeast and its sediment, and put it in a clean vat, and close it up well, and let it stand three days and three nights, and then put it in a strong sealed vessel, and take a pennyworth of cloves, and a pennyworth of ginger, and a pennyworth of grains of paradise, and a little fennel seed, and a pennyworth of the seed of the arddwy, and a little seed of Lady's lace, and as much again of cinnamon, and grind them fine like wheat flour, and put them in a strong linen bag in the vessel, hung by the linen, and place a small stone in the bag to weigh it to the bottom deep, and leave it to keep, and drink that liquor first thing in the morning and last at night, and that liquor is no worse than living water for the benefit of a person's body. Here is the virtue of each of the herbs named: rosemary quickens life, the geidwad breaks the ague, the wendon is against dumb palsy, hyssop for the chest, rue for the bowels, tormaen for the bladder, the hiddigl for the stomach, marchalan for the joints, cloves and ginger for the sinews, Lady's lace for the kidneys, grains of paradise for the brain, the glŷf and cinnamon for the lungs and veins. And the proper use of that drink for every person against the diseases mentioned above, and if there be any other ailment in a person let the herbs suited to that ailment be applied against it, and use this drink frequently, and you will find your body healthier, and younger in appearance, and lighter in the limbs, and stronger in sight, and better in will, more nimble in walking, and sweeter in breath, and this is the best bragget of all, and the best drink in the world.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 159

TO MAKE A PERSON GO TO STOOL EASILY.

§ 326. Take a hen's egg, and remove the rooster's tread from it, and mix with a little good ale, the ale and the egg together, and drink this on an empty stomach in the morning, then fast for three hours, and you will be well.

FOR A STOMACH THAT IS TURNED, THAT IS, ACTING CONTRARY ON ACCOUNT OF THERE BEING COLD AT THE MOUTH OF THE STOMACH, AND THE FOOD BEING TURNED UPWARD, AND BEING UNABLE TO GO TO STOOL.

§ 327. Take two phials of white wine every other day, or rising, seek treacle, and a quart of red sour wine, a pennyworth of mustard, worth three pennies of aloes, and boil them well together, and put them in a vessel to keep, and take two spoonfuls in the morning on an empty stomach after warming it. Get a pennyworth of pepper, worth two pennies of fennel seed, and boil them in purified honey, or the leaves of fennel are better than the seed.

FOR THE DRY COUGH, THAT IS AN OBSTRUCTION OF COUGHING WHERE THERE IS NO SWEAT ON THE FOREHEAD AND NOTHING IS BROUGHT UP.

§ 328. Take these ingredients: a pennyworth of pepper, a pennyworth of fennel seed, two pennyworth of anise seed, a pennyworth of cumin, two pennyworth of the root called liquorice, a pennyworth of cinnamon, and a pennyworth of the seed called grains of paris, grind them very fine, and boil in a quart of honey without letting it boil up on the fire, then draw it off and put in a clean vessel to keep, and take a spoonful every morning on an empty stomach, and a spoonful last thing at night before going to bed, and abstain from meat, and keep to a grain diet.

FOR PAIN IN THE KNEE OR ANOTHER PLACE CALLED THE KNOT OF THE VEIN.

§ 329. Take a pennyworth of black soap, three pennyworth of quicksilver three pennyworth, oil of ivy two pennyworth-

160 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

worth, two pennyworth of frankincense, the water of life called the blessed distillation, worth a groat, and boar's lard, all well blended together until it becomes as warm as the flux, and rub it on the pain, twice a day, rubbing it in each time; it is a proven remedy.

FOR THE COUGH.

§ 330. Take a quart of milk, and a pennyworth of garlic, and pound them, and boil in the milk, and strain it, and drink as much as you can, and use garlic with your food, and live on plain and wholesome food.

FOR SHIVERING AND SWELLING OF THE JOINTS, AND FOR PAIN IN THE THIGHS OR SIDES OF THE BACK WHEN WALKING.

§ 331. Take two pennyworth of black soap, three pennyworth of quicksilver, three pennyworth of distilled spirits of life, and a pound of red boar's lard if it can be had, and when the lard is melted cast into it the black soap along the edge of the still, and stir it well, and when it cools cast in the quicksilver, and mix it until it becomes like an ointment, and with this ointment anoint the pain by the fire morning and night well, with an anointing if needful.

FOR HAIR BECOMING MATTED, THAT IS, GROWING TANGLED SO THAT IT CANNOT BE COMBED.

§ 332. Shave the head once a week for a year, and wash every night with a strong lye of wood ash, and every morning with sea water, or water salted with salt, cold, and once a week anoint the head with chicken fat or eel fat, and after greasing it thus put about your head as hot as you can bear this plaster: take the finest white wheaten bread that can be had from baker's bread, and boil in sheep's milk, and add one or two spoonfuls of honey, and a large spoonful of beech-nut oil and beaten egg yolk, and plaster these ingredients well together, mixing thoroughly, and apply as a plaster about your head and let it remain twenty-four hours, and when it

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 161

wash your head well with feverfew, fennel and soap, and scrape it well, and take as food large amounts of milk and a little meat and boiled or roasted apples with milk as often as you can obtain it.

AGAINST ALL PAINS IN THE JOINTS, THE BONES, THE KNEES, AND THE BACK.

§ 333. Get black soap worth three pennies, a groat's worth of quicksilver, a groat's worth of ivy oil, and a groat's worth of blessed distillate, and boar's lard or another grease, and grind well in a mortar until it is as white as whey, and store in a sealed earthen box, and anoint with it by the fire night and morning.

AGAINST THE FAILING OF NATURE, THAT IS, A MAN'S NATURE RUNNING INVOLUNTARILY FROM THE ROD.

§ 334. Get a little lead and beat it thin to the thickness of a wheat grain, let it be two handbreadths in length and half a handbreadth less in width, and make a hole at one end of it, and put a string through it and bind it around your slender back by means of this string, and it will cool your nature. Then take the innermost bark of oak and of blackthorn, a handful of each, and boil well, and add honey to make it sweet, and take a small spoonful of anise seeds powdered, and the same quantity of fennel seed powdered, and half that amount of cinnamon powdered, and put these into the brew, and drink it as a drink three mornings and three nights, and take no other drink; it is proven.

AGAINST COUGH OF THE LUNGS.

§ 335. Get the root of the iris, that is the felottai, and figs, and powdered alexanders, that is the root, and make into a confection with honey, beating it well, mixing thoroughly in a mortar, and

162 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

Take a large spoonful morning and night, fasting at least two hours before and after food, and maintain a diet of goat's milk and apples.

TO PURGE THE VENOM OF ERUPTIONS OF EVERY KIND FROM THE BLOOD, FOR THE CAUSE OF ERUPTIONS IN THE BLOOD FROM WHICH COME KIDNEY STONES, AND BREAKINGS OUT ON THE LUNGS, AND WARTS AND ALL BREAKINGS OUT ON THE SKIN, AND ALL DISEASES OF THE HEAD AND STOMACH, AND MANY PAINS OF THE HEAD AND EYES.

§ 336. Take the plants of the hedges, which may be known by their small round seeds that cling to clothes when ripe, and pound them well and place in an earthen vessel with water in it, and boil spring water and pour it over the herbs placed therein, and let it stand an hour, then strain under pressure through a clean linen cloth, and drink it as the sole drink for nine days; and where there are no hedge plants, boil spring water, and for food take much milk food and as many roasted or boiled apples with milk as you can, and bread of fine wheaten flour with honey, and take no meat but fresh whelks, and a broth made from that meat by boiling hedge plants, and white clover of the fields therein, and take a handful boiled, and boil the springs with sour wine in place of bread with the meat; it is proven.

FOR WEAKNESS OF THE HEAD.

§ 337. Take hemp seed, and pound it well and soak it through a bowl of clean water as one soaks gruel, and combs of sulphur, and pound and mix them with that liquor and remove only the herbs that are there, and boil it until it is like gruel, and put upon it some of the herbs in powder, and some of the wood aloes in powder, and fennel seed, and anise seed in powder, and let the patient drink three or four spoonfuls daily, and place him in a dark room to sleep; it is proven.

FOR COUGH AND TIGHTNESS OF THE LUNGS.

§ 338. Get root of elecampane, two pennyworth of black pepper, two pennyworth of root of cleavers, and powder them

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 163

and make into a preparation with pure honey, and take as much as a pigeon's egg, first thing in the morning and last thing at night; it is proven.

AGAINST WATER BETWEEN FLESH AND SKIN.

§ 339. Take two handfuls of watercress, pound them well, and boil them in butter, and while hot place therein a handful of the tender shoots of bramble, and let it melt, and with that anoint the place where the pain is, thoroughly.

TO DRAW SWELLING FROM FEET OR LEGS.

§ 340. Take red onions, and hemlock, and the geidwad, and make an ointment from them for the person, and place the bandage where you know alongside the migraine, and wash daily with your own urine; it is proven.

FOR A PERSON WHO CANNOT GO TO THE TOILET.

§ 341. Take the root of the gloria, which others call the helesc, and the bark nearest to the elder, and the juice of the fyddarllysg, and pound them well, and take old ale and mix together with the herbs when softened, then strain through a clean linen cloth, and give to the patient to drink as a draught on an empty stomach, and he shall be freed from this affliction quickly, and let him take no other drink until his body is free.

FOR A PERSON WHO PASSES BLOODY URINE.

§ 342. Take fennel seed, and parsley seed or the leaves where the seed cannot be had, pound them well and mix with goat's whey, and strain it clean and drink a quart as a draught every morning and night for fifteen days, and eat salted and sour weglyd, and use light, fresh, and warm food, and wheaten bread with plenty of leaven in it, and broth made by boiling spring water, and spring water, and oat gruel, and use that and you will be well.

164 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

TO DRAW KIDNEYS THAT HAVE BEEN STRAINED OR SWOLLEN.

§ 343. Take a little lard, and mix it with a handful of pounded rue, and a handful of the bitter shoots of privet, well pounded, and some pounded linseed, spread it as a plaster, and apply it on a cloth to the pain; it is proven.

AGAINST CANCER THAT HAS NOT GROWN TOGETHER.

§ 344. Get dog's dung that has dried white, and glass, and grind the glass as fine and small as it can be ground, and mix this powder with the dog's dung together with ivy ointment — old ointment is best — and place on the fire and fry them together, and apply to the wound, and it will heal it.

AGAINST THE WART, OR THE CORN, OR AN OLD SORE.

§ 345. Take a measure of virgin wax, the same measure of frankincense, and the same of pitch, half a measure of French wood, and four weights of the whole of them of green rust; put these together and crush them all very small, and place in a pan and melt them together, stirring well lest they stick to the pan; then when fully melted and mixed, draw it from the fire, strain it clean and apply to the sore, and it is truly good.

AGAINST THE FRENCH WART, CALLED THE PLAGUE.

§ 346. In a dangerous time and place where there are painful and contagious diseases, this is how the contagion is avoided: take three small branches of the herb called rue, and one of the French hazel, and one or two figs, and eat them together, and you will be preserved; it is proven.

ANOTHER TO CURE THE DISEASE.

§ 347. Take the urine of a young boy between ten and twelve years of age, and dry it and grind it into a fine powder, then apply of the

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 165

the most, two spoonfuls of it in a vial of white wine, and
give it to the patient to drink as soon as possible within six hours of his falling ill,
and the sooner the better; this has been proven by experience.

FOR THE GREAT RINGWORM, CALLED THE KING'S WORM.

§ 348. Get the leaves of ivy and pound them and boil them in the fat
of an elder-bush with a sediment of sour whey, and boil them well, and
strain, then apply over it the worth of two pennies of black soap,
and mix all together well, and anoint with it.

FOR BLOOD RUNNING UPWARD AND DOWNWARD, OR HEMORRHAGE OF BLOOD.

§ 349. Take the combs of saffron, and the keeper, and scrape them, and
reduce them, and cast them like a crumbled mixture of the herbs in hen's egg, to
roast and eat before it becomes hard, and use this every full day
for a week or more, and use the powder of the mace in your broth
and your drink warm every day until you are well, and foods
light, fresh, warming, and wheaten bread throughout, and enough
leaven in it, and it is good. Good also is this remedy
for the hadred, that is the involuntary loss of a man's seed from the member.

FOR THE HADRED, THAT IS THE INVOLUNTARY LOSS OF A MAN'S SEED FROM THE MEMBER.

§ 350. Take oyster shells, and burn and powder them, and
the flesh of every apple take and add it to the powder, and make into
pills, and take two pills or three each morning first,
and last thing at night, for nine to fifteen days.

FOR THE CRAMPS.

§ 351. Get fifteen figs, and sixty-nine
bees, and pull off their heads and feet and wings
away, and pound them into powder, then add to the figs this powder,
and as much honey as shall be needed to moisten it, and pound the whole

166 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

together, and make them into pills each one as large as a white plum, and give one to the patient at the onset of the pain, holding him on his feet, and one after the pain has passed, and continue thus until he is well.

AGAINST A FILM ON THE EYE.

§ 352. Take a hard egg and split it along its length, and place within it as much white copperas as a hazelnut, in the raw state, and let it drip into a bottle, and place a drop in the eye; it is proven.

EYE WATER.

§ 353.
