Take a quart of spring water from the side facing away from the sun, and put therein one or two hazelnut-sized pieces of white copperas, and place in an earthen pot to boil, and seal the pot so that no steam escapes, and boil over a slow fire for twenty-four hours, an hour boiling and an hour standing, then strain through a clean fine linen cloth, and store in a bottle; this water will keep well for seven years without being any the worse, and place a drop at the time upon the diseased eye.

AN OINTMENT TO BRIGHTEN THE EYES.

§ 354. Take eyebright, and the effros, and strawberry leaves, and red fennel, and blessed thistle, and the mill, and the blue herb, and the hardhead, and the roots of the reed, and vine leaves, and the herbs of the vat, and the blessed oak, and take of each one an equal amount, and pound them well with butter, and leave them to stand for eight days and eight nights, and on the ninth day boil them well, and strain through a clean linen cloth, and store in a tightly sealed glass vessel, and apply as much as a grain of wheat of that ointment to the eye; apply the ointment described above for two days and two nights to the eye to dissolve the film and the membrane and the cataract, and apply this ointment on the third night to the eye, and it will make it clear and bright; it is proven.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 167

AGAINST TALKING IN ONE'S SLEEP.

§ 355. Take the seed of rue or the leaves, and pound them together with vinegar until they become a mash, then add old ale and mix well, and strain through a clean linen cloth, and give to drink.

AGAINST DREAMING IN SLEEP.

§ 356. Take the blessed oak, and hang it about the person's neck, or give them its juice to drink upon going to bed, and they will not dream, truly indeed.

TO BREAK UP PHLEGM.

§ 357. Take butter without salt, and honey of equal measure, and mix well, and anoint your chest with it, it is good.

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME THING.

§ 358. Take liverwort and boil it in good wine vinegar, and with the hot vinegar wash your chest, and take the boiled herbs and place in a linen cloth and bind it to your chest for three or four hours.

AGAINST THE STING OF A THORN, OR A NEEDLE IN A JOINT WHERE THE HOLE HAS CLOSED.

§ 359. Take wheat flour as finely ground as possible, and temper it with white wine, and boil together until they are thick, and bind it to the sore as hot as can be endured, and this will open the hole and draw out the filth and the poison, and if wine is lacking take good ale.

A REMEDY FOR WOUNDS IN THE LEG OR ARM, OR ELSEWHERE.

§ 360. Take spring water and wash clean and boil in clean water until they are tender, then beat them well

168 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

in a mortar, and place in a clean frying pan, along with deer
suet or tallow, or the fat of a lamb, and add also a measure of
wine lees and wheat bran, and fry them all together, and
make a plaster of it, and apply warm to the painful place, and
thus apply three or four plasters, as the case requires.

THINGS GOOD FOR THE BRAIN.

§ 361. To smell musk and chamomile, and to drink wine in
moderation, to eat the leaves of the houseleek frequently, to keep
the head warm, to wash the hands frequently, to walk in moderation, to sleep
in moderation, to listen a little to string music frequently, to listen to
songs of the tongue, to smell red roses, to wash the temples
in a distillation of roses, to drink a drink of water when going to sleep,
to read a little before going to sleep, light food.

THINGS BAD FOR THE BRAIN.

§ 362. All manner of passion, gluttony, drunkenness,
food in the evening, sleeping much after food, corrupt air,
anger, heaviness of heart, standing frequently bare-
headed, eating much or in haste, too much heat, too much
watching, too much cold, cheese whey, all kinds of nuts, frequent
bathing, onions, garlic, leeks, smelling white
roses, too much fornication, too much music of voice and string, read-
ing too much, strong drink before going to sleep, restlessness
in sleep, fasting too frequently, frequent wetting of the feet.

AGAINST BURNING BY FIRE OR SCALDING WATER.

§ 363. Take the white of an egg, and place on a pewter dish, and
mix with a little alum stone, stirring well until it becomes
like a posset, then take a piece of fine linen and soak in
elm ointment or beechnut oil, or any other ointment
that is easiest to obtain, and apply that linen to the burn, and
upon it apply the cheese, posset, and the alum, and the egg white on top,
and it will draw out the heat, and heal the wound.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI. 169

A REMEDY FOR THE NOISE IN THE HEAD WHICH PREVENTS HEARING.

§ 364. Take the head of a garlic clove and peel it, and pierce five or six holes toward its middle, and dip it in fresh clear honey, and place it in your ear with black wool after it, and lie every night on the other side, and let the garlic remain in your ear seven or eight days, and it will dissolve the ringing in the head, and restore the hearing again.

AGAINST SMALLPOX.

§ 365. Take sea-purslane, and cut and pound it fine, and place in a pot of sentdradoles and spring water, add butter and salt, and make a broth of them, and drink of it once or twice a week.

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME THING.

§ 366. Take three or four magpies, and split them with a knife, and place in a distilling pot the feathers and the entrails and everything of them, and with the distilled water, or the liquid you obtain from them, wash the sore, and especially the face, and these two remedies are proven.

AGAINST A BURN FROM FIRE.

§ 367. Take the mucilage drawn from linseed and apply it to the burned place with a wing feather, and it will draw out the stings of the fire, and heal the pain, as well as any remedy ever did.

AGAINST THE STONE, OR INABILITY TO MAKE WATER.

§ 368. Take a quart of white wine and make a posset of it, and remove the curds, and put into the posset four pennyweight of scrapings of white soap, and boil it, and drink of it as warm as you can, and it is truly good.

170 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR THOSE WHO CANNOT MAKE WATER.

§ 369. Take a flint stone or a pebble, and put it in the fire until it is glowing hot, and with that hot stone warm your drink of strong ale, and drink it.

TO CAUSE ONE TO MAKE WATER.

370. Take a fourth part of a handful of parsley, and as much of red fennel, and bruise them well, and put them in a cupful of old ale, and make a posset of it, and drink the ale, and it will do you good; it is proven.

TO STOP BLEEDING FROM A FRESH WOUND.

§ 371. Take leek leaves, and pound them together with honey and wheat flour, and mix and beat them well until they are thick, and do not let them go near the fire, but apply cold to the wound.

A GOOD EYE WATER.

§ 372. Take rotten apples and strain them through spring water, and wash your eyes with it, and it will brighten the sight, and cleanse them of impurities.

ANOTHER.

§ 373. Take copperas and put it in spring water, and strain it clean, and when you go to bed apply it to your eyelids, and let a little drop into your eyes.

AGAINST DISEASE OF THE LUNGS, THE LIVER, AND THE TWO BREASTS.

§ 374. Make a habit of eating nine grains of pepper daily, and it is truly good.

AGAINST ALL HEAT AND INFLAMMATION IN THE FACE, SHOULD IT BE ST. ANTHONY'S FIRE.

§ 375. Take a quart of water from a smith's trough, a handful of leaves of the geidwad plant, a handful of elm leaves or its green bark,

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 171

a pennyworth of elecampane, and boil them together until half the water is gone, and put it to keep in an earthen vessel, and anoint the face with it.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE LIMBS, OR THE BACK, OR THE SIDES.

§ 376. Take blessed distillation, or distilled wine, and sheep's foot ointment, and put in an earthen vessel, and warm them and mix together well, and anoint the afflicted place, putting sufficient warm clothing on the person.

A PROVEN REMEDY AGAINST PAIN.

§ 377. Pound celery seed, and put it in blessed distillation or distilled wine, and strain through a press, and add boar's lard in a melted state around its top, and mix well, and with this warm anoint the painful place.

AGAINST PAIN OR SWELLING IN THE KNEES.

378. Take a quart of sour wine, and a handful of the herb called thyme by some, and boil together, and when half boiled add fresh butter and boil again together from a quart to a pint, and when you go to bed wash your feet well with it, and soak a cloth of three or four folds in it, and apply it around your painful knees as hot as you can bear it for six or seven nights, and it will assuredly do great good. If distilled wine or blessed distillation is available, add a spoonful to this when it is nearly done boiling, and mix well.

TO STOP BLEEDING FROM A WOUND, OR FROM THE NOSE.

§ 379. Take an old linen cloth and soak it well in red wine vinegar, or in whatever vinegar is available, then burn it to powder and apply it to the wound, and it will stop the bleeding

172 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

haste, if the bleeding be from the nose, blow this powder through a quill into the nostrils.

A PLASTER FOR A PAIN, OR WOUND, OR SWELLING THAT IS NOT MATURED.

§ 380. Take flour and boil it in the milk of a newly milked cow, until it is as thick as pottage, and put it in a pan with about as much of the fat of a lamb, and boil them well together, and mix well, and thus make a plaster and apply it to the pain as hot as can be endured.

FOR A DOG BITE.

§ 381. Seek the blessed herb betony, and garlic, and white of egg, and make into a plaster, and apply it thereto, and it will heal.

TO RIPEN CORNS.

§ 382. Take a pint of raw milk and put it on the fire, and add about as much of the fat of a lamb, well bruised, a handful of oatmeal, and beat and stir well while boiling, and let it boil until it is thick enough to be spread on a clean linen cloth, and apply it warm to the pain, and when it bursts, put a little turpentine on white leather, and prick it full of holes.

FOR DEAFNESS OF THE EARS.

§ 383. Take the juice of leeks and the gall of a goat together, and mix well, and pour into the ears, and put wool in after.

FOR DIMNESS OF THE EYES.

§ 384. Take the seeds of the celandine gathered through the morning dew, and pound them firmly, and strain the juice completely, and mix with an equal quantity of clear honey, and boil briskly until it is reduced by a third, and put in a glass vessel, and apply to your eyes when needed.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 173

AGAINST ITCHING.

§ 385. Take the root of the dock and butter, press the root and strain through a cloth, and purify the butter until clean, and boil the juice and the butter, and put in a pan to keep, and when there is need warm it, and anoint the flesh with it three times, that is every other day, and you will be healed.

AGAINST BAD FLESH.

§ 386. Take black wool, and soap, and powder of roasted beef, and apply to the bad flesh, and it will be healed.

AGAINST PAIN IN A JOINT'S HEAD.

§ 387. Take the crumb of wheaten bread from the oven, and sour apples, and southernwood, and dandelion, pound them well, equal quantities of each, and boil in good red wine until it becomes a plaster, and apply to the pain as hot as can be endured, and it will break out into pimples.

THINGS BAD FOR THE HEART.

§ 388. Onions, peas, cumin, garlic, sadness, anger, too much worry, too much travel, drinking cold water after travel, and bad news; and a person who desires health and long life should take care to keep his heart healthy, and not eat, nor drink, nor do those things that harm it, as a wise man says: a healthy heart, a healthy whole.

AGAINST PAIN WITHIN A JOINT.

§ 389. Take chickweed, and the leaves of brooklime, and their flowers, and iris, and pound them well together, and boil through May butter, and anoint the pain with it while warm, and keep it in an earthen box.

AGAINST THE GOUT.

§ 390. Take the mallows, and boil in spring water, and make a plaster, and apply to the pain.

174 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

ANOTHER.

§ 391. Boil the leaves of pennywort in the cream of sheep's milk, and apply to the pain.

FOR FROSTBITE.

§ 392. Take the leaves that are on the surface of the marsh when dry, and pound well, and take egg white and pound well together with the herbs, and take May butter and add to them, and pound all three together, and apply as a plaster, and it will heal.

FOR TOOTHACHE.

§ 393. Take the root of the iris, and pound firmly, and strain through linen, and cast the juice and the base of a wing into the nostril furthest from the aching tooth.

FOR BURNS FROM FIRE.

§ 394. Take ferns and pound them well together with sheep's milk, and apply where the burn is along with lard, and mix these thoroughly before applying it.

TO STOP BLEEDING FROM A WOUND.

§ 395. Take the leaves of rue, and pound well and apply to the wound.

ANOTHER.

§ 396. Take a branch of broom and scrape the bark and make a ball of it, and place in the wound, and bind firmly.

FOR WARTS.

§ 397. Take the leaves of the lily and ground ivy, and pound well together, and then take sheep's tallow and fry them well together, then take a strainer and strain it and anoint the afflicted part with it.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 175

ANOTHER.

§ 398. Take oat straw, and burn it, and put that ash on the wet place, and rub it on, and it will dry and heal it.

AGAINST SEEING DREAMS.

§ 399. Take feverfew combs, and put them about your neck, or else take their juice as a drink when going to sleep.

AGAINST CANKER IN THE MOUTH, OR IN THE CHEEKS, OR IN ANOTHER PLACE.

§ 400. Take eight or nine leaves of the geidwad plant, and pound them well together with a little salt and sour wine, and make a plaster and apply it.

A MEDICINE AGAINST DIMNESS OF THE EYES.

§ 401. Take twelve grains of fine wheat, and place the wheat on top of some clean smooth cold iron, and then take another iron and make it hot in the fire, and press the hot iron on the wheat, and the wheat will become like honey, then take it off the cold iron, and draw the membrane and the honey through the aching eye.

TO STOP BLOOD WHEN ONE OF THE CHIEF VEINS IS CUT, OR ONE OF THE VEINS OF THE HEART.

§ 402. Take a piece of salted beef, the white and the red together, as much as you think will fit into the wound, and place it on the embers until it is warm throughout, and so warm put it into the wound, and the blood will cease to flow.

AGAINST PAIN IN A LIMB WITH SWELLING, OR WITHOUT SWELLING.

§ 403. Take cress and mix with honey, and egg yolks, and fine wheat flour, and apply it as a plaster to the

176 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

pain, and if it be of a festering nature, it will cause it to gather and suppurate; and if not, it will draw out the pain and make it well.

AGAINST THE KING'S EVIL.

§ 404. Take the root of the lily, and dry it under the embers, and make it into powder, and mix that powder with goose grease, or with lard, and apply it thereto, and it will heal.

TO DRAW SPLINTERS OF BONE FROM A MAN'S HEAD, OR FROM ANY OTHER PLACE.

§ 405. Take savin, and the blessed oak, and rue, and mix them with wheat bran and white of eggs, and pound and knead these ingredients together thoroughly, and apply it thereto as a plaster.

AGAINST ALL MANNER OF SCABS OR ERUPTIONS ON THE SKIN, AND THE SCABBY HEAD.

§ 406. Take onions and bruise them small, and then boil in water or sour wine, and with that wash the sore or affected place, and it will destroy the scabby head and every other eruption on the body.

AGAINST THE ITCH.

§ 407. Take the root of the dock, and bruise them fine together with fresh butter, and fry them mixing and kneading well, and anoint the patient therewith, and he will be healed.

ANOTHER.

§ 408. Take the roots of alexanders and clean them thoroughly, and boil in spring water, and when they are sufficiently boiled, pound them and knead them with good thick cream, or unsalted butter, until it forms an ointment, and anoint the skin with it three times in nine days, that is, once every three days, and drink the water in which the roots were boiled, morning and night, a full draught thereof,

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 177

and this is good against the pox in the blood, and in the lymph causing eruptions on the skin, and scabs, and warts, and itching, and wens.

AGAINST WARTS.

§ 409. Take black wool and black soap, and bind them together against the sore or the warts.

AGAINST CANKER IN THE MOUTH.

§ 410. Take the juice of the leaves of broadleaved plantain and sour wine, and distilled rose water, and mix them together, and wash the mouth frequently with it.

AGAINST THE POX IN THE BLOOD AND IN THE LYMPH.

§ 411. Take chickweed and pound it well and strain its juice under pressure, and drink a cupful three times a day on an empty stomach, and it is truly good indeed.

ANOTHER.

§ 412. Take chickweed, and the leaves of the elm or the bark nearest to the trunk, and spring water, and the herbs of the liver, called by some sea-purslane, and pound them well, and strain the juice under pressure, and drink nothing but this drink for nine days, and take no food other than good wheaten bread made with yeast and goat's milk, for it is proven; and this remedy and the one above will cure the pox in the blood and the lymph, and the stone, and the great skin disease called in Latin scabies, and every venomous eruption in the blood and the lymph, because from that poison comes the lung sickness, and other ailments very numerous, more than one who does not know it would believe.

AGAINST A BURN FROM FIRE OR SCALDING WATER.

§ 413. Take black or white soap and bind it to the painful place.

178 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST PIMPLES ON THE FACE.

§ 414. Take wheat bran, and mix with vinegar and honey, and apply to your face.

AGAINST CORNS AND CARBUNCLES.

§ 415. Take wheat bran, and lard of pork, and May butter, and leaves of the geidwad plant, and pound them together and make a poultice, and apply to the corn, and it will ripen it, and draw out the matter.

AGAINST PAIN OR SWELLING OF A WOMAN'S BREAST.

§ 416. Take the bark of smooth holly and pound it well, and mix with good old ale, and strain it, and give it to the patient to drink, and use it regularly, and she will truly be healed, as is proven, and the breast will not fester at all.

ANOTHER.

§ 417. Seek the herb called bloodwort and pass it through a sieve, and pound it well and grind them together, and apply as a poultice to the breast, and she will truly be healed.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE LEGS.

§ 418. Take the herb called colt's hoof (it resembles the leaves of the cyngaw,) with the milk of a cow of one colour, and oatmeal groats, and May butter, boil them well and apply as a poultice to the pain while warm.

AGAINST TIGHTNESS IN THE CHEST.

§ 419. Take hyssop and lady's mantle, equal parts of each, pound them well and strain them clean, and take egg whites and mix that with the herbs together, and drink for three days on an empty stomach.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 179

ANOTHER.

§ 420. Take rue and boil it well in sour wine, and give it to the patient to drink.

FOR THE HYSTERIA (FAM).

§ 421. Take the grey herbs, and red fennel, and red mint, and boil them in old ale well, and strain cleanly through a linen cloth, and drink it warm, and you will be healed.

FOR THE THIRD PLAGUE.

§ 422. Whoever drinks the juice of St. George's herb and broad-leaved plantain mixed together, will be healed.

FOR PAIN OR SWELLING IN THE LEGS, OR FEET, OR ARMS.

§ 423. Take oatmeal, and cow's milk, and add to them the juice of the herb of pain, which others call house-leek, and sheep's tallow, and boil them all together until they are thick, and make a plaster of it and apply it around the sore, and this will ease the pain and the ache, and will drive the swelling away.

FOR A RUNNING EYE.

§ 424. Take black velvet and boil it in clean water, and mix the fat that floats on the surface of the water, and with that anoint your eye.

ANOTHER.

§ 425. Take lead and melt it in an iron vessel, and draw it down and cast upon it sour wine, and close it so that the vapour does not escape, and when it is cool and clear, pour the clear liquid into a glass bottle, and place in the bottle a piece of aloe the size of a large hazelnut, and when there is need of it, add snail slime, half and half, and wash your eyes with it,

180 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

or put this sharp wine over a beaten egg white, half and half, pound them well together, and wash your eyes with it.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 426. Take an apronful of tormentil, and boil it in the milk of a one-coloured cow until it is nearly dry, and apply it as a plaster to the head, and let the patient lie in bed, and put enough clothes on him until he sweats.

AGAINST COLD.

§ 427. Take the seed of nettles and boil in honey, and with it anoint your feet and your arms, and every other place that has need, and it will draw out the cold.

AGAINST PARALYSIS, THAT IS THE PALSY, WHICH TAKES AWAY A PERSON'S SPEECH.

§ 428. Take the leaves of clary, and leaves of rose, and where there are no leaves take the root of the rose, and pound these herbs together, as much of one as the other, and strain through good ale, and give to the patient to drink; it is proven, truly true.

AGAINST A WOUND THAT HAS HEALED ON THE OUTSIDE BUT IS INWARDLY PAINFUL.

§ 429. Take barley flour, and white of egg, and honey, and mix them together, and make a plaster, and apply it to the painful place, and it will ease it and heal it.

FOR ONE WHO HAS DRUNK POISON.

§ 430. Take fresh rue, wash it, and pound it fine, and add to white wine, and strain it, and give the patient a full drink of it.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI. 181

AGAINST A SWELLING IN THE WOMB, OR HARDNESS OF THE BELLY.

§ 431. Take flaxseed and boil it in goat's milk, and apply it frequently as a plaster.

AGAINST THE MOTHER'S PAIN.

§ 432. Take the herb mint or tansy, and pound it well, and strain it clean, and boil it with old ale, and drink it as warm as you can.

AGAINST WORMS.

§ 433. Take the juice of tansy, and milk, and strain it, and boil it well until it reduces by a third, and drink it warm.

AGAINST A SCABBY HEAD.

§ 434. Take pitch and wax and boil them together, and shave the scabby head clean, and make a plaster and apply it to the head as warm as can be endured, and leave it there for nine days.

AGAINST PAIN IN AN EYE THAT IS FORMING A CATARACT.

§ 435. Take the yolk of an egg and fine wheat flour, and a little blue vitriol, and mix firmly, and apply it to the eye, and it will break the cataract.

AGAINST A CATARACT ON A PERSON'S EYE.

§ 436. Apply the juice of ground ivy to the cataract, and this will break it and heal it.

AGAINST A BRUISE.

§ 437. Take the white of an egg that has been beaten, and apply it on a cloth as a plaster.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE BACK.

§ 438. Take young broom and boil it in spring water, and with that water wash the back.

182 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR A MAN WHO HAS BEEN BURNED BY A WOMAN.

§ 439. Take ground ointment and beer, and mix them, and wet a linen cloth in it, and wrap it around the penis.

FOR TIGHTNESS OF THE CHEST.

§ 440. Take strained juice of hyssop, and as much of Lady's bedstraw, and mix with an equal amount of egg white, and drink it as your sole drink for three days.

FOR PAIN IN THE CHEST.

§ 441. Take watercress, and the leaves of the cleavers, and pound them together and apply to your chest.

FOR A STITCH UNDER THE SIDE.

§ 442. Take the juice of cleavers, and mulled wine, one measure of juice to two measures of wine, and drink it, for it will ease the stitch under the side and in the womb, and in the stomach, and it is good against pain in the head and paralysis or lameness; it is proven.

FOR THE BLACK DISEASE.

§ 443. Take thyme, that is the herb called thyme, and rue, and brooklime, and hyssop, and the root of watercress, and fennel, and the leaves of the plant called in Latin chamaerops, and two spoonfuls of anise seed, and boil all in a quart of water with three spoonfuls of honey, and strain through a clean cloth, and drink of it according to the state of the blood.

FOR CURING CANCER.

§ 444. Take a vial of red wine, three or four spoonfuls of honey, and as much as a large walnut of ointment, and mix and boil together until a third is consumed, and strain it, and put it in a bottle to keep, and wash the wound frequently with it, and this will heal it.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI. 183

FOR A MAN WHO HAS BEEN BURNED BY A WOMAN.

§ 445. Take linseed and white goat's milk, and boil into a poultice, and apply it around the rod on all sides; it is proven.

FOR PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 446. Take a spoonful of the juice of saffron flowers, a spoonful of wine, and a spoonful of honey, and put into them nine peppercorns, and drink of this for four days, twice a day.

TO DRAW OUT A WOUND AND SWELLING, AND TO EASE WHERE THERE IS PAIN.

§ 447. Take roughly a measure of oatmeal, and buttermilk, and the juice of pain-herbs, and suet of elder, and grind them together until they are not too thick, and make a plaster, and apply it warm to the painful place, and this will ease the pain and draw away the swelling.

FOR SPITTING BLOOD.

§ 448. Take parsley of the rock, and mint, and rue, and saffron flowers, and boil them in freshly drawn milk, and drink of it warm, and you will be healed.

FOR NAUSEA.

§ 449. Take a handful of red herbs and parsley, and pound them well together, and apply as a plaster to the womb.

TO STRENGTHEN THE VESSEL IN WHICH NATURE RESTS.

§ 450. Take acorns and roast them hard, and grind them to a powder, put a spoonful in a drink of ale, and drink it warm every morning for a week to nine days, and lie in your bed for an hour or two.

184 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

GOOD WATER FOR THE EYES.

§ 451. Take rotten apples and strain them through spring water, and wash your eyes with it; this will wonderfully cleanse and brighten your eyes.

FOR TOOTHACHE.

§ 452. Take holly leaves and boil them in spring water until they are tender, then remove the pot from the fire to the floor, put a cloth around your head, and hold your mouth open over the top of the pot to receive the steam, and you will be healed.

A PROVEN REMEDY FOR TOOTHACHE.

§ 453. Take the root of Spanish fern, wash it clean, pound it fine, and make from it three small balls in your hand, each about the size of a plum, and place the first ball between your cheek and the aching tooth for the time it takes to walk a mile at a moderate pace. As the water gathers, spit it out, and when you think the ball has been there that long, put in another, and after that same length of time the third. Then lie down on your bed, wrap yourself up warmly, and when you have slept you will be healed. This I have proven many times myself, and I have found it a ready remedy against the pain of toothache.

TO KNOW WHETHER THE SKULL IS FRACTURED.

§ 454. If the flesh is whole on the surface, shave the hair from where the injury is, and place a piece of thick linen cloth doubled over, with a beaten egg white spread upon the linen, and bind it over the wound for one night. In the morning remove it and examine whether the linen is wet; if it is damp and moist, it is certain that the bone is fractured.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 185

FOR WIND IN THE STOMACH.

§ 455. Take seeds of field carrots and make them into balls the size of peas, with honey, and take four of them twice a day for three days.

FOR PAIN OF THE LIPS.

§ 456. Take the root of the skull-cap, and pound it well, and take cold cream of milk and pour it over it, and mix well, and strain through a clean linen cloth, and apply that juice to your lips.

TO CREATE AN APPETITE FOR FOOD.

§ 457. Boil earth-gall in clean bright water, and let the patient drink of it, blood-warm, fasting, three days, nine spoonfuls each day, and he will be well.

FOR THE BITE OF EVERY VENOMOUS REPTILE.

§ 458. Take the leaves of broad-leaved plantain and drink their juice, and take equal parts of oat-straw and yellow-weed, and pound them finely, and temper them with sour whey and apply to the wound, and it will ease the pain, and reduce the swelling, and draw out the poison.

FOR THE BITE OF A MAD DOG.

§ 459. Take a handful of betony, a handful of wild garlic, a handful of knotgrass, a vial of hollow water, and pound the herbs well in the water, and strain, and add a pennyworth of treacle, and give it to the patient to drink for two or three mornings; it is proven.

FOR A DISEASE OF THE EYE.

§ 460. Take cream of milk and an equal quantity of white of eggs, and make a linen cloth the size of the eye, and soak it in the plaster and apply it.

186 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST DRUNKENNESS.

§ 461. Take a handful of the plant called betony, which is called St. Ffraid's combs, and pound it well and mix with spring water, and strain it clean, and drink it before eating anything else, and you will not get drunk that day.

FOR A GOOD RISING OF THE HEAD AND STOMACH.

§ 462. Take three spoonfuls of the juice of betony three mornings in succession, and blow it with the tip of a feather into your nostrils.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE LEGS.

§ 463. Seek the herb called foal's hoof, a handful, and as much of the leaves of celandine, and pound them, and mix them with the milk of a cow of one colour, and oat bran, and butter, and boil them well, and apply as a poultice to the painful area as warm as you can bear it, and it will bring relief.

AGAINST THE SAME THING.

§ 464. Take those leaves without pounding them and wrap them around your feet like a bandage, day and night; it will draw out poisonous fluid; at other times grey paper in the same manner like a stocking-wrap; it is proven.

AGAINST CHILBLAINS, OR BLISTERS ON THE HEELS AND FEET.

§ 465. Take the warm drippings of wax when wax is being strained, and put your feet in the warm drippings as warm as you can bear it, and stand on it for a long time and it will heal, drawing out the blisters.

SUBDUING THE HYSTERIA.

§ 466. Take an ointment of quicksilver, and May butter, or pig's lard rendered in the month of May, and wax, and rosin, and melt them

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 187

together with Taliesin's herbs, eating equal amounts of each, but with more of the butter, or lard, than of the wax and the resin, and boil them well together, and strain, and with that ointment anoint the side where the pain is, up and down as best you can; it is proven.

AGAINST FAILING TO GO TO THE TOILET.

467. Take the root of the herb called gloria, others call it pig's herb, and pound the roots well like garlic with old ale, let it stand for a time, and warm the strained drink a little, and give it to the patient to drink, and he will truly be able to go freely; it is proven.

AGAINST PAIN IN A SWELLING WHEN THE SKIN IS THIN.

§ 468. Take the best ale you can get, a quart and a half of it, and boil it well down until it is reduced to a spoonful full, and that is a good ointment against all swelling pain — apply it on a piece of raw linen cloth to the sore, and use it thus and it will draw out all the impurity most effectively, and after that seek a growth ointment and apply it. If there is a swelling in the leg, get foxglove leaves from the hillside, and pound them, and apply them with clay from the chest on top of the leaves, and it is good.

ANOTHER TO REDUCE THE SWELLING AND TO DRAW OUT THE BAD.

§ 469. Take oak bark and apply it piece by piece on the thin skin, and use it thus, and it is good.

AGAINST A WOMAN LOSING HER FRUIT AND HER STRENGTH.

§ 470. Take the bark of the blackthorn, the part nearest the wood, scrape away the outer part, and pound it well with the milk of a one-coloured cow, and mix it and give it as a drink to the woman, and it is truly good to use it thus.

188 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

ANOTHER.

§ 471. Take a handful of meadowsweet and pound it well, and put it into good red wine, and strain it clean, and give it as a drink to the woman morning and night, as much as she can drink of it, and it is truly a good practice, and keep the handfuls dry in the house so that they may be had in winter, and powder them at that time, and put the powder into full spoonfuls of wine, and drink it as warm as possible, and the roots are good eaten along with the wine and strained, or likewise powdered in the wine, and it is good to keep this herb in a garden by itself.

FOR A THORN.

§ 472. Take washing soap and apply it; it will draw it out well, and keep it applied until it comes out.

FOR A SICK ANIMAL.

§ 473. Take black soap and boil it in ale, and give it as a drink to the animal by pouring it into its throat, and it will be able to go to the field.

FOR BREAST DISEASE.

§ 474. Take broad plantain leaves and lard, and pound them together, and apply it.

FOR SWELLING IN THE WOMB.

§ 475. Get goats' whey, and pound the herb called goats' garlic, and put it into the whey and strain it, and drink only that as a drink for three days.

FOR SUPPRESSION OF URINE.

§ 476. Take red nettles and parsley, and make them into a plaster, and apply it to your bladder.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 189

A GOOD PRACTICE TO KEEP THE BODY IN HEALTH.

§ 477. Put cold spring water on your face every morning, and on your hands and private parts, whether male or female, and scrub well, and once a week along your back and neck, scrubbing well with a rough cloth.

TO KILL A WORM THAT IS IN A PERSON'S FLESH.

§ 478. Take the fat of a red boar, and May butter, and the leaves of the houseleek, and mead, and beat them all together, and make an ointment of it, and apply it, and that will kill it.

ANOTHER.

§ 479. Take the juice of the houseleek, and a little distilled wine, and anoint where the worm is, and this will kill it.

AGAINST BLEEDING FROM THE NOSE.

§ 480. Take an egg-shell* and catch the blood in the shell, and put it in the fire to bake until it becomes powder, and cast that powder into the nostrils, and it will stop the bleeding; it is proven.

AGAINST PAIN IN A WOMAN'S BREAST.

§ 481. Take the bark of smooth holly, and pound it well, and mix with good old ale, and strain it, and give it to the patient to drink, and by using it the patient will truly be healed; it is proven, the breast will not fester at all.

ANOTHER.

§ 482. Seek the herb of the bleeding wound and press it through its skin, and pound well together, and apply to the breast, and the patient will truly be healed.

* Cocwy means a shell or bowl.

190 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST PAIN IN WHATEVER PART OF THE BODY IT MAY BE.

§ 483. Seek the sediment of flat wine, half a gallon, and an equal amount of the sediment of good old ale, and a phial full of wheat bran, and the roots of the five-finger plant, and boil them well, and pound the herbs well, and boil all together until it becomes thick; the better they are boiled together, the better the plaster will be. Apply this to the pain, and use it regularly, and you will truly be healed, with God's help; it is proven.

AGAINST PAIN OF THE STOMACH.

§ 484. Take camomile and pound it well and boil in a pint of wine until it is reduced to half a pint, and give it to the patient to drink, and he will truly be healed.

ANOTHER.

§ 485. Boil wild carrot seeds and grind them in their own water, and drink as a beverage; it is proven.

TO HEAL A BRUISE, AND TO DRAW WATER FROM THE PAIN, OR FROM TENSE JOINTS, OR SWELLING OF THE LIMBS FROM WATERY NATURE OR BAD BLOOD OR CORRUPTED FLESH.

§ 486. Take half a pound weight of sheep's tallow, and some cheap black soap, and melt them together, and add six eggs, having mixed the white and yolk together, and mix all well together, and draw it to the floor to cool; then beat them well together and spread on a linen cloth as wide as needed, and apply to the pain, once daily or every other day, until healed.

TO DRAW WATERY NATURE OR BAD BLOOD FROM A BRUISED HEAD.

§ 487. Wash your hands clean, and take the oil of the elm tree and rub it into the person's ears, and continue this for eight days, and he will be healed.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 191

AGAINST THE FILM ON THE EYES WHICH IS CALLED THE ANGLE (PTERYGIUM).

§ 488. Take pepper and grind it to powder, and mix it with the marrow of an old goose's wing bone, and place it in fine linen, and burn upon a flat stone to fine powder, and apply that to the eyes until they are healed.

ANOTHER.

§ 489. Take the flowers of white hawthorn and the flowers of elder, and make a water from them, and use it morning and night; it is good for eyes that are becoming red, and burning, and watering.

ANOTHER.

§ 490. Boil the juice of celandine into your eyes by means of a feather-quill, twice a day.

AGAINST THE ITCH.

§ 491. Seek the leaves of the cleavers and pound them and press out their juice, and with that anoint the skin well, morning and night, for nine days, and you will be healed.

AGAINST A BLOW TO THE HEAD, OR A FALL UNTIL THE BONE IS BROKEN, AND TO SCATTER THE BRUISE.

§ 492. Take betony, that is saffron-combs, and pound it firmly, and boil it well in the dregs of red wine, and apply it as a plaster to the head; this will cool it and press the bones each back to the other, truly.

AGAINST PAIN OF THE NATURE OF THE PLAGUE OR PESTILENCE.

§ 493. Take clean oats and fry them in fresh butter until they are browning, and apply to the pain on a piece of cloth, and healing will come, truly, very truly.

* Maen, a word used in Glamorgan for a griddle.

192 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDFAI.

AGAINST ERYSIPELAS (THE JEWISH FLAME).

§ 494. Take the dung of geese that graze outside, and the carllys, and eyebright, and bettain, and May butter without salt, pound them together, put them on the fire to boil, strain them clean, store in a clean vessel, and anoint the patient and he will be healed.

TO ENLARGE THE CHEST, THE THROAT, AND THE BREAST.

§ 495. Take red fennel, and the tops of hyssop and *briw, and glyf, and boil in running water from springs that never dry up, and give to the patient to drink, and he will truly be well.

AGAINST THE BITE OF A MAD DOG.

§ 496. Boil the wild geidwad in ale or water, and drink it as a beverage for nine days; it is proven.

AGAINST ALL MANNER OF EVIL PAIN IN THE WORLD, HOWEVER IT COMES.

§ 497. Take parsley, and plantain, and eyebright, and garlic, and grains of paris, pound them well and strain them, and put the juice into ale, and drink it; and if there be beef, or dairy food, let none be eaten or drunk until the patient recovers.

AGAINST THE CROUP.

§ 498. Take grey horehound, and a handful of red ones, upon whey of goats, and boil well, and drink a cupful every morning, and you will be healed.

AGAINST THE WHOOPING COUGH AND THE COUGH.

§ 499. Take lion's claw in buttermilk, and give to the patient on an empty stomach in the morning, and late at night, and he will be healed.

* qu. is it Briweg?

MEDDYGON MYDDFAI. 193

AGAINST COUGH.

§ 500. Take a handful of white horehound and pound it well, and put it into old good ale, and strain it clean under pressure, and make a posset of that ale, and drink the clear liquid, and you will be healed.

ANOTHER AGAINST COUGH.

§ 501. Take stone parsley seeds with hard-boiled eggs, and take it twice a day for thirteen days, and you will be healed.

AGAINST COUGH.

§ 502. Take duck fat, and hen's fat, and the marrow of a fresh meat bone, and make an ointment and anoint your breast, but do not touch the stomach with it, and it will heal you.

AGAINST A HEAD ERUPTION CAUSED BY HEAT.

§ 503. First take the sediment of strong good ale, and rosin, and rye flour, and make three plasters and apply them to the head, allowing a week's interval between each one, washing with sour brine, and scraping well, and pulling out all the dead hair, and letting blood where there is redness, and this between each of the three treatments above; and then take egg whites and rye flour, and make three plasters for three treatments, washing each time cleanly, and then take the root of elecampane, and the root of dock, and ground ivy, and tormentil, and pound them well together, and boil thoroughly in beef fat, and strain cleanly, and when cool take blue vitriol, a small measure of sulphur and make into a very fine powder and mix into the strained ointment, pressing it in completely and sealing it well from the breast, so that it becomes like thick honey, and with that anoint the head well, and then take butter with any of the earth herbs named

* From pounding.

194 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

above, but avoid the powder, and make an ointment of them, and anoint with it and he will be healed.

HERE IS A REMEDY FOR A MAN WHO HAS A RUNNING HEAD,
WHICH WILL NOT CEASE.

§ 504. Get pitch and new wax, and melt together, and apply as a plaster as hot as can be endured, and leave for nine days without moving it.

ANOTHER.

§ 505. Take sulphur and quicksilver, and grind together with roasted garlic and fresh lard, and mix together, and with this anoint the head.

ANOTHER.

§ 506. Take two handfuls of the plant called in Latin petilion, before it flowers, and boil in a bottle of strong brine until half is gone, then wash the head with that brine while warm, and scrape the eruptions off, and then make a plaster of the plant and apply to the head while warm, and leave there a day and a night and then remove it, and make a plaster of rye flour and running water, and make it like thick porridge and apply on a piece of linen large enough to cover the sore, and leave for three days and three nights, and then remove it and wash the head in strong buttermilk, and scrape it down to the flesh, and take red onions and make a plaster over the sore by boiling them in water, and temper them with the juice of mountain mint and the melted fat of an old boar, and use this until he is healed.

ANOTHER.

§ 507. Get pitch, and wax of equal measure, and melt together, and pour into a bowl, and let it stand in water until it is cool, and scrape the head, and wash as described above, and take a linen cloth and apply to the head, and apply

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 195

linen on that, then take some of the same from the box and make it into a poultice and apply it on the linen, and put linen over that, then obtain a headband and bind the forehead and the whole so that the poultice is not lost, and leave it there seven or eight days, and for each dressing wash the head as described, and when you see there is no further need of this, take foot-grease when it is being rendered, and skim it from the water in which it is being boiled into another vessel, and put it in a box, and with that anoint the head until it is healed; it is proved.

TO MAKE THE HAIR GROW.

§ 508. Shave the head clean with a razor, and take honey and onion juice, equal parts of each, and with that anoint the head and rub it well every morning, and every night wash the head with distilled honey; it is proved.

ANOTHER.

§ 509. Shave the head clean with a razor, and anoint it with honey and apply soft sulphur upon it.

TO CURE THE ITCH, ALSO CALLED THE DUEGWST, AND THE DISEASE OF THE ITCH.

§ 510. Take fox fern, the best being that which grows on the oak, and boil it in strong dark brine, and drink a full draught of it every other day for eight days, and live on a diet of fresh meat without vegetables except taking wheaten bread of fine quality with it, and drinking as a beverage good wine or ale and milk in equal parts of each, but drinking sparingly, and take seed of garden cress, and fennel, and field carrots, and anise, and cinnamon and such dry herbs in your drink, and walk well every day, and engage in vocal music and instrumental music played by another, and do not practice music yourself, and by practicing these things you will recover through God.

196 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST PALPITATION OF THE HEART.

§ 511. Take the fat of the red liver, called in Latin cariophilum major, with honey, powder of anise seed, and fennel seed sprinkled upon it, a full drink morning and night, and keep the flowers dry so that you may obtain them at any season throughout the year.

A PLASTER TO REDUCE THE SWELLING OF A BRUISE OR BLOW, OR ANY OTHER SWELLING ON A PERSON'S BODY, OR ON A LIMB WHERE THE SWELLING CONCEALS THE BRUISE.

§ 512. Take a good handful of the leaves of lovage, called in Latin oleoselinum, and wheat bran, and the whites of four eggs, pound the herbs well, and beat the egg whites until thin, place these upon the wheat bran and mix into a plaster, and apply it, and it will draw out the swelling entirely, so that the bruise may be plainly seen.

AGAINST THE DROPSY, CALLED IN LATIN HYDROPS.

§ 513. Take fine sifted dough and make into a large pot or pastry case such as would hold a goose or at least two capons, and fill the pot with these good herbs, namely two handfuls of garden parsley, two handfuls of elderberry, and one handful of dandelion, that is saffron combs, and one handful of brooklime, and one handful of hart's tongue, and one handful of the root of parsley or lovage well washed, and half a handful of hyssop, and half a handful of columbine called in Latin aquilegia, and place all these herbs, except the parsley, into the vessel, then take an ounce of powdered leek root or leek beard, an ounce of powdered anise, two ounces of powdered liquorice, and put them all together into the pot above and close them well with the dough, and place it in an oven heated like that for bread, and bake well, and take it out when done and cut it into four parts, and quickly place them in an earthen vessel of sufficient size, and pour upon them two gallons of good strong old ale that has been drawn

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 197

from the sediment, and close the vessel tightly, and thus let it settle for one night, and from then on drink a good draught of it three times daily — morning, midday, and night — and that liquor will be more soothing for you than the others; cast a little wood-ash of broom upon it each time, and drink it thus, and it will preserve you and prevent the dropsy; it is proven.

THE METHOD OF MAKING BROOM-ASH, WHICH IS VERY GOOD
AGAINST THE DROPSY AND AGAINST FEVER, WHEN PUT INTO A SUITABLE DRINK,
OR MIXED WITH HONEY AND MADE INTO AN ELECTUARY, OR INTO PILLS, AND
TAKING A MEASURE OF IT NIGHT AND MORNING, NO LESS THAN FOUR PILLS OR
THAT AMOUNT OF THE ELECTUARY.

§ 514. Take a large slice of iron or a baking stone, and heat it until it is red-hot, and place fresh broom upon the slice when they are in their full seed, which is best, and let the herbs burn and be thoroughly reduced, and burn them thus until there is a vial-measure of six of the ash; then store it away, and cover the vessel in which it is kept very tightly, so that no air gets to it or from it; and when there is occasion to use a spoonful of it, take it in a good draught of old strong ale, or on good old mead, or in a drink of good white wine.

FOR HOT RED ERYSIPELAS, AND SWELLING WITH PAIN,
AND BURNING IN A JOINT OR OTHER MEMBER.

§ 515. Get the finest barley flour and butter that has been well clarified, and put a little salt in it as if one were to eat it, and mix it with the flour little by little in equal measure, and keep in a clean closed vessel as long as you wish; apply it on cloth or linen to the place of the pain, and if it rises like leaven, work it well with a flat piece of wood, and if it hardens or dries, temper it with egg white, and use it thus; and you will be healed, in God's truth, for it is proven.

FOR A BAD RINGWORM.

§ 516. Get litharge and powder it, and mix with black soap, and apply it frequently, and it will heal.

198 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST ALL BINDING OR SWELLING PAIN THAT BINDS A MAN'S LIMBS AND HIS BACK, OF A HOT BINDING NATURE.

§ 517. Seek hemlock, plaintain, mallow, and red fennel, and the flowers of iris if available, and if not seek hollyhock, and bruise them between your hands, all the herbs, and boil them in the patient's own urine for a long time, and cast about his head a little clarified butter well boiled, and draw it from the fire, and with that wash the pain while hot, and apply the herbs as a plaster to it while hot upon a cloth of woollen, and leave it there overnight, and then remove it and warm it again and apply it a second time, and continue using it until he is well; and the man's own urine is better than another man's urine lest it be infected, and by following this practice you will truly be healed.

AGAINST RINGWORM ON A PERSON, AND WATER TO KILL IT WHEREVER IT MAY BE ON THE BODY OF A MAN.

§ 518. Take a bottle of clean water, and put it in a clean vessel on the fire, and take one measure of alum, and an ounce of blue vitriol, and put them in the water, and boil well, and then draw it from the fire and allow it to settle clear, and put it in an earthen pot and seal it well, and when it is needed take some of it to warm, and then take a linen cloth and wash the sore with it, and you will be healed, and it will dry the ringworm and destroy it.

AGAINST PALSY, THAT IS TO SAY PARALYSIS.

§ 519. Take a little of the leaves of bay, and wild clary, and leaves of strawberry, and leaves or roots of elder, and leaves of woodbine, and rosemary, and pound each one separately very finely, and mix with lard and make a small ball of each one of them, and put in an earthen pot for ten days, and then put in a pan and break them up small, and apply heat to them over the fire, and mix with May butter or coarse oil, and strain through a cloth while warm, and put in

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 199

glass, and when you go to work with it, apply it by the fire every morning and evening, and it will heal, by God's grace — this is proven.

AGAINST THE GREAT GOUT OR THE MILD GOUT, WHICH OCCURS IN THE JOINTS AND THE FEET, AND THE HANDS, AND IN THE STOMACH, AND THE KNEES, AND THE HEAD, AND CAUSES SWELLING AND IRRITATION, BECAUSE THE SINEWS DRY INTO A CHALKY SUBSTANCE, AND THIS PAIN IS CALLED IN LATIN Arthritis.

§ 520. Take the juice of tansy, that is tansy, and pure honey, equal parts of each, and mix them together, and if the sore is warm, fry them together in a pan and keep it well; if the sore is cold, let the medicine be cold, and apply it to the pain on a woolen cloth of camomile, and this is good and proven; for I have witnessed it: a woman who had lain for four years with this disease was healed within one month by using this medicine.

ANOTHER REMEDY AGAINST THE GREAT GOUT.

§ 521. Take a measure of rue, and a measure of coarse salt, and the white and yolk of an egg, and a little black soap, and pound the rue and the salt together and add the egg and the black soap to them, and spread well, mixing as you go, and apply as a plaster to the pain, and it will heal.

ANOTHER REMEDY FOR THE SAME DISEASE.

§ 522. Take one or two onions, and set them to bake well before the fire, and take a little of the blessed distillation and place it over the fire in a pewter still, then cut the onions finely, and boil them in the blessed distillation, and let them boil a little together, then take a clean cloth and strain into a bowl, and apply that to the pain night and morning until it is healed, and it is

* Arthritis, I. M.    † Camomile perhaps.

200 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

Many of the physicians say that this is a proven thing, and as inexpensive in cost as it is.

FOR THE SAME DISEASE.

§ 523. Take linseed, and the lees of wine, and lime that has not been slaked, equal amounts of each, and boil together for a long boiling, and make into a plaster and apply it; and if it is warm, seek pennywort and bruise it fine, and apply it to the pain, and it will draw the heat from the swelling; it is proven.

FOR THE SAME PAIN.

§ 524. Take a handful of geidwad, and a handful of liverwort, and a handful of leaves of the withered plant, and boil in a gallon of still water until it reduces to a quart, and wash the pain with it, and after you have finished washing it, apply the herbs to it, and with God's help it shall heal.

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME PAIN.

§ 525. Take the yolks of three eggs that have been hard-boiled, and grind them fine in a pan over the fire, or as into a powder, and then strain clean, and this ointment is good against the great gout, and against many other diseases indeed.

FOR THE SAME PAIN.

§ 526. Take the juice of pennywort, and a little aloe, and the juice of plantain if it be their season, and two spoonfuls of the powder of madder, and put in a gallon of running water, and boil well together, but it is not good to boil them too much, and anoint the patient with it as hot as he can bear it, and soak a linen cloth in that liquid, and apply it to him, and he shall heal.

MEDDYGON MYDDFAI. 201

A ROYAL PLASTER AGAINST THE GREAT GOUT IN THE HEAD.

§ 527. Take two handfuls of barley and pound them fine in a mortar, and take a handful of bittain, that is the combs of saffron, and pound them fine on their own to the amount of half the barley, and then mix together with viii of wine, and broth half as much as that, and mix the bittain and the barley together into a consistency like porridge, and put on the fire to warm well, and spread on a cloth, and apply to the head where the pain is, as warm as you can bear it, well away from the cheekbones to the middle of the forehead, and you will be healed.

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 528. Obtain distilled rose, and distilled water of the blessed oak, and woman's milk, and the white of an egg that has been cleaned, and mix together, and apply to the head; and if there is any pain in the eye, let the juice drop into the eye, and you will be healed.

AGAINST THE GREAT GOUT.

§ 529. Take half a measure of white wine and deer fat, or if that is not available, the fat of a wether sheep, and wheat bran, not the least nor the most; and boil them together until they become thick, and then take a measure of garlic and peel them clean and pound them fine, and add together with the rest but take care lest the other be too warm, as then the garlic will lose its potency, and mix together, and apply as a plaster between the gout and the healthy place, so that it may draw it away until he is healed.

AGAINST ALL PAIN.

§ 530. Take the suckers of briars, that is blackberries, the tender ones, and tips of broom, and tips of rue, and pound them fine and smooth together, but first wash them clean, and temper them
2 D

202 THE PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

with the ointment of the willow-tree, and thus this ointment is made, and with it the pain is cured.

AGAINST THE FLUX, COLD OR HOT.

§ 531. Get anise seed and the seed of smallage, which is called in Latin letisticwm vulgaris, and make it into a powder, and use it in your food and drink; and spikenard of Spain is good in that drink and in every other drink.

AN OINTMENT AGAINST THE FLUX, COLD OR HOT.

§ 532. Get the tops of the white vines, and the roots of the red fennel, and the bened, and boil them together in a pan until the herbs sink to the bottom, and put it in a vessel so that the patient may anoint himself therein and wash himself, and make a broth by boiling spring water with wild boar flesh or mutton, boiling this through it, and coloring it with saffron, and it is good against every kind of flux, whether cold or hot; in the name of Jesus.

AGAINST BLEEDING OF THE SEAT, CALLED THE HORSEMAN'S COMPLAINT, AND THE PILES.

§ 533. Get the best blessed distillation and soak a fine linen cloth in it, and insert it between the two buttocks as far as you can; if the piles are internal, if they are external wash them with the distillation three or four days upon going to bed.

AGAINST THE SAME COMPLAINT.

§ 534. Get the liver of a he-goat, and the leaves of the elder tree, bruise them together, and make them into small balls, and let the patient sit in a perforated chair, and close the chair, and place a bowl with burning coals beneath, and throw the balls upon the fire, and keep the vapor around the person, and cover him over with clothes.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 203

ANOTHER.

§ 535. Let the patient sit in a chair over a warm ointment of mallow, pennywort, and cow's milk.

AGAINST THE QUINSY.

§ 536. Boil grey herbs, green mint, and the seed of the wewyrllys, and fennel seed in water and milk, half and half, and drink a good drink of it as warm as you can, and another drink of it when quite cold, and drink nothing but water with your food, and be prepared, abstaining from butter and meat drippings, and good ale, and live on mutton at dinner time, and cow's or goat's milk morning and night with fine wheaten bread, and a good drink for this ailment is burnt limestone ground very fine, placed in water and milk as a small spoonful of drink at the time of meals; it is proven.

HERE IS A GOOD REGIMEN FOR A MAN WHO IS FREQUENTLY TROUBLED BY THE QUINSY.

§ 537. Take every morning, two hours before mealtime, a slice of the best fermented wheaten bread, toasted before the fire until it is very hard and brown, taking care not to burn it, and eat this by itself and drink nothing at all after it, and if you eat meat remove all the fat, and the best meat is mutton, and fine wheaten bread made with the best ferment from the oven with it, and a drink of water or whey with the food, and make use of gruels and oatmeal porridges with milk or honey, or wine or verjuice, and avoid all garden vegetables, and endeavour to grind fennel seed and caraway seed, and wewyrllys seed with your wheaten bread, and keep from butter, and pork especially the old, and fat cheese, and goose flesh, and duck flesh.

204 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST THE ABSCESS, CALLED THE POSTWM.

§ 538. Take cow's milk, and linseed, and a little boiled garlic, and boil them well together, and make into a plaster, and apply it.

WATER AGAINST ALL KINDS OF THE GREAT GOUT.

§ 539. Seek the seed of purslane at the first feast of Mary in autumn, and place in an earthen pot filled to the brim and sealed tightly upon it, and put it in the ground a full half yard in depth, and leave it there until the last feast of Mary in spring, then open it, and you will find in the pot clear water; keep it well in a tightly sealed glass vessel; it is very good against all kinds of the great gout.

TO MAKE THE EYES BRIGHT.

§ 540. Take fresh fish, namely those that appear like small herrings, and place them in the sun or at a distance before the fire in a heat comparable to the sun until oil comes from them, and mix that with honey, and anoint your eyes.

AGAINST RUNNING EYES.

§ 541. Take the leaves of red cabbage, called in some places red kale, and hen's lard, and pound them well together, and apply it at night under bandages.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE EYES.

§ 542. Take the juice of lady's chair, which some call Lleurwg's herb, and the juice of celandine, and boil together, and anoint your eyes.

AGAINST LOOSE BONES IN A PERSON'S HEAD.

§ 543. Drink the juice of goldenrod four spoonfuls three times a day on an empty stomach, and they will come out.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 205

AGAINST CANCER.

§ 544. Take hardhead [knapweed], and goats' feet, and burn them in an oven, and make into a powder, and apply to the cancer.

AGAINST THE GREAT STINKING GOUT.

§ 545. Seek the juice of Mary's herbs, and the herb called ribwort plantain, and the white of an egg, and mouse-ears, and wheat flour of rye, and make a plaster and apply it, and put a linen cloth over it until it dries, and thus do daily until he is well.

AGAINST GWRTHLYS [HERB OF REPULSION / RINGWORM].

§ 546. Seek broad plantain and make into a plaster, and apply it, and he will be healed.

AGAINST THE FESTERING SORE IN THE HEAD, CALLED POSTWN Y PENN, CAUSED BY STOPPAGE AND OBSTRUCTION IN THE EARS.

§ 547. Take the bitter of the dunes and pound it well, and oil of almonds, and put in a silver spoon and place it on top of embers, and let it boil, and mix it well, and take a clean linen cloth and make a bandage, and dip it in the liquid, and put it in the painful ear, and bind it until the pus breaks out; it is proven.

TO DRAW A TOOTH AND ITS ROOT.

§ 548. Take the root of pig's herbs [sow thistle], and black seeds, and put the root in goats' milk and pound them together well, then add to them the black seeds pounded separately upon their own tops, with the pounded root, and work the whole into a lump, and put it in sour wine three times, and renew the sour wine three times, and then make the lump into a powder, and put sour wine on it for three more days, and when it clears pour off the sour wine and let the powder dry in the sun or in the warmth of a fire, and put it in the tooth, if closed, and it will draw it out painlessly and completely.

206 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR PAIN IN THE HEAD AND THE WHOOPING COUGH.

§ 549. Take a red onion and bruise it very finely, with a little bile, and add to the weight of it a little honey and boil well, and when it has boiled bring it up tightly and push some into his nostrils, and let him rise to his feet, and he will sneeze, and will be healed and eased.

TO MAKE A PITCHED CLOTH.

§ 550. Take two ounces of pitch, two ounces of tar, two ounces of turpentine, two ounces and a quarter of mastic, one ounce of frankincense, and mix them all together well, and put on the fire and take a portion of the juice of plantain, and mix with them, and put the cloth in that melted mixture, and let it absorb enough of it, and take what goes into it, then let it cool, and when you wish to use it again put it by the fire to soften, and apply to the wound, wherever there is a sore or other pain in a person's body.

THE WAY TO MAKE A FOOTSORE PLASTER, PROVIDED IT IS FOR WOUNDS THAT ARE BURNING.

§ 551. Take the helogan, that is the herb of the sun, and which others call the great herb of the sun, and senna, and the root of iris or flag, and the root of the pig's herb called morel, and plantain, and pound them well until they are like meal, and add to them honey, and white of egg that has been cleaned, and wheaten flour, and then mix them all together thoroughly, working and blending them together, and know that it is not on the fire, but worked and blended cold until it is as thick as porridge, and spread on linen, and apply to the wound; it will kill the burning and bring the wound back to its natural state; this is the chief of all plasters for every pain.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 207

TO MAKE A GOOD POULTICE TO DRAW BLOOD OR A WOUND FROM A SORE.

§ 552. Take old bacon, and melt it in a pan, and let it stand until the salt has gone to the bottom, and take virgin wax as much as the melted fat, and frankincense in powder, and let them melt together, and mix well, and when the heat has gone from it, take powdered mastic in moderate quantity with the frankincense, and put on the fire, and mix well, and when cool add as much powdered sulphur as of the frankincense and the mastic, and work it well and diligently, until the whole is like honey, and put in a box for when it is needed.

AGAINST YELLOWING OF THE TEETH AND BAD BREATH.

§ 553. Take the leaves of the geidwad and pound them fine, and take twice as much salt and mix with it, and make into balls, and dry it until it burns, and then powder it, and rub your teeth frequently with it, and this will make the teeth clean and white and without bad odour.

AGAINST CANKER.

§ 554. Take unslaked lime, and pepper, and horse-mint, and strong ox-gall, and honey, and barley flour, equal quantities of each, and boil well in an earthen vessel, and make into a powder, and apply to the canker and it will destroy it.

ANOTHER.

§ 555. Take unslaked lime and powder it, and calcine quicksilver to a quarter of the lime, and add as much honey as will make it into a dough, and put in an earthen vessel in an oven, at bread-heat, and bake to the degree of baking bread, and when cool store in a tightly sealed glass vessel, and take as much as is needed and powder it, and cast it on the canker and it will destroy it entirely, then

208 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

apply a cleansing plaster to the sore, and when it is quite clean, apply a growth ointment to it, and the patient will be healed.

FOR WATER-BLISTER WHERE WATER FORMS BETWEEN FLESH AND SKIN.

§ 556. Get the parings of sheepskin, and boil these in tallow until thick, and apply on a linen cloth.

TO BREAK A WOUND AS OFTEN AS NEEDED, OR TO OPEN IT AGAIN.

§ 557. Get equal parts of black soap, honey, and wheat bran, mix them together and apply. If you wish to break the wound quickly, use more of the soap, and it is good.

FOR ST. ANTHONY'S FIRE, BEING THE DISEASE FROM WHICH A MAN WHO CONTRACTS IT WILL DIE.

§ 558. Get warm pigeon dung and rye flour, a pound of each, and pound them together, then add half a pound of sour wine, and mix thoroughly, and apply cold to the wound, and place cabbage leaves over it to hold it together, and bind a linen cloth tightly around the sore, and leave it there for three days without moving it, and at the longest he will be healed within the plaster.

FOR THE GREAT GOUT, BEING SOFTENING OF THE JOINTS.

§ 559. Get the sorel of the wood, and the herb called Grace of God, called in some places the yrddon or orddon, and the tryw, and the tanclys, and the herbs of the sickle, and the yellow ddilwydd, and the fabcoll called by some fanwylyd, and ivy leaves, and the maeseifiau, equal amounts of each, pound them well together, and strain, and drink the juice as a drink, and it is good.

TO MAKE AN OINTMENT AGAINST THE GREAT GOUT.

§ 560. Get the fat of a small pig called in some places byrhwch, and horse fat, and boar fat, and the herb called the tormwyth or white wormwood, and in Latin ffebriffuga,

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 209

having been well pounded, and mixed together with melted fat until boiling, and after boiling until the virtue of the herbs is obtained, then strain and put the ointment to keep in a closed glass vessel, and anoint the pain in the warmth of the fire.

ANOTHER.

§ 561. Get the boiling-stone, and the herbs of the body, and the keeper, and as much sugar as a fist, and put them in a glass vessel up to its half, and fill up the rest with salt until the vessel is full, and know that it is necessary to pound the herbs fine through old ale, and to set the vessel ready in the sun for a week or in the gentle warmth of a fire, and you will get an oil from it; keep it carefully, and with it anoint the pain; then get wheat bran, and white wine, and boar's lard, and boil together and make a plaster, and apply it as hot as you can bear it upon the swelling, and this will drive it away.

ANOTHER.

§ 562. Take black snails and melt them all before the fire in an earthen vessel, and keep the melted matter in a clean vessel, and with that anoint the pain; it is good for gout both hot and cold.

ANOTHER.

§ 563. Take pitch, and virgin wax, and frankincense, and mutton tallow, and boar's lard, and fry them well together, and strain, and put to keep in a box, and with that anoint the pain.

A GOOD OINTMENT FOR CORNS AND WOUNDS.

§ 564. Take melted lard from pork and let the salt sink to the bottom, and then take the fat, and virgin wax, and pitch, and frankincense, and make an ointment of them, and apply it wherever there is need.

2 E

210 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AN OINTMENT FOR HEADACHE.

§ 565. Take the juice of the elder of Mary, called by some the blood of men, and honey, and salt, and wax, and frankincense, and boil them together, and anoint your head or temples therewith.

FOR THE GREAT PAIN IN THE STOMACH.

§ 566. Take a handful of tansy and pound it moderately fine, then put upon it a quart of dry wine, and let it stand overnight under a good cover in a vessel of oak wood, then put it in an earthen vessel without rust and apply boiling lees to it, then strain and drink it in three draughts during the night upon going to bed, and put on good coverings so that you sweat; take the second draught on the second night and the same thing on the third, and you will be well. It is good to accustom oneself to sleep in sheets of flannel or half-woollen cloth.

ANOTHER.

§ 567. Get handfuls of tansy and one of mallow, and one of horehound, and half as much of smooth groundsel and of rosemary, and boil well in a cauldron, and add to the water a pound weight of salt, and make a bath in a vessel large enough to immerse yourself completely, and go into it up to your neck, and wrap woollen sheets around you to sustain your full sweat, remaining therein for about two or three hours, keeping the vessel supplied with warm liquid to maintain the heat, and drink three good spoonfuls every half hour of good old mead with a little fennel seed bruised into it, and after the time aforesaid let the bath cool, and when it reaches the warmth of fresh milk newly drawn or from under the cow, come out and go to your bed and wrap yourself well in flannel and take a spoonful at the top of every hour of the blessed whey for six hours, and keep yourself for some days from catching cold, and you will be well.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 211

FOR PAIN IN THE JOINTS FROM COLD, OR FROM SPRAINING, OR FROM A STRAIN.

§ 568. Take sea-wrack and boil it in sea-water, and anoint the pain with it as hot as you can bear it, then apply the boiled wrack in the manner of a plaster, having been well pounded and tempered so that it is easy to bear, and this is good medicine for all pain and swelling from a fall or a blow.

FOR THE WHOOPING COUGH.

§ 569. Take hog's wort, and pounded garlic with a little honey, and boil well, and rub the feet of the patient with it, then wrap the feet and put plenty of bedclothes over the patient in bed, and take care to throw off the covers while sweating, and he will truly and certainly be healed.

FOR CANCER.

§ 570. Apply the juice of red onions to the sore, and make a plaster of the leaves of the lesser celandine together with its stalks, its flowers, and its seeds if they are pounded with honey, and vinegar, and a little aloe; it is proven.

FOR POCKS OF THE LUNGS.

§ 571. Take elder flowers, and when the flowers cannot be had, use the buds, or the leaves, or the inner green bark of the tree, and wood sorrel, and boil in goat's or cattle's whey, and drink this as your only drink for nine weeks; and so that you are not without flowers, gather them in their season and dry them well in the sun and store them, and boil them in the whey when needed; and where wood sorrel cannot be had, boil a finely chopped apple with the flowers in the whey; and this is good for all pocks in the blood and the lymph.

212 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST RHEUMATISM.

§ 572. Take a pound weight of garlic and pound it well and put on it a quart of good mild wine, and where that is not available, good old ale or strong mead, and let it stand sealed with a lid, and then strain under pressure, and drink lukewarm, and if the pain be in a joint or limb, apply the garlic after pressing it into poultices, and place as warm as you can bear against the pain; it is proven.

AGAINST PAIN OF A CATARACT ON THE EYE.

§ 573. Take the juice of celandine and a little honey and mix well, and apply with a feather to your eye night and morning; it is proven.

AGAINST THE BLACK PLAGUE.

§ 574. Take anise seed and fennel seed and grind well, and take rue and pound it well, then put white or mild wine on it and let it stand six hours, but the first dose given to the patient should have the ingredients brought to a boil so as to be obtained quickly, then strain it clean and give to the patient as the only drink.

ANOTHER.

§ 575. Take the fresh yeast of new ale, and give the patient a good swallow once every three hours or every four-and-twenty hours, and then give him wheat bread toasted through fermentation in a slice of loaf before the fire with good warm wine poured on it, and let him eat and drink the wine in small portions at the end of the four hours; it is proven.

AGAINST BRUISING OF THE EYE.

§ 576. Take parsley and pound it well with virgin butter, and apply as a warm poultice to the eye, lukewarm.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 213

AGAINST SPECKS ON THE EYE.

§ 577. Take the juice of celandine, and the juice of fennel, and a little honey, and apply it to the eye morning, noon, and night, and cover the eye so that no light reaches it; it is proven.

AGAINST DIZZINESS.

§ 578. Take the roots of privet, and the leaves of the geidwad plant, a good weight, and boil well, and mash the roots first, let it boil until the water barely covers the herbs, then strain under pressure, and take a good drink of it morning and night, two hours before and two hours after food.

AGAINST SUNBURN ON THE SKIN.

§ 579. Take the leaves of pennywort ground fine and cream of milk, and boil together over a slow fire and grind into an ointment, and anoint the painful area.

A GOOD EYE OINTMENT.

§ 580. Get sour wine, white wine, and the juice of celandine, which some call sharp for the eye, and broad plantain juice, and put in a pan and mix together, and place a cover over the vessel, and let it stand three days and three nights, then put it in a box, and with it moisten your eyes.

A TREATMENT AGAINST CORNS AND BRUISED BLOOD.

§ 581. Take the fat of an old boar, and take one half of virgin wax, and frankincense, and mastic, and boil together, and when it is near to cooling, add as much powdered sulphur as there is frankincense, and work it into an ointment, and keep it in a box.

AGAINST A WOUND THAT IS OPEN AND WILL NOT CLOSE.

§ 582. Take oak gall, and verdigris, and grind them to a powder, and apply to the wound.

214 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR GOUT.

§ 583. Take broadleaf plantain, and sickle-wort, and wild tansy, and pound them well together with fresh lard, and let them putrefy for nine days, then boil well and strain through linen, and add to it wax, and frankincense, and * pure rose, melted together, and it is made.

AN OINTMENT FOR PAIN IN THE HEAD.

§ 584. Take the juice of the blessed elder, called the blood of men in some places, and fresh wax, and storax, and boil together, and anoint your spinal cord with it.

TO MAKE A GOOD OINTMENT.

§ 585. Take the juice of clary, and the juice of tansy, and morel, and the juice of broadleaf plantain, and the juice of pennyworth, of each an equal amount, and honey, and wheat bran, and boar's lard, and sheep's tallow, and wax, and boil them on the fire until thick, and strain it through linen, and it is good.

FOR DARK EYES.

§ 586. Take the juice of ground-ivy, and the juice of fennel root, and the juice of celandine, that is the swallow-herb, and sow's lard, and honey, and a little sour wine, and the blood of an eel, and the gall of a cock, and put in a vessel to flower, and anoint your eyes with it; this will cause people to recover their sight after losing it; it is proven.

FOR SORE EYES.

§ 587. Fill an eggshell with fennel juice, and ruddle, and clear honey, and wine, and the spittle of a young boy, and anoint your eyes with it.

* Rosin, most likely.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 215

EYE SALVE.

§ 588. Seek black slugs in the month of May, place them on embers to roast, and take the fat from them, keep it as long as you can, and anoint your eyes with it.

FOR A FILM ON THE EYE, OR PAIN.

§ 589. Take the yolk of an egg and wheat flour, and a little blue vitriol, and apply it when you go to sleep at night, and it will draw out the matter during the night; do this for three days and you will be healed.

FOR DEAFNESS.

§ 590. Take the bile of a sow, and goat's milk, and clear honey, and put it warm and lively into your ears; this is a medicine that will never fail.

FOR BAD FLESH THAT BREAKS, AND AFTER IT HAS BROKEN.

§ 591. Take a full handful of cleavers, and half a handful of waybroad, and an equal amount of red fennel, and boil them all in a quart of water, and another quart of honey, or two quarts of water will be best so that they may sufficiently simmer, and a pound weight of white aloe, and boil this long and well until it is reduced by a third, and put the herbs in whole, only breaking them between your hands, and place in a vessel to keep with the herbs therein, and that is a good water to anoint every cancer, and every bad flesh, and every ache, and every raw flesh, where there is a poisonous or cruel nature, and wash it with that water, and it will be healed through God.

FOR BAD FLESH AT ITS BEGINNING, IF YOU SEEK TO KILL AND DESTROY IT PROMPTLY.

§ 592. Take honey, and treacle, and aloe, and sulphur that is brimstone, and quicksilver, and powdered lead, and make into a plaster, and apply it frequently, and it will heal; and if it is not healed by

216 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

thereto add fat of honey and black soot, and you will be healed, truly, with God.

A DRINK TO MAKE A PERSON SLEEP.

§ 593. Obtain the juice of opium, and the juice of the mullein or its seeds, and milk, and make pills thereof, and give them to the patient, and let him swallow one, and if he does not sleep after one, give him another and then another until he sleeps, and wait two or three hours to see whether he sleeps or not before giving what was given to him.

AGAINST THE ERUPTION OF SCROFULA.

§ 594. Obtain lard, and black soap, and quicksilver, and pound them together, and make an ointment thereof, and anoint the wound, and you will be healed.

AGAINST LEPROSY OR THE GREAT RINGWORM.

§ 595. Take mushrooms, and what grows in the earth called toadstool, and the red leaves that grow on the alder, and clarified butter, and boil together in sheep's milk, and then strain through raw linen, and anoint frequently with this, and you will be healed with God.

AGAINST SCURF ON A PERSON OR A RASH ON THE SKIN.

§ 596. Take the root of the red dock and boil in sheep's milk for at least two hours, and take it off the fire, and add clarified butter to it, and strain through raw linen, and anoint the afflicted part with this, and it will be healed.

AGAINST ITCHING SCABS.

§ 597. Take the white of an egg strained firmly through linen, and the juice of red fennel, and the juice of celandine, and clear honey, and a boy's urine, and white wine in equal measure, and mix thoroughly, and with this anoint your body and your eyes if need be.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 217

AGAINST VARIOUS ERUPTIONS, CALLED THE LEPROSY.

§ 598. Seek the root of the red dock, and the root of the alexanders, and the leaves of the privet, and the rooks' leeks, and the tips of the broom, and the bark of the trees, and the mediciners, and Mary's fern, and the hazel, that is the leaves of the beloved plant, and pound them together with unsalted butter, and bring to a good boil, then draw from the fire and strain cleanly through raw linen, and add thereto about a measure of burnt lime-ash, and verdigris, and with that anoint frequently and the patient shall be healed, through God.

AGAINST ITCH-MITE, WHICH IS A PAIN RESEMBLING A WATERY ERUPTION, WITH EXCESSIVE ITCHING.

§ 599. Seek pure honey, and fox marrow, and storax, and mix them well by pounding them firmly in a mortar until they form an ointment, and with that anoint the pain.

AGAINST THE CORN.

§ 600. Seek the juice of the samphire, and the juice of the elecampane, and barley flour, and white of egg, and make a plaster of it and apply it.

ANOTHER.

§ 601. Seek garden bitters called in some places tormwyth, and the hard-head, and the grey herbs, and Mary's herbs, and the dwale, and the daisy, wash them well, pound them well with old ale, and give the patient a spoonful at once, and if taken in time it will protect him. This is a drink.

AGAINST SHOOTING PAIN.

§ 602. Drink the juice of the tansy in old ale, which is good, pounded well together, and strained.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE THROAT WHERE THERE IS AN ERUPTION OR A CORN IN THE GULLET, WITH SOFTNESS ACCOMPANYING IT.

§ 603. Take the leaves of the plantain, and rue, and boil in water, and after it has boiled a little draw from the fire and

218 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

Add sour wine to it, with honey as it pleases, and with that, lukewarm, wash your mouth and throat, spitting the wash out and taking care not to swallow it; and after washing well, drink a good draught of the liquid.
