Do this three or four times in the day, and as many times at night. Take the slugs, and the leaves of the clown's woundwort, and rue, equal parts of each, and pound them well, and add a little sheep's milk, or whatever milk is available, enough to make a poultice, and apply it warm around the neck, changing it as it dries; and keep in your mouth as it dissolves a piece the size of a hazelnut, twice over, of old refined hard honey. Do this for three days and you will be healed, by God.

ANOTHER.

§ 604. Take the leaves of the clown's woundwort, and red ochre, and the berries or flowers of the elder tree, and where the bark is nearest the wood, and the slugs, and the tormentil, and place them in a mortar, with a little honey and a little white wine or sour wine over them, and pound them well, and of the pounded mixture make a plaster on a cloth and apply it warm around the neck; then strain the remainder, and drink two spoonfuls of the juice every two hours, and another spoonful before each drink; wash your throat and mouth and spit out the wash after working it around your mouth and throat, and do not let it be swallowed, for the poison of the ailment will be in it. And in place of the plaster, you may anoint your neck with the juice at each drink, and keep a cloth around the neck. Do this for three days and you will be healed, by God.

ANOTHER.

§ 605. Boil the red ochre in white wine and strain it, and drink four spoonfuls at the head of every three hours, and wash the neck under a cloth with each drink, and before each drink wash your mouth and throat with the boiling and sour wine, half and half, and then spit out the wash, and you will be healed, by God.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 219

ANOTHER.

§ 606. Take a large apple and pull out its eye, then draw out its core and some of the flesh, then take red lead and grind it very fine and place it inside the apple, and put back the eye that you pulled out tightly, then roast the apple before the fire, and when it is well done, take it and pound it together with a little honey and a spoonful of white wine, and mix them into a smooth compound, and of that take a spoonful every two hours until well, and before taking it, wash the mouth and throat with red watercress and vinegar half and half.

HERE IS A GOOD GARGLE.

§ 607. Take the leaves of the plantain, and red lead, and the mallow, and the flowers of the elder whether green or dry, and boil them well in water, and after boiling a while, add vinegar and honey, a spoonful and a spoonful to the boiling, and let them cool from the boil, and strain cleanly through a fine cloth and keep it, and when needed warm it from two to four spoonfuls, and take it in your mouth, and then work it back and forth along your throat as far as you can while avoiding swallowing it, then spit it out, do this two to four times, a spoonful each time, and it is good for all pain of the mouth and throat, and use it in all dangerous times when plague is abroad, and this will cure it with God's help, and after washing the mouth, if plague is present drink a spoonful of the liquid and it will protect you with God's help.

FOR THE FESTERING SORE ON A CHILD.

§ 608. Boil a handful of pimpernel leaves in cow's milk, and give a spoonful every hour to the little one for three days, and it will heal with God's help.

TO KILL DEAD FLESH IN A BRUISE OR WOUND.

§ 609. Get old tallow, and old goose dung, and rye bread crust and egg shells, and salt, as much of each as

220 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

together, and put them all in a pot and burn them to a powder, and grind that powder fine and apply it.

ANOTHER.

§ 610. Take a pound weight of burnt lime, and an equal amount of the plant called aurbibau, and put them in a vessel to boil with a large measure of water for a good while, then take it off and let it dry somewhere that no moisture can reach it, and when it is fully dry, make it into a powder, and apply that to the dead flesh, for it will kill it; it is also good for killing cancer — apply it to rest on the sore for an hour and up to three hours, then wash it with warm sheep's milk, or where that is not available, cow's or goat's milk. Do this once every day until the cancer is seen to be killed. Then apply a growth ointment to it, and all the while let the patient drink bramble shoots and agrimony as their only drink, and their only food boiled in milk — best of all goat's milk — and twice a week the meat of a fully grown rabbit.

FOR A BITE.

§ 611. Get a nettle, root and all, wash the root, beat the nettle well, then boil it with clarified butter, make it into an ointment, and apply it to the bite, and it will heal.

A MEDICINE FOR BITES.

§ 612. Get pig's lard and melt it, with honey, wine, and rye flour, boil them together, and apply on a woollen cloth to the bite; it will cleanse the bite and heal it. If it closes over too much, get the herb called wild nep, make it into a plaster and apply it, and it will open it up.

There are various kinds of liver conditions, namely hot and cold; the hot is the more dangerous of the two, and wide nostrils accompany it, while the cold has moderate nostrils, and because of this different medicines are required for them,

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 221

because the hot condition requires treatment with cold things, and the cold complaint with hot things. This is how the cold complaint is healed, this pain which is called lancole; Get the white of an egg and rye flour, make a dough and apply it to it, and leave it until it works of itself, and do thus until it be healed.

A MEDICINE FOR FLESH THAT HAS ROTTED, AND FOR FESTERING HOLES AND THEIR SURROUNDINGS.

§ 613. Get canrig and clear honey, and make a dough, and form it into a cake, and apply to the holes, and when it is needful apply another, and thus let this be healed and well.

A GENERAL MEDICINE AGAINST ALL KINDS OF SWELLING.

§ 614. Get scurf and a wound finely ground, and wash in a liquid made from wheat ale, and boil it well and apply it to the sore night-time and half a day-time, and then draw it off, and wash the sore with the stalk of a man, and then apply to it a powder made as follows: get goose quills and pull away the rough parts, and burn them, and make into powder, and apply that to the sore, and apply thereon fat of a wildcat or fat of a boar, afterwards apply a cabbage leaf upon it, and take old good ale made from wheat without barley, and fill a new vessel with the ale, and add salt to it, and arsenic and figs of each the same amount, and of wax more than one of them, and boil them together until they be thick, and then draw to the floor, and let it cool, and make a plaster and apply thereto, first the powder mentioned above, and a plaster of the fat upon it, and a cabbage leaf over that, and change morning and night, and give the sap or juice of hazel to the patient to drink, for on the day that they absorb it the pain will be no greater nor wider than before.

ANOTHER

§ 615. Get the juice of hazel, and the juice of blessed mallow and linseed, bruise them all together, and apply with honey and cow's milk

222 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

of the same colour, and put them in a new pot and boil them well, and apply them as warm as can be borne to the pain.

ANOTHER.

§ 616. Powder of pepper, boiled in sour wine until the sour wine is fully consumed, then aloe powder, and storax, and verdigris, and honey, mix all well together in a mortar, and apply on a cloth as a plaster to the pain.

A MEDICINE AGAINST BONE-ACHE.

§ 617. Put the seed of purslane in a pot, and place it under the embers to roast well, and press through a linen cloth well and cleanly, and this will produce a gum, and with that anoint the pain; and if the seed is not available, take the herb root and all, and place it to roast and press as above.

ANOTHER.

§ 618. Get oil of roses and anoint with it, and make a decoction of wild garlic and hyssop in wine, or the juice of herbs in wine, and give to the patient as his sole drink until he is well.

ANOTHER.

§ 619. Get white leeks and place them on the fire to toast well, and after that make a powder, and anoint the pain with clear honey, then apply this powder to it, and leave it there until it falls off of its own accord, then do as before until it is healed.

AGAINST BONE-ACHE AND SWELLING.

§ 620. Get the roots of fern and pound them well, and mix with a little warm water well, and after that press through a linen cloth and make a plaster of it with barley meal, and break the white of an egg over it as it is made into a plaster, and heat and spread on a cloth and apply to it.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 223

A REMEDY AGAINST PAIN, TO DETERMINE WHERE THE WOUND IS, WHETHER THE FLESH IS FROM ONE RIB TO ANOTHER, OR ROTTING OTHERWISE.

§ 621. First, anoint the pain with honey on every side of it, then get fresh cheese and rye flour, and place that in the earth overnight, and then upon the holes where you think the worm to be, and bind it there, and the next day when you remove it, if there are holes in the cheese, know that the worm is there.

ANOTHER.

§ 622. Take and apply a black slug, and if you see the slug has been eaten the next day when you remove it, the worm will be there.

THE FORM AND MANNER BY WHICH THE WORM IS KILLED.

§ 623. Get the root of the black iris and bruise it in wine and honey, and take a slug, and place it near the pain where the wound above is, or bad flesh, and apply these to affect it, and it will kill the worm.

ANOTHER.

§ 624. Get pepper and husk, and linseed, and wormwood, and dry these three together, and make a poultice, and apply it, and it will kill it.

A REMEDY AGAINST BITES OR MOIST PAINFUL WOUNDS THAT ARE FESTERING, OR CANCER.

§ 625. Get ointment and make into a poultice, and anoint with that.

ANOTHER.

§ 626. Get old lard, and quicksilver, and frankincense, and mastic, and a little pepper, and bruise each one of them separately, and mix them with the lard when cold, and add the quicksilver with it, and it will kill very effectively, and with that anoint the pain by the fire.

224 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

ANOTHER.

§ 627. Take a small amount of the juice of the root of taf, a small amount of the juice of hazel, a small amount of the juice of field mint, a small amount of the juice of blessed thistle, a small amount of the juice of plantain, and place in a pan on the fire with lard, and make into an ointment, and anoint the sore with it wherever it may be, and it will heal.

Among all the afflictions that are especially dangerous to the sick — those that are feared concerning malignant flesh in wild cancer — it is by diligent medicine that they are remedied, namely,

AGAINST MALIGNANT FLESH OF EVERY KIND OF NATURE AND EVERY KIND OF TUMOUR ALSO.

§ 628. Take grains of corn, and hen's dung, and black beans, and garlic, and salt, and goat's dung, and horse bones, and pieces of blue rags, and place in an earthen pot and close it well and set on the fire and let these become ash, and cast that powder with as much pepper and powder of white glass and of garlic, and wash the sore with vinegar and dregs, or with sour dregs, at night and in the morning, and apply the powder to it, and it will heal.

Also take goat's dung and butter and mix, and apply the powder first.

Also take turpentine and new wax, and apply the powder first to it, and over that the new wax, and when its poison and inflammation subsides apply to it a plaster of the juice of plantain, and honey, and white of egg, and rye flour, and in the morning drink the expressed juice of hazel from the wren. Avoid cheese, and nuts, and women, and it will heal.

FOR THE SAME THING.

§ 629. Take woad and burn it in an earthen pot until it becomes ash, and grind it finely and cast this powder on it and in the

* The meaning of "as" is a little bit.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 225

where the dead flesh is, take orpine and wall-pellitory, pound them well with a little honey and butter, make into a plaster and apply it, for it will kill the dead flesh and make it healthy.

Also cast upon it the pollen of the leek, and it will bind it and make it healthy.

FOR THE SAME KIND OF THING.

630. Get sanders and aloe, and copperas, and myrrh, and verdigris, and grind to a fine powder and cast it on, and leave it there two or three days, and then apply thereon wormwood well pounded as finely as you can, and mix with pure honey, and apply a full covering so that nothing is bare, and clean it well twice daily, and the swelling will heal.

If you cannot obtain the above herbs, get a sieve-full of ash from hollyhocks, and sour whey, and mix them well and apply to kill the pustule, and make it healthy with wormwood and honey as aforesaid.

FOR CANCER.

§ 631. Take copperas, and pepper, and grind them together, and temper them with white of egg and honey after washing the sore over the fire; anoint the sore firmly where the cancer is.

FOR CANCER.

§ 632. Make a poultice of white aloe and apply it.

FOR BAD BREATH.

§ 633. Take the juice of garlic, and the juice of wormwood, and the juice of angelica, and the juice of ribwort, mix with honey and give a spoonful in the morning fasting, and one at going to bed, and the patient will be healed.

226 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

FOR A PERSON WHO LOSES HIS SENSES OR HIS SPEECH IN HIS ILLNESS.

§ 634. Seek the lesser centaury gathered on White Sunday or on the eve of the feast of John the Baptist, boil these, dry them and make into a powder, and give in drink to the patient to drink, and it is good.

FOR PAIN IN A LEG THAT HAS BECOME PUTRID.

§ 635. Boil the leaves of the oak in white or red wine, and apply the wine and the leaves to it, and it is good.

ANOTHER.

§ 636. Take the ointment of the old elm, and white wine, and mix well, and anoint the pain, and it will draw away the infection, and will heal it.

FOR A WOMAN WHO FAILS IN LABOUR.

§ 637. Seek the juice of the mugwort, and give it to her with water.

TO STOP BLOOD FROM A WOUND OR BITE, OR FROM ANY OTHER CAUSE OR INJURY OF ANY KIND.

§ 638. Take a handful, and pound well, and pour sour wine over them, and apply to the wound, to prevent the person from fainting, and if he does faint, take sour wine and anoint his temples with it, and give him drink.

FOR A WOMAN'S BLEEDING.

§ 639. Take walnut shells and grind them to a powder, then make a decoction with the bark nearest the wood of the blackthorn, add a little honey, and cast the powder into the liquid, and let her drink only that drink for a month, and do likewise for another month if need be.

FOR A PAINFUL MOUTH.

§ 640. Take a spoonful of the juice of the houseleek, and a spoonful of rue juice, and a spoonful of white wine or sour wine, and a spoonful of honey, and mix; then let the patient wash his mouth first with

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 227

water and salt, then let him take the liquid shown in his mouth at the time and work it well with his tongue and breath, but let him not swallow it, and spit it out, and take another spoonful and swallow it, and it will heal him, and do this again and again until he is well, and this is a good remedy to guard against dangerous ailments.

TO GUARD AGAINST DANGEROUS AILMENTS.

§ 641. In time of dangerous ailments take the juice of rue and white wine or old strong mead, half and half, and drink a spoonful or two in the morning, at midday, and at night going to bed, at least an hour before or after food.

ANOTHER.

§ 642. Take a handful of rue, and four heads of garlic, and a handful of the herb geidwad, and pound them together with good wine or mead, then strain clean and drink four spoonfuls every morning on an empty stomach for as long as the plague lasts.

A GOOD PURGE FOR THE BODY.

§ 643. Take a spoonful of the juice of the celandine, and frankincense pounded over it, and it is good for the chest and the stomach.

ANOTHER.

§ 644. Seek the juice of houseleek, a spoonful, and boil it in a quart of red wine and let it boil down to the half, then give it to the patient to drink, warm at night and cold in the morning.

A PRECIOUS OINTMENT AGAINST EVERY KIND OF DISEASE.

§ 723. Take sheep's suet, and buck's suet, and old lard, and wax, and bitter water-cress, and the hazel, and the chwerwyn, and the samwl, or in their place the priellau, and grind them and boil them together and press through a cloth, and keep it, and it is truly good.

HERE IS AN OINTMENT THAT HIPPOCRATES MADE AGAINST THE PALSY, THAT IS THE PARALYSIS, AND AGAINST EVERY KIND OF COLD PAIN.

§ 724. Get a fat capon, and draw the fat from it, and an equal amount of fat from a male cat, and an equal amount of fat from a †barren cat, and fox fat, and a portion of pepper, and hen's fat, and storax, and two heads of onion, and 6 pounds of new wax, and water-cress, and the hazel, and hyssop, and priellau, and the bitter elder, and grind them all together, and place them inside the capon, and roast before the fire until nothing drips from it, and take them out of the capon, and boil a second time in butter, and resin, and melt

store albanum with them, and strain through a cloth and keep well and carefully, and with that anoint well by the fire for every kind of cold pain.

AN OINTMENT TO HEAL BITES.

725. Take old lard, and frankincense, and wax, and put on the fire to boil, and press it through a cloth, and when it is cold spread it and smear it on a cloth, and change it twice in the day, and warm it and apply it again, and every time work the smearing along the full length and breadth of it.

ANOTHER.

§ 726. Take what is a handful, and what is the root of Cadwgan's herb or the pylor, and what is the blood of men, that is the blessed elder, and clear honey, and white of egg, and wine, each one of them equal in amount to the others, and add thereto a handful of wheat, and make into a plaster and spread on a cloth and apply to the bite morning and evening until it is healed.

AGAINST PIMPLES.

§ 727. Take the erllyriad, and eyebright, and leaves of elder, and the tryw, and the edafeddog, and the bengaled, and the strawberry, and the orpine which is the fywydog, with unsalted butter, and press through a clean cloth and keep it, and anoint the sore with it, and make a drink for the patient with leaves of strawberry, and the orpine, and the blessed oak by steeping in wine or ale, or by boiling in water, and give it to the patient as his only drink, and that is truly good.

HERE ARE THE HERBS FOR A GROWTH OINTMENT, NO LESS.

§ 728. The wrnerth, the violet, the glesyn, the llwynhidydd, the bittain, the diwythl fedi, hyssop, equal amounts of each, mortar them together, and add butter to them and clarify it beneath and above first before adding the herbs, and boil the herbs

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 247

with the butter, boil lamb or bleak fish, blend it with the membrane, strain it through raw linen, and put it away for keeping.

ANOTHER.

§ 729. Get twopennyworth of rosin, a phialful of sheep's tallow, and as much again of new wax; melt them together, then draw off the heat and strain it; divide the melted substance into two parts, and colour one part with three halfpennies' worth of verdigris, letting the colour of the herbs remain on the other half.

HERE IS HOW TO MAKE A YELLOW SALVE.

§ 730. A cupful of rosin, and as much again of tallow, and half that amount of wax, and purified butter half a cup full; boil and strain through linen, and colour one half with copper rust or verdigris, and to the other half add a little honey, let it boil, and keep it yellow.

TO MAKE YELLOW TREACLE.

§ 731. Take new wax, and yellow rosin, and purified butter, and mutton tallow in greater measure than the wax, and the rosin more than the butter and the tallow; boil together for a time, then draw off the heat and strain through linen.

TO MAKE A GROWTH SALVE, AND THAT ONE GREEN.

§ 732. Take wax, and rosin, and purified butter, and herb robert, and the violets — namely the violet, and the woad, and the woodbine; melt the solids and the herbs, pound them well and boil upon the melted matter, leave them a short while on the fire, then draw them off the heat and strain through clean linen and let cool, then put away for keeping.

TO KILL CANCER.

§ 733. Take mastic, and camphor, and frankincense, in equal measure, and dragon's blood, and grind them in a clean vessel, and put away within

248 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

a clean bladder, and when you go to treat, seek a full measure of tinder, that is the fungus from under oak wood, and take a silver spoonful of the powder and throw it in the fire and put the canker over the smoke, and that will kill it, but follow it up well.

TO MAKE A ROLTON OR ROLTON.

§ 734. Take six spoonfuls of the oil of the olive, and twice as much of red lead, and grind the lead into the oil and put it in a brass pan on the fire, and take a stick and mix well, and take a pewter dish in your hand, and strike the stick on the dish whenever you see it turn black, then draw it from the fire, and let it stand until it begins to cool, then roll it into rolls, and put it in paper before it is fully cool, and let it cool enough, then put it away.

TO MAKE A DRAWING PLASTER.

§ 735. Take wax, and rosin, and tar, and pig's lard, and put on the fire, equal amounts of wax and rosin, and the rest in proportion of 6, and let this boil until it is like hard wax.

TO MAKE A PLASTER AGAINST GOUT, OR SWELLING, OR A THORN PRICK.

§ 736. Take the water-cress and butter, and pound together and warm on the fire for a short while, and apply to the wound three or four times.

TO MAKE A DRY PLASTER.

§ 737. Seek the root of the alexanders and bruise it and boil it well, and pour over it the milk of a one-coloured cow, and mix well, and remove the roots, and add wheat flour or barley flour to it, and honey, and a little rosin, and boil this until thick, and draw from the fire, and put in a clean vessel, and when you apply it to a wound put some lard on top of it, lest it be too dry.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 249

TO MAKE A POWDER OF EGG WHITES.

§ 738. Take a broad flat stone and place it on the fire, and put the whites of eggs upon it until they turn black, then gather them up and keep them carefully.

AGAINST THE DISEASE THAT SPREADS LIKE WILDFIRE, WHICH IS BAD FLESH OR FLESH TURNING INTO CANCER IN THE EYE, AND IT SOMETIMES DESCENDS TO SETTLE IN THE THROATS OF MEN, AND THE LIPS, AND THE PALATE OF THE MOUTH, AND BENEATH THE ROOTS OF THE TONGUE, AND CANKER THERE AND INFLAMMATION, AND THUS IT IS TO BE CURED.

§ 739. Take a vial of sour wine, and a vial of the juice of the perllys herb, and half a vialful of honey, and a portion of treacle, and mix them well together with a powder of aloe, working it so that it be of a thickness like that of fine flour paste; apply this to the affected area, and this is proven, and the best of all medicines, provided it be done properly, this shall bring health.

AN OINTMENT FOR A BITE.

§ 740. Take the hazel, and the violet, and the eyebright, and the woodbine, and the privet, and the plantain, and pound them well, and boil them well together with clarified butter and strain, and keep it, and it is truly good indeed.

AN OINTMENT AGAINST SPOTS.

§ 741. Take leaves of bay, and the violet, and the eyebright, and the hardhead, and the wilfrai herb, and the powder of the glyf herb, and the marrow of an old ox, and mix them together, and boil, and strain.

AN OINTMENT FOR A SWELLING WHERE THE SKIN IS TIGHT.

§ 742. Take clarified butter and place it on the fire, and skim well what rises to its surface while boiling, and take the wrnerth, and the woodbine of equal amounts of each, and if you cannot get the woodbine use the wilffrei, and boil them well in the butter, and if you wish to add a little reed it will be none the worse for

250 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

ointment, and place on the fire, adding a quantity of the above herbs so that the ointment is of a proper consistency, and let it boil as long as it takes to cook a leg of lamb, then add a little new wax and mix well and let it boil a little, and when it is coming down, throw in a spoonful of purified honey and mix all together well, and let one shiver pass through it, and draw it from the fire and stir well, and strain cleanly through coarse linen, and put away. If you wish to make something to burn away dead flesh, obtain alum or blue vitriol and bruise a little of it and place on the surface of the ointment in a wide box or dish, mix well and let it set, and that is good against dead flesh; for it will burn it away.

HERE IS HOW TO MAKE THE YELLOW OINTMENT.

§ 743. Get a bottle of rosin, and as much sheep's tallow, and the same quantity of wax, and half a cup's worth of purified butter, boil them together, then draw from the fire and strain through linen. Colour half of that ointment with green rust, and mix a little honey into the other half and boil it a little more, and that keeps it yellow; store it well in a clean vessel for your use.

A WASH TO GROW SKIN OVER A BARE SHIN OR OTHER PLACES WHERE IT IS NECESSARY TO BURN AWAY THE DEAD FLESH.

§ 744. Get plaintain, daisy, and tutsan, and a gallon of cold spring water, and pound the herbs and add them to the water and boil it, and add a pound weight of alum and boil it down until it is reduced to a third, and that wash is ready.

AN OINTMENT OR WASH AGAINST BURNING OR RED INFLAMMATION CAUSED BY SCALDING, OR THE HEAT OF FIRE, OR SUN, OR A BRUISE, OR THE GRIP OF HOT FOOD ON THE PLACE.

§ 745. Take milk and water half and half, and take the mallow, and the flowers, or the seeds, or the green bark of the

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 251

elder, and pennywort, and wherever they may be found, wood sorrel, or meadow sorrel, or French sorrel, which is the garden variety, and boil in water and milk, and anoint the pain with it while lukewarm, and after that take the boiled herbs as many as are needed of them and apply as a poultice to the pain, and keep a portion moving within six hours.

AGAINST ERYSIPELAS (THE JEWISH FIRE).

§ 746. Get * fwg, and the figwort, and house-leek, and the herb called pricc maed, and Jew's ears which grow on the elder, a glove-full of each, or of those that can be obtained, and pound well, and boil in fresh butter, and press through linen, and anoint the pain with this ointment, and it will extinguish and destroy it, and heal it forthwith; apply it in the morning frequently.

IF THERE BE MATTER (PUS) IN A PERSON.

§ 747. Get sheep's fat, and oatmeal, and † figwort leaves, and the dew-cup, and boil these together into a mash, and apply it to the affected part, and it will draw out the matter.

AGAINST WEAK RUNNING EYES.

§ 748. Take a glazed earthen vessel and melt tin-ash in it to the depth and breadth of the base, two or three thumbnail-thicknesses, and when you go to bed at night make your water in that vessel, and in the morning wash your eyes with it; then throw the water away and make your water in the morning in the cup and let it stand until night and wash your eyes with it when going to bed, for the morning water is best, as it is stronger than the night water prepared in this way from morning to morning; and if the hearing is heavy, wet black wool in that water and place it in your ears at night when going to bed.

252 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

AGAINST THE COLIC.

§ 749. Take the grey groundsel, and the agrimony, and a handful of red ones, and boil through goat's whey, and strain through a cloth, and give to the patient to drink.

AGAINST A BRUISE FROM A BLOW.

§ 750. Take the celandine, and the agrimony, and fennel, of each an equal amount, and pound them together with rye flour, and honey, and the white of eggs, and apply as a plaster thereto, and he will be healed.

AGAINST ITCHING AND FILM ON THE EYES.

§ 751. Take the juice of the celandine, by boiling the herbs well in the milk of a woman who is nursing a male child, or in the milk of a cow that has had a male calf, and strain through a press, and apply the juice with a feather to your eyes.

ANOTHER.

§ 752. Boil the celandine in goat's milk and strain through a press, and mix with a little honey, and apply to your eyes with a feather, three times a day.

AGAINST JAUNDICE.

§ 753. Take dandelion, and white scabious, and garden parsley, and pound them well together, then boil them in good strong old ale, and put them in a linen pouch to keep tightly closed, and take first thing in the morning an hour before food, and last thing at night an hour after a full meal, four cupfuls or half a quart of it.

ANOTHER.

§ 754. Take the twigs, and leaves if there be any, of the yellow tree, that is the spindle tree, and bruise and boil well in good strong old ale until a third is reduced, and drink as your sole drink.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 253

AGAINST CORRUPTION OF THE LYMPH NODES.

755. Take the root or seed of nettle, and pound it well, then boil it in good cider of half a year to a year old, and drink it as your sole drink; the best cider is that made from keeping apples that are somewhat sour.

ANOTHER.

§ 756. Take apples, and boil them all, or stew them, and add to them the milk of cows or goats, and take this as your sole food and drink from one month to nine weeks according to the severity of the disease; this nourishment is very good against pustules of the lungs and pustules of the blood, and it destroys the poison of the lymph nodes. With this remedy Hywel the Physician of Llangynwyd cured King Edward the Confessor when no physician in Christendom would promise him an hour of life, such was the violence of the eruption of the lungs; and the Emperor Antoninus used it for every outbreak and every attack of disease, and it relieved all corruption of the blood and lymph nodes, which is the prevailing cause of every boil and abscess in the human body.

AGAINST NOSEBLEEDS.

§ 757. Take henbane and pound it very finely, and place it in your nostrils.

TO KILL INSECTS.

758. Take yarrow and pound it well, and apply it to the affected part.

AGAINST PAIN IN THE EYES.

§ 759. Apply egg yolk and wheat flour to each of the temples, and you will be healed.

AGAINST THE PILES.

§ 760. Take lime and the root of fern and grind them together and apply it, and you will be healed.

254 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

ANOTHER.

§ 761. Boil the root of the fern in spring water until it is reduced by half, and cast upon it a lump of freshly burned lime, and when the clear portion settles, pour it off into another vessel and wash the sore with it.

TO KNOW WHETHER A SICK PERSON WILL LIVE OR DIE.

§ 762. Bruise the violet and place it on his temples; if he sleeps he will live, if he does not sleep he will die.

TO BE RID OF WARTS.

§ 763. Pound the bark of the willow with weak ale or sour wine, and apply it to them.

AGAINST HEAT AND PAIN IN WOUNDS.

§ 764. Take the root of the blessed mallow, and the inner bark of the elder, equal parts of each, and add to them an equal measure of white wine, and boil well until it thickens, then take a linen cloth and bind it as tightly as you can, and place the plaster on it upon the wound; if the wound is large and will not close, take the herb called ground ivy and make it into a plaster and apply it, and it will open it.
Whoever drinks the juice of the violet will expel broken bones, should they be lodged in a person's limb.

AGAINST GOING ABROAD.

§ 765. Take the yolks of seven eggs, and as much again of pure honey, and the crumb of white bread crumbled very fine, and obtain a pennyworth of ground pepper, and boil them together, and eat it warm, and drink nothing after it for as long as you possibly can, and follow this diet for your health, and this is one of the best remedies for good health.

Various daily unhealthy diseases arising from around the heart of a man in oppression and suffocation, and stuffiness

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 255

the heart, and through great diligence and skill of art, and fruitful medicine, are they cured and no otherwise.

AGAINST DISEASE OF THE HEART OF MAN.

§ 766. Take red century and boil it in good old ale, and after that pound the herbs and boil again through the same liquor, then strain through a clean linen cloth, and add thereto a spoonful of refined honey, and then boil again, and put in a closed box, and give the patient three spoonfuls daily fasting, and this will drive the oppression from the heart, and will give him appetite for food and drink, truly by God.

AGAINST SUFFOCATION ABOUT THE HEART.

§ 767. Take the juice of fennel and honey, and boil together until they become hard, and eat that first thing in the morning and last at night an hour before and after food, and you will be well, by God.

TO MAKE A MOUTH WASH.

§ 768. Take rosemary, and sage, and hyssop, and honey, and aloe, and good ale, and put on the fire and boil until the quart becomes a pint, and draw it from the fire and put it warm in the mouth, and hold it there a good while, and do this every day for a week.

HERE IS THE MEDICINE OF RHIWALLON THE PHYSICIAN TO CAUSE RELIEF OF THE BELLY WHERE THERE IS COSTIVENESS OF THE BELLY.

§ 769. Take thin ale, and unsalted butter, and wheat bran, and boil well, then strain, and pour into a bladder, and put a pipe made from the stem of a goose's wing into the bladder, and tie the bladder around the pipe, and insert the pipe into the patient's bowel, and place him with his head low and his seat as high as possible, and drive the liquid into the patient's body, squeezing the bladder gradually.

256 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

TO CAUSE VOMITING, THAT IS, TO CAST OUT WHAT IS IN THE STOMACH.

§ 770. Take a handful of the vomiting herb, and boil it in good ale, strain it, and give it to the patient to drink.

AN OINTMENT TO HEAL PAIN AND DYSENTERY.

§ 771. Take the flesh of a fat old sow and melt it, let it stand until the salt settles to the bottom, then take an equal quantity of fresh wax, boil them together, and add powdered mastic and frankincense; when it has become thick like honey, keep it well covered under a dish on a piece of cloth or leather, apply it to the affected area, and it will draw out the pain and soreness; anoint with it twice daily and you will be healed.

AGAINST COLIC, THAT IS, THE GRIPES.

§ 772. Boil spring water well and pour running spring water over it, and take oatmeal groats and make a gruel of the two together, strain it cleanly, and drink it three mornings and three nights, first and last of all things taken, an hour before and after food.

TO CAUSE SLEEP.

§ 773. Take the lily, which bears the sign of the lion, and mix it with the juice of the tree called the laurel tree, and in Latin lawrus; place them for a time in dung with plenty of dung over them, and they will breed insects; take these insects, grind them to powder, and place that powder around the neck of the person, or in his clothing, and he will sleep until it is removed again a second time.

TO KNOW WHETHER A SICK MAN SHALL RECOVER, WHETHER HE BE ALIVE OR DEAD.

§ 774. Take the juice of liverwort and white wine, and give it to him to drink; if he vomits it, he will live, and if he does not vomit, he will die.

* Gwiscon, for gwyscon.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 257

ANOTHER FOR THE SAME KNOWLEDGE.

§ 775. Take the breast milk of a woman who has a suckling boy, and put a little of the milk on the palm of your hand, and take the patient's throat and place the milk on the tip of your finger into the throat: if the milk goes to the bottom of the throat, the patient will die; if it remains on the surface, the patient will live.

TO KNOW A PATIENT'S CONDITION.

§ 776. Bruise the violet, that is the pansy, and place it on his temples: if he sleeps he will live, if he does not sleep he will die.

ANOTHER SIGN.

§ 777. Take the herb and bruise it, and bind it around the medicine finger, and if he is alive he will sleep, and if he does not sleep, he will be dead; and learn this thing before you treat him in the world.

AGAINST THE SWELLING (GLANDULAR).

§ 778. Seek the root of the lily and wash it clean and bruise it fine, and boil in white wine until it is reduced by half, and strain clean through raw linen, and give it to the patient to drink, and it will restore the man to health.

AGAINST BOILS.

§ 779. Seek the herb of the elder, and boar's fat, and earthworms, and bruise them together, and apply to the sore.

BOILS.

§ 780. Take egg yolk and salt, and beat into a plaster, and apply it.

IF A PERSON IS SICK WITH THE SWELLING, AND BLACK SPOTS.

§ 781. Seek the sanicle, those that have black centers, and the fern, and rue, and if you wish add a leaf of the elder, and

258 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

wash it clean, and pound it through water like garlic, and give it in strong ale to the patient as warm as he can take it, and do thus with him by the fire on a bed with a linen cloth over and under him, and leave him there to sweat, and keep a good fire, and it will drive the eruption onto the linen, with God's help.

AGAINST THE STING OF A THORN.

§ 782. Get pig's lard and the root of red nettles, pound them well, and apply it nine times, and he will be healed, with God's help.

AGAINST FLUX AND RUNNING OF NATURE.

§ 783. Get powder of garden mint and powder of anise, and give them to the patient on his food or in a sauce, and this will stop the running, with God's help.

AGAINST THE COSDARDD, THAT IS, THE ITCHING ERUPTION.

§ 784. Take the root of marsh mallow, and boil it well, and boil likewise a measure of garlic in separate water, drink the full liquid of the marsh mallow nine mornings, and mix the two boiled waters together and wash your whole body every morning, and mix the boiled garlic and the boiled marsh mallow with butter without salt, and make an ointment, and anoint your whole body with it until the end of the nine days, every morning.

These are the virtues and various properties of herbs for the healing of man.

THE VIRTUE OF ALEXANDERS.

§ 785. It is good to boil them for the benefit of the sinews; if the boiling is drunk with good honey it is good for the stomach; and if a woman has a dead child with her, let her take alexanders and boil them with white wine and strain it clean and drink it cold, and she will be delivered safely of her burden. Also take this herb and pound it fine and apply it to a venomous bite, and it will draw out the poison; and also if one is full of wind, apply the herb to him and it will purge his interior, and let him take the herb

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 259

this, and pound it fine and press its juice into white wine, or leave it to steep in white wine or dark barm-brew or good old mead overnight, and drink it warm and strained on an empty stomach, and he will be well, by God. It is also very good for a healthy person to drink this drink half a mouthful on an empty stomach in the morning, to maintain health and prolong life and existence.

THE VIRTUE OF THE CAMOMILE.

§ 786. The camomile is a herb with a white flower upon it, and its virtue is this: if its juice be taken with honey and wine it will break the stone of fever, and likewise it will destroy the ague and the yellow disease, and will cure the ailment of the liver; and where there is no wine, take the juice in wholesome and strong mead, or in dark barley barm-brew; it is warming and drying.

HERE IS THE VIRTUE OF THE HENBANE.

§ 787. Take the juice of this herb in white wine, strain it clean, and let it cool, and drink it as a drink night and morning, and it will heal you of the yellow disease, and will enliven the blood by purging it of every ailment that is in it. If its juice be taken with dark barley barm-brew as a drink, half and half, it will relieve the hot stitch in the side and the armpit; and this also gives a man in advanced age agility and vigour of body and mind. If the seed of the henbane be taken in powder with honey, it is very good against flatulent wind, and against fever, and against a chronic cough, and to reduce swelling in the patient, and will cause water to be expelled from the body without injuring the bladder.

HERE IS THE VIRTUE OF ST. FFRAID'S COMB.

§ 788. Whoever is accustomed to drinking its juice will not be afflicted with fever, and if boiled in white wine and drunk as a drink, it will cure the nausea and swelling in the belly, and if pounded fine and the juice squeezed out and placed with a wing upon the eye

260 THE PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

man it brightens the sight and strengthens it, and clears the film from the eye. And the juice is good for pouring into ears that are going deaf; and it is good as a powder with honey for one who is developing a cough, for it breaks the cough and does good to many sick persons in the stomach. And it is good against the ague that comes, and if taken before the ague arrives, it will not come that year. And if boiled with leek seed it will heal a man's eye and brighten it, and strengthen the sight. A man learned in the art has said that if it were made into seed, the snake would sooner be shattered to pieces than pass through the seed. And if there be a tumour in the belly, it will reduce it by boiling it with wine and figs and giving it to the patient in bed. And it is good to eat it mixed with the juice of red fennel and clear honey with it, and it will truly drive the eyes to health and brightness, and strengthen the five senses wonderfully.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF THE HERB CALLED IN LATIN PETROSILIWM (PARSLEY).

§ 789. Parsley is a good herb, warm in its nature, and hot, and moist in the third degree; it is good in all food to increase the blood, and it opens the blood vessels and the vessels of the lymph, and the veins throughout the body of man, so that the blood and the lymph and the water may pass freely along the ways they should, and this it truly does.

Also parsley is good to use against faintness of the heart, and against the tertian fever, and the stitch, and moisture, among other fluid disorders of that time. And it greatly gladdens the heart, and heals the stomach.

There is a kind of parsley called in Welsh perllys yr hêl (marsh parsley), because it grows of a kind and nature on marshes near the sea where the salt water comes at high tide, and in Latin it is called petorsil marina; it is good in every case of retention of water and lymph in the body, and against constipation and tightness, from gym-

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 261

its juice is good, and its juice is good for destroying dead flesh in a deep and complete wound, and this grows in gardens, where it should be kept in every place far from the sea.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF FENNEL, CALLED IN LATIN FUNICULWM.

§ 790. Fennel is of a warm and dry nature in the second degree, and it is good against diseases of the eyes, and good against all kinds of poison in a person's body when drunk as a powder in white wine, or in old strong mead; and it is good against the softness of the tertian fever, and persistent softness. And if the seeds or the herbs are boiled in water until it is strong and full of the nature of the plant, and a sore head washed with that water, it will do great good and heal it, where the pain is caused by cold and softness, and it will break the headache very quickly indeed.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF ROSEMARY, ALSO CALLED YSBWYNWYDD, AND IN LATIN ROSA MARINA.

§ 791. Rosemary is a tree and herb warm in its nature and dry in the third degree, and it is called a shrub because it is of a kind between an herb and a tree.
Take rosemary flowers and mix with honey and eat it fasting every day, and neither plague nor antidote nor anything else poisonous shall rise against you while you practise this medicine.
Also the flowers are more especially good boiled with honey, or white wine down to about half, and strained clean, and drunk cold in the morning a spoonful or two, and a little honey with it, and a few grains after it will drive away the colic within three hours, and if you wish to apply it to your belly on the outside, put none of the honey into it.
Also, take leaves of rosemary and leaves of chwerwyn, and make into a poultice in the same manner, and honey in it likewise, and apply it after. And it is a very good medicine against the sickness

262 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

stone, and the soreness of phlegm, and it expels and drives it away in the water.

Also, place its flowers or its leaves under your head in your bed, and you will not be troubled by troublesome dreams, nor by a tempting evil spirit.

Also, if you carry with you a staff or piece of that herb, no evil spirit will come near you, nor will anyone work temptation upon you.

And rosemary has all the virtues of the stone called the muchudd.

Also, make a spoon from the stem or root of this plant, and on the day you eat broth with that spoon you will not be poisoned that day, and you will be protected throughout that day from thunder or lightning, and you will be protected from every harmful deed.

Also, gather the leaves of rosemary and pound them fine and strain it, and drink the juice, and it will break up the phlegm from the head and the lungs, and destroy it, truly and truly.

Also, it is good against the heat of the liver, and drives it out, and draws away the inflammation therefrom, and makes it healthy.

Also, if a person has difficulty making water, let him seek the flowers or the leaves and boil them with white wine, and drink that liquor first thing in the morning, and last thing at night.

Also, by taking the flowers and placing them with white wine in a still and distilling them, the liquor obtained from them is as good as the blessed distillation, and good in its place for everything, and it is very good for washing the head against cold headache and for bathing it therein, and against a person going mad, a spoonful of that liquor with a spoonful of honey and a spoonful of melted butter, or thick fresh cream, is good against the cough and for drawing phlegm from the lungs.

Also, the water in which they are boiled is good for the person

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 263

who is out of his wits or going out of his mind, this herb is also good against every kind of disease that exists in the body of man.

Also, it is good to boil the flowers and leaves in water, and to wash with that water every morning without drying with a linen cloth, but letting it dry of its own nature, and by washing thus it will make an old person appear young in looks forever; this water clears the mucus from the brain of man, and removes the pain from the cartilage and sinews, and drives away rheumatism, and heals the liver, and brings warmth to the veins and sinews, and destroys the pestilence, and gladdens the heart, and makes the bones strong and nourishes the marrow within them, and heals the marrow within them, and it heals the eyes, and it is good against running eyes — boil them in sour wine and apply to the patient's stomach, it will cause the blood to be nourished; and it is good against the three-day fever, and if a man has been weakened by women he will recover again by using this alone as drink and liquid for nine days.

Also, if a person has no children, whether man or woman, let them use this herb in their food and it will open them perfectly. If a man or woman have no children and the wife is young, let them use rosemary.

Also, if a man has a cold in his head like a heavy cold, let him take the rosemary and burn it, and let that smoke into his nostrils, and he will be completely healed.

Also, take the water in which the flowers or leaves have been boiled, and put into it a little purified honey and pepper, and drink it warm, and it is good against coughing, of whatever kind it may be, and this is true. Also, take the roots of the herb and roast them well in embers and grind them small and add [illegible passage in cipher/damaged script] truly.

HERE AGAIN ARE SHOWN THE VIRTUES OF THE PLANT CALLED IN LATIN SALVIA [SAGE].

§ 792. Sage is a herb warm and dry in its nature. It is good to boil it in all food and drink for the benefit of the sinews, and it is good to drink its essence through boiling water as a sole drink, and best for the benefit of the stomach to drink it with good honey. Also if a woman has a dead child within her womb, let her take sage with white wine and boil them well together and drink it cold, and she will be delivered safely of the dead child. If it is chewed fine and applied to a venomous bite, it will draw out the venom and heal the wound.

Also, if a wound is full of blood, crush the leaves fine and apply them to the wound, and it will cleanse the sore cleanly.

Also, if a man has a pain under his ribs, take sage and wine, and warm the wine on the fire as hot as can be drunk, and take it as a drink, and he will be healed.

Also, the essence through water, and a decoction through wine or mead, or ale, is a good drink above all to heal dampness of the joints, and the cough, and pain in the head, truly.

HERE AGAIN CONCERNING THE VIRTUES OF THE MANDRAKE.

§ 793. The mandrake is a herb burning, warm and dry. To boil it together with white wine and strain it clean through a linen cloth and let it cool, it is good to drink morning and night to help a person with jaundice.

Take the seed of the mandrake and make it into a powder, and boil it well in spring water or in goat's milk, or in wine

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 265

good white mead, or in strong old mead, and this remedy is good against chronic cough, and against colic, and to enlarge the blood vessels and other swellings, if salt is added to it at the same time.

Also, take henbane seed and crush it together with pepper, and temper them with wine or honey, and give to drink; and however wild the body of a man or woman who takes it may be, it will become as tame as the tamest of all.

THE VIRTUES OF THE BLESSED THISTLE.

§ 794. The blessed thistle has the property of opening the body and causing it to go to stool, and this herb when eaten gives relief from pain in the head and the temples, and causes good hearing, and it improves the brain and the eyesight, not only by eating it, but by anointing the eyes with its juice; and when the juice cannot be obtained, use the herb in a poultice and mix it with water, and let the juice drip into the eye, and this is good against blood that has settled in them. This herb is also good for improving the senses and the memory, and good also against lightheadedness in the head; it is also good against bleeding from the nose and mouth, and the powder of this herb mixed with honey causes phlegm to be expelled by spitting, and it benefits a weak stomach, and causes appetite for food, and soothes the heart, and it expels bad blood and generates good blood. If the herb is boiled in water and drunk, it will purge the bad from it and keep it well, and by eating the herb it will strengthen the limbs weakened by the disease of the sinews called palsy, and it strengthens the spinal cord and the brain, and delivers them from the cold humour which causes failure and weakness of mind and bodily strength and senses. And it heals painful bowels, and the herb boiled, or drunk with wine, breaks the stone, and whoever smears it on the trunk of a small healthy person shall receive healing.

of the gland and the moisture, and it will cause horn-warts to break, and it overcomes cancer and the fainting sickness — but take the powder of the herb within twelve hours and it will dispel the faintings, and the flowers of the herb, if placed in a wound, will heal it without pain, and it is good to chew the herb in the mouth to strengthen the breath; and it heals the ague by boiling it in wine and drinking it warm about a quarter of an hour before the fit comes on, and put sufficient clothing on the person to cause sweating. And that will protect against the cold ague, the hot ague, and the ague of the joints. In the same way, the powder of this herb with warm wine, or a distilled infusion of the herb, will relieve a suffering person in a short time from all poison received into the veins as well. If the herb is drunk through a strainer, or its juice, or its distillation, and afterwards sweating occurs for the space of three hours, it will heal the patient. And the powder of the herb, whether eaten or drunk, will ease the pains in the sides and the chest; these are the virtues of the blessed thistle.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF THE CLEAVERS, NAMELY THE CLEAVERS OF THE HEDGES.

§ 795. Taking their juice as the only drink in spring and summer will utterly destroy the corruption in the blood and the lymph, which is the cause of all eruptions, scabs, horn-warts, hard swellings, the great shingles, cancer, goitre, lung disease, joint disease, rheumatism, the great gout, soreness, all fever and inflammation, all eruptions on flesh and skin, all running sores on the eyes, all mucous discharge of the head and stomach, all white swelling of any joint or other part, all heat and burning in the blood and lymph, all hot shooting pains in the head, all tightness in the chest and stomach, and under the diaphragm, all swellings in the legs and feet, and all other parts of the body; for there is scarcely one of the ailments that afflict the body of man that does not have its cause in corruption of the blood and lymph.

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 267

The way to obtain their juice is as follows: take the herbs, both leaves and flowers and seeds, at the time when they are in season, all together, and pound them well and place them in an unglazed earthen vessel, and fill the vessel without pressing the herbs, then pour over them just enough clean running water to cover them, and let it stand overnight. Some say it would be better to add one quarter of the water as sea water, or water salted to the same strength as sea water, for the first week of drinking, and then to leave off the salt and keep to the fresh, and drink only this drink for nine weeks, and it would be remarkable if you were not healthy within that time, all things considered.

Gather the herbs in the spring and summer, and dry them well in the morning sun, turning and handling them so that the sun can penetrate them and dry them thoroughly, and keep turning and handling them lightly during the day, and take them indoors at night, and if they are not fully dry, put them out a second day in the sun and do as the day before, and if there is need for further days, where there may be occasion due to rain and dew, take care not to leave them out in dew and mist, for these will draw out all the virtue of the herbs. Take the herbs in their leaves and in their flowers and in their seeds, and dry each one separately in closed oak chests or in straw baskets of wheat straw. And when there is occasion, take the herbs through the leaves and make a brew of them and drink it for three weeks, then make a brew through the flowers and drink it for three weeks, and then make a brew through the seeds and drink it for three weeks, and in this way you will proceed in accordance with the order of God and the provision of nature, and the natural cycle of the year.

The way to make a brew of the herbs is this: crush the fresh herbs very finely with your hands, and place them in an unglazed earthen vessel full, and boil running water and pour it carefully over the herbs just enough to cover them, and before pouring, place a milk strainer — that is, a base without a rim — over the mouth of the vessel to keep the herbs from floating over the edge of the vessel when the water is poured in.

268 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

hot upon them, then close tightly on the vessel for six hours, then drink only the liquid, and at night press the herbs firmly and receive the juice through a strainer into a clean vessel, and drink that upon going to bed, lukewarm; and if there be upon your body any kind of eruption, or swelling, or tumor, or ringworm, or scab, or itching, or burning, or wound, or sore, or bruise, wash with the liquid of the herbs, whether their juice or their decoction it be, and where the pain is great, apply the herbs through their juice as a plaster upon it; and this preparation for drinking and plastering has healed the white plague, and the great ringworm called in Latin lepra, and the cancer that has eaten the flesh to the very bones.

Take the seeds of the chickweed at their full ripeness, and dry in an oven after taking out the bread, twice or three times, until sufficiently dry; then powder them in a stone mortar, and keep the powder in a glass vessel well sealed, and carry it with you on every journey away from home, and take a full spoonful of it in clean water three times a day, and it will keep you healthy against all pain, and will serve in place of food for you in need. It is good to treat the seeds of the mallow in the same manner, and to use them in the same way.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF THE MISTLETOE, CALLED BY ANOTHER NAME THE UCHELFAR.

§ 796. The uchelfar grows most commonly on apple trees and on hawthorns, and is also found by chance on the oak, and that which is found there is better than the rest, yet each one of them is good and very good. The virtue of the mistletoe is to strengthen the body beyond and above what any other herb can do. Gather the plant in the days of Christmas, when the berries, that is its pods or fruit, are at their full ripeness, and gather the berries from the branch and pour boiling water upon them and close the vessel containing them, and place near the fire where they will not boil too rapidly

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 269

for a day and a night, then strain through a fine hair-cloth strainer into a clean vessel; and take the leaves and the tops, that is the whole of the plant, and bruise them very fine, and place on a warm bread-stone, and toast them well, turning and handling to prevent burning, and when they are as dry as you can make them into powder do so, taking for that purpose half of what is on the stone of the herbs, and leaving the other half to burn down to fine ash; put the powder and the ash each separately into sealed glass vessels.

If there be weakness in the body, whether in the sinews, or in the joints, or in the back, or in the head and brain, or in the bowels, or the heart, or the lungs, or the kidneys, take three spoonfuls of the strained liquid and put in boiling water, or ale, or mead, or milk, and let it steep in the warm liquid, then add to the full drink thereof a spoonful of the powder and drink it every morning fasting, and half a drink of the same thing at night on going to bed; and it is good against all ailments of the brain, and the sinews, and the back, and against the falling sickness, and madness, and weakness of the head of every kind, and the palsy, and all weakness of the joints, and it will strengthen the eyes and the hearing and all the senses, and cause fruitfulness of body and the getting of children; and it is good for man and woman against barrenness or loss of nature, and a person who drinks a spoonful of the powder once every day in their drink when thirsty shall obtain health of body, and bodily strength, and manly vigour; and the same also by taking a spoonful of the strained liquid in their broth or other warm drink once in the day.

If one is sick with fever, or with wind colic, or with the jaundice, take a spoonful of the ash in drink three times a day, and where possible let the drink be a decoction of this herb, whether fresh or dry it matters not, and it shall deliver you, and healing shall it bring.

Where the herbs grow nearby, it is only necessary to gather the new young shoots fresh each day, collecting them from day to day as needed, and boil the herbs fresh each time; but where they grow far away

270 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

one may make as was said, and keep the herbs dry in the house throughout the year, gathering them in summer, winter, and spring as they may be obtained in every condition.

The best place to find these herbs is Gwent, and the land of Summer (Somerset), and Brecknockshire, and Montgomeryshire, and the best time to gather them is the depth of winter from the feast of Andrew to the feast of Candlemas (Mary of the Candles), and it is good to gather the green herb from the feast of James to the beginning of winter, so that their juice may be obtained before they lose their virtue.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF THE OAK.

§ 797. The oak provides various medicines against every pain that arises from weaknesses of the sinews, the spinal marrow, and the brain, and there are many ways in which medicine is obtained from the oak.

Take freshly cut oak chips and place them in running water until they bleed their sap, then take them out and put in fresh chips, and do so as before, do this thus until nine days have passed, then boil the liquor until it is reduced by half, then add honey, a pound's weight to every two gallons, and make it into a bragget, and if there be added to it some of the husks of the husk-herb, as much as there is of honey, if available, or whatever there is, and where this liquor is not then very good, it is called oak bragget, and it is the best of all drinks for strengthening the body and nature, the sinews, the brain, and the spinal marrow, and it will heal those who are sick from weaknesses, and drink a full draught of it in the morning on an empty stomach.

The bark of the oak, the part nearest to the wood, is good against all weaknesses; take it and parch and powder it, also dry it very thoroughly and keep it in that manner, so that you may have it and the powder at hand in time of need, and they are good in drink or as a poultice against all weaknesses, and against every infection whether it be continuous or intermittent; and the third and fourth day fever, and it is good against every eruption in the blood and the humors; and

the bark's inner layer, which is very good against all the same pains, boiled in ale and in cow's or goat's milk.

Take acorns of the oak at their ripeness, and dry them thoroughly, and powder them, and keep them in an oak vessel tightly closed, and cast a spoonful into your drink morning and night; and where there is weakness and loss or wasting of nature in a man or woman, take three spoonfuls of this powder, and boil in a full drink of goat's or cow's milk, and add honey to it, and drink at night and in the morning, and it will cure the disease, and it is good against all the weaknesses already mentioned concerning them, and good against a woman's bleeding, and against the flux that affects every person, and against a painful spleen, and it is good as a food with wheat bread for every person weak in body, and against consumption of the lungs, and every wasting of body and nature when taken as a prepared food.

Take acorns and make malt of them, and make ale from that malt, and it is the best and most wholesome of all ales, and good against all weaknesses and their resulting pains.

Gather oak leaves in the month of August or the month of September, and dry them well and keep them sealed, and apply to every skin wound, and to watery sores, and you will be healed.

Take dry acorns, or the bark nearest to the dry wood, and grind with bread grain, and make bread from it, and that is the best of all breads for strengthening a man's body, and it is the best to protect against all winter pain and cold and wetness.

HERE ARE THE VIRTUES OF THE BLESSED OAK.

§ 798. If you are sick with kidney stones, take the bark or inner layer of the blessed oak, and gather it, roots and all, in the time of its seed, and dry it well, and powder it, and keep the powder carefully under a tightly sealed cover, and cast it into your drink as a prepared remedy without fail. Also boil the herb through its roots and seeds in ale, or mead, or goat's or cow's milk, and drink it as a prepared drink; also mix the powder with your flour

272 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

bread, and take it as food prepared with goat's milk, and if there be no goat's milk, use cow's milk; and if running sores cast their matter upon them, take the herb by root and all, and pound it well and boil it with fresh butter and a little wax, and strain it well and apply it, and take the juice of the herb through root and leaves, and anoint the dry chest with it every day as long as the herbs are to be obtained, and in the winter mix the powder with honey and anoint in the same manner, and all this is good against all pains that come from the poison of calculi, upon the lungs, the liver, the kidneys, the brain, and the eyes, and in every other place; gather it and every other herb in the name of God, and give no credence to those who say it should be gathered in the name of the devil, for there is nothing that the devil does that is good.

HERE IS SHOWN THE FOUR ELEMENTS OF MAN, AND FROM THEM THE FOUR COMPLEXIONS OR FOUR DISPOSITIONS OF MAN, FIRST THE SANGUINE, SECOND THE CHOLERIC, THIRD THE MELANCHOLIC, FOURTH THE PHLEGMATIC.

§ 799. To recognize people of the sanguine complexion, or blood-full. One who is sanguine, or of the blood-full complexion, will be naturally stout, and is not stout alone, for that is a sign of a cold nature, but as Avicenna says, abundance of flesh signifies a warm nature. And abundance of flesh is nourished by the abundance of blood, as Avicenna says. Every ruddy man without fatness is of the sanguine, as Galen says. Sanguine people will be merry and will listen to tales and entertainment, and for that reason also they will be lustful and prone to the desires of the flesh, and they will drink wine merrily as well. A sanguine man desires the best food, for sanguine people desire the food most suited to their nature; also, a sanguine man laughs readily, for the blood desires joy; also, he will be fair in the nature of his complexion, and he will speak quickly, and he will be apt to learn all knowledge, and deep arts and disciplines, and he will be inspired and he will

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 273

imaginings and pursuits, and he is not easily angered, and he will be generous of heart and without envy, and he will be loving, and affectionate in his conduct and his deeds, and he will be ruddy in complexion, as Avicenna says that a red complexion on the skin of a man signifies an abundance of blood, and this is known by a clear and bright red colour, and not a dark red, such as those who are red in the face from the habit of excessive drinking, and those who make use of herbs, for such a colour as that signifies leprosy, and scabbiness, and complete phlegm, and blood; also, he will sing sweetly and lovingly with his voice, and will listen to singing, and he will frequently associate with singers, and the joyful, and the merry, and he will love strings and all musical instruments, and will be swift and diligent in his work and his undertakings, also he will be brave and confident by reason of the heat of the blood, and will be noble by nature through sanguinity, and where he finds no teacher he will think too highly of himself, and will be cross and loud-mouthed and foolish on account of the excess of sanguinity, and in immediate action and thought, and not often in distant matters; and also he learns from inspiration and not from deliberation, and it is his nature to be very vain and hasty in what he says and does, and he will often fall into the fault of laughing and contradicting in matters he does not know, through the quickness and wildness of the over-sanguine temperament.

TO KNOW THE TEMPERAMENT OF THE SPLEEN.

§ 800. One whose temperament is of the spleen will be swarthy because his nature is but weak; in the second place the people of the spleen will be short and stout, because their nature is not strong enough for them to grow in height; also they will be less fruitful than people of the other temperaments because of their coldness, and this causes them to sleep more than others sleep, and they will be sensible people,

274 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

they will also be lazy, and this is because of cold, for just as warmth makes a man light and lively, so cold makes a man heavy and lazy; also people of the phlegmatic type will be fat because of the impurity of the body; they will also be heavy in mind and drowsy, or great sleepers, and if they find a teacher they will be intelligent and will know what is fitting to know about it, but because of their cold and the weakness of their heaviness they will fail in every endeavour very easily, and they will not remember well, and they will care for nothing but their own benefit and gain; and they will desire no joy, nor singing, nor merriment, and though cleverness may be found in them, inspiration will not be found, except where there is a mixture of the sanguine in the constitution, and where that is frequent one sees a wise man and one firm in his inspiration, and patient, and long-suffering, and a prudent man, who does not like to quarrel, nor to beg, nor to jest, because he cares for nothing but what is fitting and steadfast.

TO KNOW THE CONSTITUTION OF STEAM AND THE PEOPLE WHO WILL BE OF THAT TEMPERAMENT.

§ 801. One whose temperament is of steam or heat will be irrational because of an excess of warmth, which turns him to wildness; and one who is of this constitution will be very desirous of gaining eminence and dignity and of being chief and master over others, because of the natural warmth which turns a man's mind to folly. Also people who are ardent will learn easily because of the warmth of the heat, and they do not greatly reflect on what they learn; also they will be of high heart, which means they cannot endure any wrong because of their warmth, and they desire great eminence, and offices, and advancement, and a choleric man will be as lecherous as a goat, and the desire of every charm found upon him stronger than love, and he will be a deceiver, and he will grow angry easily over small matters, and this signifies the warmth of steam, and blood

PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI. 275

seething around the heart, and he will be cunning and rash and unwise in his schemes and imaginings, and more given to plundering than to guile in what he does and thinks, and he will be thin in his limbs, and sour, and of the same color as saffron; as Avicenna says, that color signifies pride, and the body and limbs will be lean, and he will see fault in another where none exists, yet he who has this condition will not see fault in himself; also he will be affectionate toward whoever honors him, and proudly churlish toward whoever does not, and vengeful toward those who wrong him by force or falsehood, and the yellow bile cannot be mixed into him, and if one could go into the constitution of the blood that would result from this, they would be faithless and fickle, all those of this temperament; and of the four constitutions in man, this is the hardest to heal and to bring to moderation; and this temperament Rhys the Physician called the steam, because of the steam of the boiling around the heart and the bitterness of the gall in man.

HERE IS SHOWN THE NATURE AND CONSTITUTION OF THE SPLEEN, AND THE TEMPERAMENT OF PEOPLE WHO WILL BE SPLENETIC.

§ 802. One whose constitution is of the spleen will be sour and ill-mannered, like one who fights with himself; also, the greater part of people who are splenetic will be sad, and little given to conversation because of their coldness; also they will be studious, and pensive, and contemplative, and desirous of being alone and to themselves, and they cannot sleep well because of the dryness of the brain which causes them to dream and to wake from their sleep, and they will be diligent of mind and of good memory, and difficult to serve, and envious and covetous, and they will act badly because of a weakness that prevents them from doing well as they desire, and for that reason they will be bad and deceitful in their dealings. A splenetic man will be a great reader, and one who fasts, and fearful, and the people of this temperament will have the color of earth.

276 PHYSICIANS OF MYDDVAI.

This colour, if it be green, signifies dignity, as Cassys the wise man says, and all of the kind spoken of will be excessive in all things; if sad and heavy in such a way, if merry, then overly merry and without measure in the world; they love to sing in solitude, and love to listen alone to music and strings, and love to display their thoughts about others, yet do not love to show their own condition; they will be inspired and skilful, and do not greatly love to show it, and they will improve in knowledge and arts, and will learn thoroughly and will be careful in what they do and say. And if the mixture from the sanguine is in them, they are wiser than others in observation; and if the mixture be from the choleric, they will be bitter and sour, more disagreeable than any others; and if from the phlegmatic mixture, they will lose themselves and fight with themselves. They will be pale of body and limb, and many a poet is found among this temperament, and often are seen in them excessive love and excessive hatred.

Here are the parallels and masterpieces of medicines received by the grace of God, and the knowledge of the wise and godly men of old times, none other than the remedies shown here.

TO CAUSE A MAN TO CONFESS WHAT HE HAS DONE.

§ 803. Take a frog alive from the water, and pull out its tongue, and put it back in the water, and place that tongue upon the heart of a sleeping man, and he will confess what he has done in his sleep.

AGAINST TOOTHACHE; IT IS A CHARM.

§ 804. Saint Mary sat upon a rock, upon a stone near her hermitage, and the Holy Spirit came to her when she was sorrowful. Why are you sorrowful, mother and lady, and what pain afflicts you? My teeth are in pain, and a creature called migram came here and afflicted them, and I bit it and swallowed it.

A CHARM AGAINST THE FAM (HYSTERIA), WHICH RHIWALLON THE PHYSICIAN GAVE TO GWYRFYL DAUGHTER OF RHYS AB GRUFFUDD AB RHYS AB TEWDWR.

AGAINST TOOTHACHE.

§ 806. TO CAUSE SLEEP.

§ 807. Take a goat's horn and write upon it the names of the seven sleepers, and set it as the handle of a knife, beginning the inscription from the blade, and these are their names: Anaxeimeys, Malchws, Marsianws, Denys, Thon, Serapion, Constantynn; and after writing the names, place the knife beneath the head of the patient without his knowledge, and he will sleep.

For the falling sickness, THAT IS THE STRONG DISEASE, WHEN A PERSON FALLS AND COLLAPSES.

§ 808. Turn your mind sincerely to God and say these words three times into his ear: Anamzapta, and when the man recovers from the fit, give him dog's bile, and hang it in the house where the patient lives, and place it where it may get wind for three days, then *boil in a quart of ale this amount to a pint, and give it to the patient to drink before the affliction comes again.

Here is a charm that the Lord Jesus Christ Himself made, and showed to the three brothers, asking them where they were going; they answered that they were going to the Mount of Olives to gather herbs to heal wounds and bruises, then He said: return again and take the oil of the olive tree, and the white of an egg, and black wool, and apply them, saying thus: I adjure thee, wound, by the grace and power of the eight wounds which were in the true God and the true Man, and which were received in the most holy body in redeeming us, and for the sake of Him whom thou didst desire thyself, and for the suffering thou didst endure, and for the ransom thou didst pay thyself, Jesus Christ, that this wound of mine may not fester, nor rot, nor become corrupt, in the name of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; so be it true. AGAINST THE SHIVERING AGUE (FEVER WITH TREMBLING).

§ 809. Place this writing on the hollow of the patient's chest, hung around his neck.

When our Lord Jesus Christ saw the cross that was prepared for him, he trembled greatly, and the Jews asked him then, are you afraid at seeing this cross, or is it the shivering ague that afflicts you, and Jesus answered them thus: I am not afraid of this cross, nor does the shivering ague pain me, but I tremble before my heavenly Father at seeing his preparation for those who would crucify me, and I tell you truly that any man who hears these words that I now speak, and believes them, and does all that I have ordained therein, bowing before his heavenly Father, shall never be afflicted by the shivering ague, nor shall anything cause him fear. And now, O Lord Jesus Christ, may it be of your mercy that the shivering ague afflict not and weary not this your servant and servant of God the Father of heaven, neither now present nor at any other time throughout his life and his days in this world, in the name of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and may it be so. Amen forever.

TO KNOW, WHEN A MAN IS SICK, WHETHER HE SHALL LIVE OR DIE.

§ 810. Take an egg laid on a Thursday in the house where the patient is, and write these letters upon it:
ℐ. Ꞡ. ℗. Ꞡ. ꙅ. ℤ. ℗. ꙅ. ℨ. and place it in a safe spot in the field away from the house, and the next morning break the egg, and if blood comes the patient will die, and if no blood comes he will live.

AGAINST DROPSY, THAT IS THE IDROPS.

§ 811. Take small limpets and saffron, and within a short time the old limpets and the stone within them will come, and with that the patient will be relieved of the Dropsy.

ON LETTING BLOOD TO PROTECT A MAN'S SIGHT.

§ 812. Whoever has blood let from him on the twenty-second day of March in the right arm, and on the twentieth day of April in the left arm, shall never go blind, for this has been proven many times.

AGAINST WARTS.

§ 813. Wash the warts with water from the baptismal font where the seventh son of a married couple was baptized.

THE WAY TO SEE THAT WHICH ANOTHER CANNOT SEE.

§ 814. Take the bile of a cat and the fat of a hen, mix them together and put them on your eyes, and you will be able to see that which another cannot see.

THE WAY A MAN MAY HOLD FIRE IN HIS HAND.

§ 815. Take the blessed slug and the whites of two eggs, anoint your hands with them mixed together, and put powdered aloe on your hands, and thus you will be able to feel fire without pain, and hold fire and hot iron in your hand without fear.
